nodes.hypothesis: Retain the policy and matching Adam optimizer checkpoint with the lowest unchanged combined current-and-historical augmented-target mean squared error among the starting state and every iterate visited by the inherited bounded online update, choosing the earliest exact tie instead of automatically retaining the last iterate.
nodes.finding:
The intended checkpoint intervention happened. Of 435 updates followed by new proposals, 142 retained an earlier policy and matching Adam state: five initialization updates and 137 later feedback updates. Every intervention produced a measurable parameter difference from its discarded endpoint. On those same update paths, terminal-minus-selected mean squared error averaged 0.202718, summing to 28.785889. All 450 updates, including 15 terminal updates, retained the minimum logged loss on the fixed training tensor. Seven early sitagliptin updates retained their starting state. Targets, training membership, equal row weights and the executed Adam rule remained unchanged.

Final benchmark performance declined despite that lower fitting loss. The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.513272 to 0.487621, a paired mean change of -0.025651; the individual seed changes were -0.036109, -0.010057 and -0.030788. Population standard deviation increased from 0.001984 to 0.012470. Four of five task means fell, led by sitagliptin from 0.288538 to 0.197063; drd2 was essentially unchanged. Both algorithms delivered all 4,350 novel accepted optimizer proposals. Canonical-novel yield among raw draws rose from 51.81% to 52.79%, and distinct chemical-core coverage increased on four tasks. Those coverage improvements did not provide the predicted score gain.

Useful earlier prefixes are much more common than endpoint-versus-start checks alone reveal: 132 of the 142 nonterminal interventions occurred even though the discarded endpoint was already better than the starting checkpoint. Selecting the best visited fitting loss is therefore an active intervention, but it is insufficient to improve this molecular search. The seven zero-progress updates all occurred at the beginning of the task with the largest score loss. Suppressing those early parameter changes, or more generally discarding useful momentum and learning progress, is a plausible contributor; the experiment does not isolate either explanation. The discarded endpoint is a same-path training comparator, not an evaluated alternative molecular trajectory.

The preserved objective still has positive, unattainable log-probability targets in 1,217 of 4,425 training-row exposures, and historical-group error worsened in 148 of 420 nonterminal replay updates despite lower combined loss. Better combined fitting therefore does not imply that each historical example improves. Broader observed core coverage also rules out a uniform collapse of sampled core diversity as the sole account of the score decrease. The chemistry assessment finds abundant aromatic and cyclic medicinal-chemistry motifs, but recurring high-score families, unspecified stereochemistry and occasional uncontrolled molecular growth remain. This narrows the next question to the relationship between retained update progress, these fixed targets and useful future proposals, rather than assuming the last iterate or simple core scarcity was the main utility bottleneck. Checkpoint-loss equality is supported on identical tensor shapes; the inherited larger diagnostic tensor has small numerical discrepancies beyond the registered tolerance on 32 updates and should not be substituted for that criterion.

nodes.hypothesis: Enable a direct formula-preserving reversal of an acyclic secondary amide at an otherwise empty carbonyl-carbon replacement site, exchanging the nitrogen-side and carbonyl-side attachment relationships while retaining both external fragments.
nodes.finding:
Every one of the 120 selected eligible sites produced a checked, identity-changing reversal while preserving formula, size, the complete local amide and both attached fragments. Of 95 pooled descendants, 93 retained the reversed orientation; all eight descendants selected for evaluation retained it. Two later edits destroyed the amide, and a double reversal returned to an already seen molecule and was rejected as a duplicate. Of four evaluated sole reversals of accepted parents, one improved its source score by 0.011119 and three tied; none created a new incumbent. A reversal followed by deletion produced one incumbent gain, improving its real parent's score by 0.049026, but that gain cannot be assigned to the reversal alone. All 15 task/seed sessions completed their budgets with no invalid or duplicate oracle submissions. Mean final-best score fell from 0.544374 to 0.524013, a decline of 0.020361 instead of the registered minimum gain of 0.002. Population standard deviation across seed means fell from 0.013310 to 0.007408. Every seed's macro score declined; the 15 paired task outcomes comprised three wins, eight losses and four ties. The inherited identity checker also rejected two unstable candidates before pooling, while every admitted identity remained stable.

Failure to generate, preserve or evaluate a reversed amide is ruled out as the explanation for the missed score target. The direct comparisons show limited measured benefit: three source pairs tie, including the leading sampled amide pair, and the only incumbent gain combines two edits. The largest task-level loss occurred in docking, where 20 reversal-bearing candidates entered pools but none was selected. That loss cannot be read as an observed penalty on a scored reversed amide; opening an empty-menu action changes later random draws, pool composition and search history even when the new alternative is unselected. A contribution probe that distinguishes the local alternative's value from these trajectory changes remains informative. The change also does not establish globally better chemistry. Eligible-amide-containing emissions increased from 328 to 563, yet measured nonaromatic C(=O)-N coverage stayed nearly flat at 1,669 versus 1,667 molecules, and mean heavy-atom count increased from 33.39 to 35.43. The molecular assessment associates the weak docking seed with a less aliphatic-amine-rich branch and still finds reactive linkages, oversized repeated cores and unspecified stereochemistry. These are descriptive associations, not causal functional-group effects. The evidence supports a narrowly correct local transformation with sparse direct score exposure; broader utility and practical chemical quality remain open.

nodes.hypothesis: Retain accepted breeding molecules by successive score-ordered rounds across Murcko cores, prioritizing each core's best member before any core's next member, then restore global score order for the unchanged parent sampler.
nodes.finding:
All 4,365 retention calls matched the declared core-round rule, preserved the incumbent and respected the 64-member capacity. Among 3,540 capacity-limited contests, 1,606 changed the local greedy survivor set and added one represented core; 1,266 also changed the immediate breeding support. Mean cores actually used per breeding batch rose from 12.98 to 24.20, and all fifteen final populations contained 64 distinct cores. There were 12,012 actual parent uses outside greedy breeding support reconstructed from the same accepted history. Those uses contributed to 326 evaluated offspring, including 35 best-parent beats and two incumbent gains.

The direct protection route remained unused: none of the 602 records retained against local greedy eviction, including 542 evaluated offspring, subsequently entered the breeding bands. Overall strict best-parent beats fell from 565/4,350 (12.99%) to 526/4,350 (12.09%), and incumbent gains fell from 218 to 175. Mean final-best score fell from 0.544374 to 0.514684, a paired change of -0.029690. All three seed deltas were negative, as were all five task means. The retention mechanism and changed breeding support are confirmed; the intended score improvement was not observed.

Preserving a low-ranked core and exploring it are separate events under the unchanged sampler. Of the 542 protected offspring, 116 survived into a later breeding state, but all remained below the sampled score bands. Six were still retained when the experiment ended and had first received protection in the terminal batch. The broader breeding came through changes to stronger analogues and the ranks of other survivors, rather than descendants of the directly protected records. A local support-promotion trace confirms that this indirect route can produce a parent-beating child, but such participation did not offset the overall loss in productive evaluations.

The actual trajectory also changes the apparent opportunity: on the already diversified Child states, only two incoming molecules were rescued from immediate greedy rejection, while 1,058 newcomers that local greedy selection would accept were excluded. Both rescued newcomers stayed outside breeding support. This narrows the result to a strong redistribution of survivor competition, with little evidence for the hoped-for exploration of protected weak parents. Mean generating-parent strength and mean offspring score both fell, so the smaller average parent deficit is not evidence of better candidates. The molecular assessment still finds repeated oversized heterocycle assemblies, tiny fragments, reactive bonds and constrained ring systems. Core coverage increased without resolving those chemical limitations. The passive greedy lists use existing labels only; they provide no alternate descendants or scores for an independently executed search.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove sampled residual influence on successful pool allocation by selecting each available candidate with the highest original posterior mean, resolving exact ties by increasing pool index, while retaining the inherited full count posterior and correlated sampled arrays as passive controls.
nodes.finding:
Every one of 4,350 choices followed stable posterior-mean order, despite 3,977 strict disagreements with the sampled rule. All fifteen task runs completed. Final macro mean fell from 0.595670 to 0.518808, a paired loss of 0.076861 against the registered 0.002 scale. All three seed macros declined; twelve task–seed endpoints fell and three improved. On identical Child pools, mean-only selection reduced predicted uncertainty and nonempty typed cores from 6.46 to 4.33 per batch. Across real accepted streams, typed cores fell from 1,851 to 687 and mean accepted batch maximum from 0.488662 to 0.429045.

Sampled departures from the learned mean support the endpoint score in this exchange-free composition. More local successes did not compensate for losing them: parent-beating offspring rose from 629 to 698, more survivors bred again, and prediction MSE fell from 0.012718 to 0.004033 while every seed macro worsened. Those proxies therefore cannot replace the endpoint test. Lower uncertainty exposure and narrower selected families fit the loss, but their mediation is not isolated, and this removal does not identify the separate value of residual correlation. The chemistry also resists a simple quality verdict: tiny-fragment output almost disappeared and some conventional leaders improved, while elaborate aromatic families, reactive bond environments and unresolved ring geometry persisted. The result supports conditional residual-sampling benefit, with the three endpoint gains and contrary batch-level coverage changes preserved.

nodes.hypothesis: Ablate optional multi-call continuation in ordinary single-parent mutation proposals by using one GraphOperators.mutate call whenever the inherited saturation floor is one, while preserving the Parent's full sampled-length and escalation rule when that floor exceeds one.
nodes.finding:
Ordinary single-parent proposals now made exactly one mutation call in all 41,858 attempts. The retained length draw requested two or three calls in 7,387 attempts, suppressing 8,595 requested continuations. Of the resulting first products, 6,975 entered pools and 506 reached accepted evaluation; 88 beat their generating parent and 31 improved the incumbent. Crossover, its finishing mutations, nitrogen exchanges and correlated posterior selection all remained active. No saturation recovery branch was exercised.

All fifteen tasks completed. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.574344 to 0.555164, a paired loss of 0.019180 that exceeds the allowed 0.002 loss. Seed changes were -0.024068, -0.039845 and +0.006373. Population score dispersion increased from 0.012317 to 0.027680, and mean recorded AUC fell from 0.482560 to 0.438018. All five task means declined, with the largest losses in docking (-0.049788) and sitagliptin (-0.023491). The mechanism executed correctly; its non-inferiority prediction was falsified.

Total mutation calls fell from 62,704 to 54,089 and raw inner attempts from 78,045 to 67,702, with the same 69,600 pool entries and 4,350 accepted proposals. Accepted single-parent descendants were slightly closer to their parents: mean count-fingerprint similarity rose from 0.8885 to 0.9010 and exact core retention from 46.41% to 49.11%. Chemistry did not improve uniformly: nitrogen-halogen-containing proposals rose from 745 to 1,208 and proposals with three- or four-membered rings from 268 to 1,558, while peroxide-containing proposals fell from 236 to 56.

Giving the selector access to more first-mutation products did not preserve the developed search loop's final quality. The affected first products have real successes, but those successes do not establish that their omitted continuations were wasteful. The parent also obtained 52 parent beats and eighteen incumbent improvements from accepted multi-call products. Across the whole Child run, parent beats and incumbent improvements actually became more frequent while final scores fell. Those local improvement counts depend on the changing parents and search history, so they cannot substitute for endpoint quality.

A mutation-call bound is a weak chemical constraint. Much of the small increase in parent similarity comes from removing the less similar multi-call cohort; the remaining one-call products are close to the parent's existing one-call products. Ring closure and nitrogen relocation can still change molecular presentation substantially, and crossover can produce much larger rearrangements. The molecular assessment finds that useful aryl/amine and carbonyl frameworks remain available, alongside more strained small rings, reactive heteroatom bonds and unspecified configurations. In docking, small-ring incidence rose from nine to 680 proposals even though the strongest observed open-chain amine did not require that strain.

This result supports retaining ordinary continuation in this particular composition and panel, without establishing an optimal mutation depth or identifying which omitted molecules would have helped. Seed two improved all five endpoints, so the effect is not universal across trajectories. No recovery-walk opportunity was observed. Fewer calls also do not establish faster generation: the large total wall-time reduction is dominated by a long Parent oracle evaluation, and Child wall time is higher in the other two seeds.

nodes.hypothesis: Extend the existing change_bond menu with relocation of an intact single-attachment acyclic branch from an aromatic carbon to an adjacent hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon, exposing positional isomers to the inherited fresh-pool selector while preserving the branch, ring framework and molecular formula.
nodes.finding:
All 368 sampled branch reconnections preserved the registered atom and bond counts, molecular formula, branch composition and aromatic ring framework. Of the 365 moves that changed molecular identity, 362 reached pools and 20 were evaluated with the relocated attachment still present. The evaluated set contained 13 one-atom and seven multi-atom branches. Two moves beat their generating parents; both moved fluorine. Sixteen evaluated products survived their batch, and 14 were chosen as breeding parents 979 times across 972 later attempts. One fluorine shift increased its source score from 0.382775 to 0.394039, raised the incumbent, and was reused in 444 attempts with 85 later accepted descendants. Every evaluated multi-atom move scored below its best generating parent.

Mean final-best score across three seeds was 0.542797, versus 0.544374 for the Parent: a paired change of -0.001577, which misses the required +0.002 gain. Seed variation decreased from a population standard deviation of 0.013310 to 0.004718, but the paired seed changes were mixed. All 435 pools filled to 160 candidates and all 4,350 proposed evaluations were accepted. Stable identity bookkeeping was preserved; its inherited guard rejected seven unstable representations before pool admission.

The fresh-pool selector and accepted-survivor breeder can carry a useful positional edit into later ancestry, resolving the earlier graph-walk experiment's absence of retained relocation winners. The demonstrated benefit is narrow: two of 13 evaluated one-atom moves improved their parents, while none of seven evaluated multi-atom moves did. Keeping a larger branch intact therefore establishes access to positional alternatives without establishing better scores. A score-neutral methyl relocation also entered extensive later ancestry, so immediate parent improvement and later usefulness are different observations.

Two final-best molecules have recorded relocation ancestry, but subsequent edits and crossover prevent assigning their endpoint gains to a conserved moved group. Changing the option menu also changes the search path, so the paired panel measures the complete method; it supplies no scores for unselected alternatives. The molecular assessment still finds concentrated aromatic polycycles, reactive heteroatom bonds, strained ring arrangements and unspecified stereochemistry. Local formula and ring conservation did not resolve those chemical limitations, and the panel loss leaves the registered score-benefit expectation refuted even though construction, evaluated positional access and useful breeding ancestry are confirmed.

nodes.hypothesis: Jointly replace nonincumbent greedy survivor membership with the exact incumbent-preserving newest-serial rule from n-8fa256ded991 and replace rank-preferred live-parent choice with the exact all-eligible-live uniform law from n-a56491c332aa, on the single code Parent n-62daf219c70a, to connect directly protected survivors to their breeding consumer.
nodes.finding:
The access mechanism worked. Of 196 records retained against a local greedy eviction, 182 reached a later live population and all 182 were subsequently sampled, in 3,736 parent draws. The other 14 had no later opportunity. Those parents produced 155 accepted offspring, of which 151 later bred. Only two immediately advanced the incumbent. The stricter group still directly protected at the consumed retention contest produced 61 accepted offspring and no immediate incumbent gains. In median_2 seed 2, protected parents were drawn 140 times but produced no accepted offspring. All fifteen joint task runs completed.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.530508, a paired loss of 0.065161. All three seed macros and all five task means declined; three of fifteen task-seed endpoints improved. The joint mean was also 0.053355 below recency alone and 0.019163 below uniform-live sampling alone. The four-treatment interaction, joint minus recency minus uniform plus the Parent, was −0.007357, beyond the registered 0.002 descriptive scale. Its seed values were +0.025676, −0.057736 and +0.009990, with population deviation 0.036194, so the negative mean does not describe every seed.

Changing the consumer removed the storage-without-use obstruction observed with recency alone, but making protected alternatives breed did not recover endpoint performance. This is a resolved negative result for the exact joint intervention and its matched-panel interaction. It does not assign the loss to either component separately or settle the value of the wider graph-evolution foundation. The original losses from both single controls remain.

Participation and productive search separated sharply: the joint run produced 1,060 strict generating-parent wins versus 629 for the Parent, against weaker generating parents, while sequential incumbent advances fell from 258 to 201. Protected ancestry reached 525 accepted records and twelve incumbent advances, but only one final leader; overlapping ancestry is not proof that a retained structure mediated the endpoint. More perceived molecular cores likewise did not establish useful chemical diversity: the molecular assessment found 2,005 typed and 1,327 generic cores versus 1,850 and 1,117 for the Parent, alongside 299 tiny products versus 99 and continuing unusual ring bonds and unspecified stereochemistry. Recognizable cyclic amines and carbonyl frameworks remain counterexamples to treating every product as implausible. Neither core counts nor founder reachability measures retained atoms or synthetic feasibility.

The fixed combination has an exposed, complete answer without rescue tuning. Why particular trajectories lose, which chemistry would be useful, and how the broader foundation contributes remain open; this shared-Parent panel supplies neither independent replication nor reliability beyond the issued seeds.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace only the active fresh-pool sampled-score mean with the pinned original synthetic-pretrained TabPFN-v2 regressor mean conditioned at every refit on all current accepted standardized scores and their unchanged Morgan-count rows through one Objective-fixed, initialization-seeded 2048-to-128 Gaussian projection; retain the original full-count GP fit, covariance, Cholesky, raw-score scale and correlated residual draws, then use the inherited sequential masks and first-index maxima.
nodes.finding:
The pretrained model ran in all 15 sessions and changed 2,994 of 4,350 selection positions while preserving the original correlated GP residual law. Its predicted ranking benefit failed on the same accepted molecules: mean squared error rose from 0.00655 to 0.00742, within-batch ordering accuracy fell from 68.94% to 63.49%, and mean Spearman correlation fell from 0.484 to 0.353. Fourteen of 15 sessions lost ordering accuracy and correlation. Local parent wins increased from 648 to 703 and sequential incumbent advances from 255 to 268, but accepted scores and advance magnitudes were lower. The complete Child endpoint mean was 0.54477 versus Parent 0.59645, a descriptive difference of -0.05168; 14 of 15 endpoints and all three seed means were lower. The official comparison has no compatible seed pairs because the Child adds 23 packages to the Parent’s 43-package lock, so the registered profile-matched +0.002 efficacy criterion remains unevaluable. The Parent’s late deco_hop breakthrough remains in the primary panel; descriptive sensitivity also stays negative.

This recipe clears the earlier practical obstacle: a pinned synthetic-pretrained model can condition on every accepted row and change real molecular allocation offline within the issued resources. That successful integration does not establish useful ranking transfer. The passive original GP orders the exact Child-selected labels better, so the result rules out the intended intermediate ranking improvement on this observed stream without mixing different search histories. More novel cores and more sources with improving descendants coexist with lower absolute quality and smaller cumulative gain; novelty and local parent wins alone are weak progress proxies here. The chemistry makes that distinction concrete: accepted streams still include compact useful carbonyl and amine arrangements, but often grow elaborate rings and appendages while retaining reactive bonds and incomplete stereochemical identity. These associations do not identify the cause of the loss or imply a universal filter. Projection, pinned preprocessing and pretrained response priors remain one coordinated test; separate contribution and global or counterfactual ranking are unresolved.

nodes.hypothesis: Extend the existing graph replace_atom option menu with a direct formula-preserving exchange of a neutral aromatic nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon in the same six-member ring, retaining the ring connectivity and substituent attachment framework.
nodes.finding:
The exchange ran 397 times. Every construction preserved molecular formula, bond connectivity and the qualifying aromatic ring; 341 products were different positional isomers and 56 were symmetry-equivalent to their immediate source. Ordinary novelty checks admitted 315 distinct positional alternatives to temporary pools and reserved one for a protected handoff. The posterior selected 19 of those 315 alternatives, and the protected product was also evaluated, establishing 20 accepted positional isomers. One further evaluated molecule contained a symmetry-equivalent exchange after crossover and is excluded from that activation count. All 150 protected handoffs and every announced batch remained valid.

Fourteen evaluated positional isomers came from an accepted parent followed by exactly one exchange. Five beat that parent and nine lost, with a mean score change of -0.030970. All fourteen entered the immediate survivor population, twelve later served as generating parents, and one increased the running best score by 0.000290. The six positional isomers produced after crossover all scored below their best recorded generating parent; their immediate crossed sources were unscored. Across the entire graph channel, strict parent-beating descendants slipped from 452 to 449 of 2,850, and mean child-minus-best-parent score worsened from -0.089170 to -0.103903.

Despite that weak direct yield, the complete three-seed endpoint mean rose from 0.550198 to 0.587094. Paired gains were 0.052557, 0.021169 and 0.036962, giving a mean gain of 0.036896, above the registered 0.002 target. Deco hop, median and sitagliptin means increased; zaleplon and DRD2 means decreased slightly. All 4,350 generated submissions were accepted within the supplied 4,500-evaluation panel.

Larger temporary pools successfully expose this conserved-composition channel to real evaluation, but they do not establish that the posterior favors it: 19 of 315 positional alternatives were selected, or 6.03%, compared with the overall pool allocation of 6.25%. Most constructed alternatives therefore remain unscored. The clean cases show that moving a nitrogen can improve a particular accepted molecule, while their negative average and the nearly unchanged total parent-beating count rule out a general improvement in direct offspring yield in this panel. The registered parent-relative yield prediction is contradicted even though physical activation and the endpoint score target are established.

The endpoint gain cannot be assigned to those five local wins. Expanded menus change stochastic search paths and pool competition, and accepted descendants can subsequently breed and train the policy. The evidence does not separate those continuing effects from the immediate nitrogen relocation. The molecular assessment also places a limit on the chemical interpretation: useful ring and functional-group arrangements coexist with reactive peripheral groups, unusual ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry. Preserving formula and attachments can preserve those liabilities as well. The remaining question is which local positional contexts merit evaluation; neither a universally favorable nitrogen position nor improved synthetic plausibility is demonstrated.

nodes.hypothesis: Deterministically thin repeated atom/bond-typed Murcko cores within each suggestion: after k molecules of a core have been emitted, admit its next member only on the (k+1)-th distinct valid canonical-novel draw of that core since its preceding emission, resetting that per-core interval after admission; first occurrences and identity-keyed acyclic or extraction-fallback draws pass immediately.
nodes.finding:
The admission mechanism ran correctly and changed which constitutional cores reached evaluation. Across 435 batches, it rejected 436 eligible repeated-core draws in 167 batches. Comparing each recorded stream with its first ten valid novel structures, actual batches gained cores 159 times and never lost a previously represented core. Mean core count increased from 9.106 to 9.662, delivering 242 additional batch-level core representatives and changing 304 canonical output identities. Mean core concentration fell from 0.133 to 0.110. All state transitions, original-string provenance and paired behavior before the first intervention passed the passive audit.

All fifteen task sessions completed their budgets. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.522705 to 0.508247, a paired change of -0.014458 against the required +0.002 increase. Seed changes were +0.009826, -0.032176 and -0.021023; population dispersion across seed scores changed from 0.020072 to 0.019593. Task mean changes were -0.014692 for zaleplon, -0.014459 for deco-hop, -0.005454 for median-2 and -0.037685 for sitagliptin; docking decreased by only 0.000000211 near its ceiling. Recorded mean AUC nevertheless rose from 0.405593 to 0.430066, chiefly through earlier progress on docking and zaleplon.

Broader batches required more work. Raw draws increased from 35,568 to 36,880, and batches needing extra sampling increased from 16 to 28. Raw duplication rose from 32.21% to 34.50%, while validity fell from 91.79% to 91.11%. No generation limit was exhausted. Recorded generation time rose from 24.75 to 37.90 seconds across the panel, including 10.38 seconds for core extraction and 0.52 seconds for receipts; the interval gate itself took 0.009 seconds.

The experiment resolves the delivery question: additional cores already present in fresh policy samples can reach the oracle without losing the first-come batch's core support. That delivery was often unproductive. Of the 242 additional core representatives, only six improved the actual incumbent: four on zaleplon and two on docking. Deco-hop received 116 additional core representatives without an incumbent improvement from any of them. Its previously dominant phenyl/anilinoquinazoline core was evaluated 54 times instead of 160 and reached a lower best score. This is compatible with diluted exploitation, although unscored discarded molecules cannot identify the value of any particular forgone proposal.

Coverage is also a poor predictor of the magnitude of the final change. Sitagliptin gained only seven batch-level cores yet had the largest mean endpoint loss. Admission changes alter later feedback and therefore later generated streams; a same-stream comparison isolates immediate delivery, not the complete search that would have followed different admissions. The higher AUC and lower endpoint further separate earlier progress from the final objective.

The chemical assessment narrows what broader coverage did not repair. Productive functional-group attachment arrangements remain inconsistently preserved, and the many structures with potential stereochemistry still have no specified configurations. Those are open chemical capabilities, not established causes of this score loss. Useful next evidence would need to show that broader admission preserves productive local series or transfers their attachment chemistry, rather than using core count as a proxy for usefulness. The utility claim is rejected while the admission and delivery mechanism is confirmed.

nodes.hypothesis: Within the fixed selected historical replay group, weight each original accepted identity inversely to one plus the number of earlier task-local updates that executed at least one optimizer step with that identity selected, and renormalize those weights to preserve the Parent historical loss share; keep current-elite weights, selected membership and fixed augmented targets unchanged.
nodes.finding:
The intended weighting reached the real updates. All 405 nonterminal batches with unequal historical fitting counts reduced the weighted prior-use mean and changed gradient direction. Across the 420 historical batches, the same selected records had mean prior fitting count 4.610 with equal weights and 3.356 with the actual weights. Every first backward pass matched the weighted diagnostic exactly, and all 450 updates changed policy parameters. Current loss coefficients, total historical share, accepted targets, original strings and memory rules remained intact. Separately combining group gradients produced small numerical discrepancies in 31 updates; these do not replace the direct agreement between the weighted objective and the real backward pass.

Subsequent raw duplicate draws fell from 40.78% to 36.22%, novel yield rose from 51.81% to 55.90%, and batches needing further sampling fell from 41 to 29. All fifteen tasks completed their 300-call budgets. Mean final Top-1 rose from 0.513272 to 0.517655, a paired gain of 0.004383. The three seed changes were +0.001516, -0.007474 and +0.019107. Four task means increased, including an almost unchanged near-ceiling docking endpoint; sitagliptin decreased. Mean recorded AUC fell from 0.419605 to 0.406769, so the higher final endpoint did not come with faster useful discovery across the budget. Terminal updates are excluded from the generation conclusions.

Redistributing influence can change search without broadening replay membership. The child replayed 536 distinct session-local historical identities versus the Parent's 540, and its ordinary mean fitting count actually increased. Yet records with at least ten previous fitting uses received total loss coefficient 13.01 instead of 26.50 under equal weighting on the same child stream. This separates reducing repeated influence from selecting less-repeated records. The cost is a smaller effective historical batch: 4.18 rows on average despite five selected rows.

The effect does not establish better protection of every remembered molecule. Historical squared error fell from 85.86 to 84.09 on the child's fixed tensor, but 906 of 2,100 historical row exposures worsened, compared with 834 in the Parent. Both upward and downward likelihood moves occurred, and 489 historical exposures still had positive, unattainable log-probability targets. Every repeated training appearance was consecutive, leaving no skipped-fitting interval that demonstrates forgetting. The positive endpoint result is therefore compatible with weaker exploitation, slower progress in some objectives and a better late discovery in one seed.

Chemical coverage also moved unevenly: distinct docking cores increased from 431 to 537 while deco-hop cores decreased from 392 to 372. The molecular assessment shows familiar ring-rich medicinal chemistry, recurring analogue families and unresolved attachment arrangements. It also finds frequent questionable nitrogen chains in one seed, N-hydroxyaminal linkages and missing stereochemical specification. The counter reduced repeated loss influence; it did not resolve those chemical limitations. The open question is whether this endpoint benefit persists while preserving earlier useful progress and coherent chemistry, rather than whether the weighting can alter learning.

nodes.hypothesis: Admit a complete, valid, canonically novel direct-policy sample only when the parsed canonical identity has zero RDKit-assigned radical electrons; reject positive-radical candidates before emission and refill from fresh policy draws.
nodes.finding:
The electronic-state gate executed correctly. Across all three seeds and five tasks, it rejected six valid, novel, positive-radical draws while capacity was open and delivered six newly drawn closed-shell replacements. Those interventions occurred in six of 435 batches, spanning four task/seed sessions. Emitted positive-radical occurrence fell from the parent’s six in 4,350 proposals to zero in 4,350; the passive first-come comparator on the child’s actual stream also contained six. All 4,350 eligible zero-radical rows passed, including 315 charged molecules and 1,058 sulfur-containing molecules. Seventeen positive-radical raw-valid draws still occurred: six were rejected and eleven arrived after capacity was full. Thus admission changed; reduced raw radical generation has not been established. All 15 sessions completed their 300-evaluation budgets.

The promised score non-inferiority was rejected. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.522705 to 0.516739, a paired change of −0.005966, exceeding the allowed 0.002 loss. Seeds 0 and 1 were unchanged; seed 2 lost 0.017898 in macro score. In that seed, zaleplon_mpo fell from 0.500000 to 0.391286, outweighing deco_hop’s rise from 0.666949 to 0.686174; the other three endpoints were unchanged. Population seed SD was 0.011993 versus 0.020072, and recorded mean AUC fell from 0.405593 to 0.404156. None of the six immediate replacements improved an incumbent; two entered subsequent real training. Total suggestion time rose from 24.745 to 31.427 seconds, including 6.185 seconds of inspection and 0.792 seconds in receipt regions. These are recorded regions, not isolated estimates of causal overhead.

Rare admission changes can matter even when the excluded parent molecules were poor and never selected for training. All eleven sessions without an open-capacity gate intervention reproduced the complete parent molecular and score sequence. Every affected session preserved its matched proposal prefix until the first rejection. One affected deco_hop session changed only two batches’ admissions and ordering: its selected training records and audited training quantities remained exactly equal throughout. In two other sessions, replacements entered the unchanged elite-selection rule, giving a direct route into later feedback. The same immediate chemical exclusion can therefore leave learning unchanged or alter it, depending on what fills the slot.

The largest loss followed a replacement that never trained. In its first affected zaleplon_mpo update, the ten selected training records, rewards and targets were identical to the parent, but the inherited padding width shrank from 72 to 60 tokens because it is set using the larger batch, including unselected strings. Tiny recorded update differences appeared immediately; a further proposal difference appeared in batch five, followed by broad trajectory divergence. This exposes a route for an unselected molecule to affect numerical execution and makes numerical sensitivity a plausible contributor to the loss. The logs do not isolate a hardware arithmetic cause or show that the radical-bearing chemical feature itself was useful. The evidence rules out treating “never elite” as sufficient assurance that rejection will preserve the later search.

The molecular assessment helps explain what this narrow predicate leaves open. The main losing trajectory explored many more long hydrocarbon appendages and failed to recover its parent’s compact heteroaryl-ether amide endpoint, whereas the improving trajectory favored less overdecorated anilinoquinazolines. These are observed chemical associations, not proof of a causal feature. Ring-rich exploration remains broad, while undefined stereochemistry, reactive closed-shell handles and uncontrolled appendage growth persist. Zero RDKit radical electrons therefore establishes the intended representation constraint, not general medicinal quality or stability. Future attempts would need to resolve replacement usefulness and sensitivity to batch representation; the present result does not support a score-safe blanket exclusion or a reduction in raw generation of unusual states.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace the original dot-product count-Tanimoto covariance T_DP by the fixed squared law K(x,y)=T_DP(x,y)**2 on unchanged folded Morgan integer occurrence rows, coherently in every GP Gram block while preserving inherited zero/unit conventions and exact T_DP=1 aliases.
nodes.finding:
The squared covariance ran throughout all three seeds and five tasks, changed 1,442 accepted choices relative to original preferences on the same masks, and added 1,209 accepted records outside the passive original sets. On those actual accepted labels, pair accuracy rose from 0.73967 to 0.74039 and mean batch Spearman from 0.59327 to 0.59635, but MSE worsened from 0.0092124 to 0.0094384. Productive new typed/generic cores increased from 262/163 to 287/197, and later-used sources with useful accepted descendants from 146/91 to 176/121. This did not produce stronger overall progress: sequential incumbent gains fell from 255 to 242 and their summed magnitude from 5.81942 to 5.15234. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.596453 to 0.551982, a paired loss of 0.044472 against the required +0.002. All three seed macros fell; fourteen of fifteen task/seed endpoints fell. Macro dispersion narrowed from 0.033970 to 0.016362.

This exposed test separates genuine allocation and discovery-to-reuse delivery from useful final optimization. Weakening partial covariance while preserving zeros and count magnitude can produce more productive new cores and modestly better selected-stream ordering, yet still reduce absolute incumbent progress and endpoints. The exact fixed exponent-two route has exhausted its registered test; more novelty, narrower dispersion and ranking gains do not rescue it. Exact count aliases remain, so the route does not resolve representation collisions. The chemistry report finds recognizable amides and aryl cyclic amines alongside reactive nitrogen-halogen bonds, cyanate/acyl-fluoride or cumulated unsaturation, unresolved ring geometry and unspecified states; stronger Parent structures also have liabilities. Neither core novelty nor those differences identify chemical mediation. Passive alternatives have no labels or continued ancestry, and shared descendants do not prove independent scaffold contribution. Current composition review, whole-foundation and constituent coverage, full-current-condition and joint interactions, chemical mediation, full-history processing and partial lineage composition remain open. The distinct concurrent exponential output-path probes and historical kernel failures cannot be pooled into a covariance-floor, mean/residual or universal kernel conclusion.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace global greedy64 survival and score-quantile breeding with one persistent fixed 8-by-8 MolWt/MolLogP champion policy: keep the best actually accepted score per cell with earliest-serial ties, draw each first parent uniformly over occupied champions and each partner uniformly after distinct-identity exclusion, and retain the complete original count-GP Thompson allocator.
nodes.finding:
The retention-to-breeding connection worked. All 4,500 accepted-record map updates matched the fixed cell, score and tie rules. Across the fifteen sessions, 691 champion records received breeding draws unavailable under the old support; 527 of these were outside greedy retention. Newly supported draws produced 1,795 accepted offspring, including 1,174 from directly protected champions. Every newly supported champion with an actual draw opportunity was used, although 106 produced no selected descendant while newly supported.

Local wins increased from 648 to 738, but their summed positive score margin fell from 17.2515 to 16.9695, and mean offspring score fell from 0.3720 to 0.2898. Sequential incumbent gain fell from 5.8194 to 4.9916, with 214 advances versus 255. The complete endpoint mean was 0.541266 versus 0.596453: a paired change of −0.055187 against the required +0.002. All three seed averages and all five task means fell; twelve endpoints lost and three gained. All sessions completed, with no numerical fallback or missing endpoint.

This closes the earlier access gap: protected alternatives really did breed, enter evaluation and participate in later leaders. That access was insufficient for useful diversification. Productive typed cores increased from 303 to 386, yet only 485 parent-beating molecules bred later, versus 636 for the Parent; many local improvements were measured against weaker sources. Local niche competition also compressed the ten initial records to eight breeders in every session and retained at most 41 occupied cells, despite allowing 64.

The literature-derived elite-retention and direct-parent principles operated as adapted here; this was not a reproduction of a published molecular illumination system. Descriptor cells did not secure useful molecular context or credible geometry: the chemistry audit found 396 tiny fragments versus 105, more empty scaffolds, and inherited unusual heteroatom/ring environments. Those associations do not identify the cause of the score loss. The experiment supports a negative conditional effect of the joint fixed breeder policy, without separating retention from sampling or assigning chemical mediation. Its registered stopping condition is met, so this recipe ends. Lower dispersion, broader generic frameworks and ancestry participation do not justify a grid or sampler rescue.

nodes.hypothesis: Scale the existing correlated allocation residual by one bounded task-local multiplier learned from earlier accepted, pre-feedback standardized squared prediction errors, with shrinkage toward inherited amplitude one and no change to fitted count-GP means or cross-candidate correlation.
nodes.finding:
The fixed feedback recurrence reconstructs for all 4,350 accepted emitted predictions and excludes the 150 initial observations. Emission multipliers range from 0.586 to 2.849, preserving the raw fitted model and cross-candidate correlation. Scaling changes 377 of 435 same-pool selected sets and creates 1703 strict same-mask winner disagreements. On the actual Child stream, nominal 95% coverage moves from 77.91% using raw jittered allocation SD to 90.69% using its prospectively scaled SD; the same saved means give identical MSE 0.011318. Coverage gains are not uniform. Mean endpoint score falls from 0.595670 to 0.557528, a paired loss of 0.038141 instead of the required gain of at least 0.002. All seed macros fall (-0.044258, -0.005456 and -0.064710), while eight task-seed endpoints improve and seven decline. The largest losses are deco_hop seed 0 (-0.248112) and sitagliptin_mpo seed 2 (-0.344354); median_2 improves in every seed.

This feedback-amplitude variant is an executed but unsuccessful endpoint intervention; it does not overturn the separate evidence for retaining nonzero correlated residuals. Changing interval coverage and many selected identities is insufficient to establish useful search or calibration away from the acquired stream. Shrinkage and capped contributions preserve bounded adaptation, but 382 large errors remain in the Child diagnostics, and a common multiplier cannot anticipate a first unseen surprise. One shared first-batch miss is 253 raw allocation SDs from its prediction while the multiplier is still one. Which changed choices produce the losses remains unresolved. Molecular evidence preserves conventional alternatives and some larger improving ring families alongside reactive bond environments, crowded geometry, excessive elaboration and fragments. Those mixed examples rule out a universal size, ring or heteroatom rule as the explanation for the score loss. The next scientific question is which conditions make amplitude changes useful; these results do not justify re-tuning the preregistered constants after seeing the panel or combining sibling effects.

nodes.hypothesis: Alternate de novo sampling from a task-local GFlowNet SMILES policy with graph crossover and mutation of its refreshed scored population, then distill accepted graph descendants back into the policy through rank-weighted off-policy trajectory-balance replay with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen corpus-trained prior.
nodes.finding:
Macro mean 0.510250764298028 on the single screening seed, the highest of the thirteen roots. Per objective the run returned 0.989650581855642 on the docking objective, 0.6290937996820349 on the decoration objective, then 0.46331566856387824, 0.27137962936984883 and 0.19781414201873615 on the remaining three, so one near-saturated result plus one strong result carry most of the lead while three objectives sit low. Every pre-registered observable activated and the falsifier did not trigger. The corpus-only prior cut held-out token loss from 4.560865074576297 to 0.5625432162352548 over 29742 steps on 1268755 sequences, and 150 later integrity checks found zero changes to it. Five hundred policy-generated molecules were admitted across 50 population refreshes, and 2958 complete graph-to-policy-to-sample-to-breeding chains were reconstructed through 106 distinct policy bridges. All 76800 replay draws came from accepted observations, with realized top-rank enrichment 0.2551173919195906 above the 0.5 uniform reference. Trajectory-balance residual fell from 27.86439877950252 to 22.643096844616046 across 2400 updates, 2381 of which reduced it, and all 2240 graph-bearing updates produced nonzero graph-derived gradients over 54110 draws. Of 1450 unique proposals, 500 came from the policy and 950 from graph operators, but only 173 descendants (18.2 percent) strictly beat their best generating parent, and the mean child-minus-best-parent change was -0.09497708681416797.

The reciprocal loop demonstrably ran, and the node running it leads a field of thirteen roots whose scores span 0.2331 to 0.5103. What the run does not show is that the coupling produced the lead. Most graph offspring still fell below their generating parent, which is exactly the limitation this lineage was framed to address, so the advantage may come from the corpus-trained prior supplying realistic starting chemistry rather than from the feedback cycle itself. The per-objective spread is the sharper message: the same optimizer that nearly saturates one objective returns roughly 0.20 on another, so the campaign's current ranking is driven mostly by how well a method's proposal distribution happens to overlap each objective's answer, not by uniform competence, and a macro mean over five objectives will reward a method that wins one of them outright. With one seed and no parent this is not a reliability claim. What stays open is whether the lead survives more seeds, and whether being selective about which descendants get evaluated would convert the four-fifths of offspring that currently degrade their parent into usable gains.

nodes.hypothesis: Condition the Parent's existing graph-edit proposal distribution on a frozen unlabeled-corpus vocabulary of local atom environments, rejecting an otherwise valid novel neighbor whenever it introduces or increases the multiplicity of an unsupported environment relative to that walk's scored source state.
nodes.finding:
The intended mechanism happened on all five objectives. Using the same frozen vocabulary for both runs, 298 of 1,450 parent proposals introduced or multiplied an unsupported atom environment (20.55%); none of the 1,450 child proposals did. The mean number of introduced unsupported environments fell from 0.311 per proposal to exactly zero. The gate rejected 235 otherwise valid novel candidates and redirected 205 proposal requests to supported alternatives from the same unchanged scored source. All batches remained full, and attempts per emitted molecule rose modestly from 1.165 to 1.364. Every Metropolis decision, cooling value, working-state update and archive check agreed with the inherited rules.

On the sole evaluated seed, the mean of the five best scores rose from 0.233114 to 0.268497 (+0.035383). The improvement came from drd2_docking, which rose from 0.044776 to 0.280588. Zaleplon_mpo fell from 0.381715 to 0.322816; deco_hop stayed at 0.557517, median_2 at 0.167839, and sitagliptin_mpo at 0.013725. All 1,450 child proposals were evaluated without invalid or duplicate entries. These are single-seed results and do not establish repeatability.

The parent really was entering local environments absent or rare in the corpus: roughly one proposal in five increased their multiplicity. Supported alternatives were available with little extra retry work, so that behavior was avoidable without changing annealing or sacrificing evaluation budget. The same-run rejection traces establish this intermediate effect directly; the mixed score response leaves open whether removing these environments is broadly useful or primarily changes which stochastic paths are reached. The gain exceeds the declared 0.002 mean-score target on this seed, but one improving objective and one declining objective do not show a universal advantage or isolate which blocked chemistry caused either change.

Complete local support still allowed the chemistry assessment to find hydroperoxides, peracids, crowded bridges and N-Cl bonds. The N-Cl center environment itself occurred in eight sampled corpus molecules, so its survival follows the declared threshold rather than exposing a bypass. The improved drd2_docking maximum also retains a hydroperoxide and crowded ring topology. Local empirical support therefore narrows chemical drift but does not certify whole-molecule geometry, stability or synthetic plausibility. Coherent ring and functional-group changes remain worth investigating with rules shared across objectives. All starting and working child molecules were locally supported here, so preservation or removal of inherited unsupported environments remains an untested use case.

nodes.hypothesis: Construct each proposed molecule anew with valence-aware molecular graph actions sampled from fixed corpus-derived chemical heuristics times shared task-local bounded pheromones, then evaporate all pheromones and reinforce only the accepted batch-best molecule's actual construction trace so successful local actions guide later ants across different partial graphs.
nodes.finding:
Macro mean was 0.2523 on the single screening seed, with per-task final Top-1 of 0.5534 on the decoration-hopping objective, 0.3051 on the zaleplon multi-property objective, 0.1678 on the second median-molecule objective, 0.1371 on the dopamine-receptor docking objective and 0.0980 on the sitagliptin multi-property objective. The machinery worked in full. The construction grammar exactly replayed 39,545 of 40,000 sampled corpus molecules, a rate of 0.9886, and exactly replayed all 50 supplied starting molecules. The colony then built 1,450 molecules in 145 batches of ten, every one valid and connected, with zero invalid retries, zero duplicates and zero evaluator rejections; 77,416 construction actions were taken and 1,168 of the products were cyclic. Pheromone updates were exact in all 145 online events, always reinforcing the true highest accepted score, and probability mass genuinely shifted: 6,558 of 6,633 competitive probes increased the reinforced key's share, mean signed shift +0.0193, with 67 unchanged and 8 slightly reduced by the lower clipping bound. Sharing was real and extensive, with 71,453 selected reuses of reinforced moves in different partial molecules, 70,235 of them traceable to online feedback. The payoff did not follow. Of 1,399 accepted ants that reused online-reinforced components, only 3 beat their pre-batch incumbent, a rate of 0.0021. Initial-to-final incumbent improvements were 0, 0.00497, 0.1181, 0 and 0.0959 across the five objectives, so on two objectives no constructed molecule ever beat a supplied starting molecule, and on the decoration-hopping objective the entire 0.005 gain arrived in the first generated batch, before any online deposition could have steered it.

The campaign now has a clean separation between credit spreading and credit being useful. This root demonstrates that local-context pheromones do transfer: 70,235 selected moves reused a winner's reinforcement inside a structurally different partial molecule, with 70,175 of those reuses occurring at a different atom count entirely, so the mechanism is not a disguised prefix tree. But nearly every accepted ant inherited that bias while almost none benefited from it, which says the local key is too coarse to be selective. A context of atom identity, degree, hydrogens and ring membership recurs so often that reinforcing it nudges essentially the whole colony in the same direction rather than steering it toward the winner's chemistry. Against the twelve scored Discovery roots, whose macro means span 0.2331 to 0.5103, this root's 0.2523 ranks eleventh, in the bottom third and only marginally above the weakest root; the honest reading is that ant colony optimisation at this credit resolution is not competitive here. Two things stay open. The root deliberately deferred spreading a winner's score across the equivalent construction orders of the same molecule, which is the obvious way to make each accepted score inform more contexts, and it has not tested whether a richer key, or a deposit weighted by how distinctive a context is, would make credit selective. It is also a single seed with no parent and no ablation, so nothing here isolates the pheromone contribution from the fixed corpus heuristic that was doing the rest of the work.

nodes.hypothesis: During unlabeled prior preparation, replace the uniform nonpadding token loss by an equal-weight mean of branch-entry target loss and remaining-target loss, where a branch-entry target immediately follows the input token (, while preserving the original unweighted holdout checkpoint criterion and all online learning and generation.
nodes.finding:
The loss changed in all 89,226 preparation batches. Branch-entry targets accounted for 9.81% of 1,101,205,242 training targets; their mean assigned weight in the batch loss rose from 9.48% to 50%. All 183 registered checks showed a nonzero balanced-minus-ordinary logit-gradient change, at least 263,723 times its tolerance, with no extra optimizer steps. On the full fixed holdouts, mean branch-entry NLL fell from initialization's 4.5903 to 0.7763 nats per target. Against the paired Parent checkpoints, the mean fell from 0.8660 to 0.7763, with improvement in every seed; branch accuracy rose from 69.48% to 72.80%. Remaining-target NLL rose from 0.5318 to 0.5950, with accuracy falling from 81.32% to 79.19%; overall unweighted NLL worsened from 0.5646 to 0.6128. All preparations executed 29,742 batches, taking a mean 245.7 seconds versus 243.5 for the Parent. All 15 objectives finished with unchanged online learning and a frozen prior. Raw validity fell from 90.43% to 84.15%; duplicates fell from 30.11% to 25.61%, but novel draws also fell from 60.31% to 58.54%. The three-seed macro score fell from 0.507554 to 0.501572, a paired mean change of -0.005982. Individual seed changes were -0.016173, -0.011505 and +0.009733. Decoration hopping improved by 0.026994 on average, while sitagliptin decreased by 0.069296 and was lower in all three seeds.

The full holdouts extend the initial small probe: branch-entry prediction is a real, repeatable learning opportunity, and changing its loss allocation improves that prediction. The cost is also repeatable. Giving half the loss to roughly one-tenth of targets degrades the remaining contexts enough to worsen the ordinary language-model criterion. The observed logit-gradient movement establishes actual loss influence; it does not identify a parameter-level causal contribution to any task score. The downstream results separate branch syntax from useful attachment chemistry. Accepted scaffold variety remains broad, yet lower duplication accompanies lower validity and fewer novel raw draws. Conventional aminoquinazoline refinement can succeed locally, while the sitagliptin trajectories do not sustain favorable size, polar-group placement and nitrogen-functional-state combinations despite broad atom and ring coverage. Configurationally relevant products still lack stereochemical specification, and oversized or reactive outliers remain possible. This rules out failed loss activation and insufficient training exposure as explanations for the missing expected gain. The open question is whether context learning can preserve the much larger remaining-token group and improve useful molecular neighborhoods at the same time; improved accuracy immediately after an opening parenthesis is insufficient on its own.

nodes.hypothesis: Extend the existing graph change_bond menu with relocation of an intact single-attachment acyclic branch from an aromatic carbon to its adjacent hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon, preserving the branch, ring framework and molecular formula while exposing positional isomers to the unchanged offspring posterior.
nodes.finding:
All 191 sampled relocations preserved the complete branch, ring framework, atom attributes and molecular formula. Of these, 190 changed molecular identity and 187 became novel, encodable positional alternatives. The optimizer evaluated 15: 13 selected from ordinary pools and two protected descendants. Four of the 11 single relocations without crossover improved their scored source; one of four crossover-plus-relocation descendants beat its best generating parent. All 15 entered replay, and 14 were later used for breeding. Their later direct descendants received 64 evaluations, although only one of those 64 beat its best parent. This establishes evaluated and retained structural contribution beyond temporary pool access.

The complete three-seed panel mean rose from 0.550198 to 0.553056. The paired gain of 0.002859 exceeds the registered 0.002 minimum, but seed changes were +0.011491, -0.048498 and +0.045583. Sitagliptin and zaleplon task means rose by 0.107257 and 0.007994; deco hop, median and DRD2 fell by 0.078129, 0.019214 and 0.003614. Overall graph parent-beating yield declined from 452 to 440 of 2,850 evaluations, or 15.86% to 15.44%. Every task completed its budget, every pool filled, and all 150 protected handoffs preserved accepted neural-parent provenance.

The earlier graph-walk transfer case left useful retention unresolved: ten moves were evaluated, only one improved its source, and none was retained for a later walk. The reciprocal optimizer now demonstrates that positional alternatives can improve real molecules and enter both breeding and neural replay. The four improvements from a single relocation provide the clearest local evidence, including a fluorine move that gains 0.033311 and an ether-group move that gains 0.139485. Three task/seed terminal winners have graph ancestry through accepted relocations. This narrows the question from whether the channel can be used to when its limited evaluation allocation is worthwhile.

Selection remains a substantial filter: 172 of the 187 admitted positional alternatives were unselected and have no measured scores. Every legacy bond-order choice on an expanded menu failed sanitization, so the added options provide valid exits from otherwise failing bond choices, but they also change subsequent retries and random trajectories. The small panel gain therefore cannot be assigned wholly to the successful relocations. The largest task gain is in sitagliptin, where neither evaluated relocation improved its source and the terminal winners have no recorded graph ancestry through a relocation. Indirect effects through replay and altered search allocation remain possible. The poorer overall graph yield and opposing seed effects limit any claim of a broad efficiency improvement.

The molecular assessment supports a placement question within already abundant aromatic, amine and carbonyl chemistry. Conserving an existing group does not make that group chemically conventional: unusual nitrogen, sulfur, peroxide and strained-ring motifs, along with unspecified stereochemistry, remain in the generated molecules. Formula and core preservation establish the intended graph edit, while synthesis and stability remain outside the measured result. A separate inherited identity issue also persists in a few unselected legacy pool products; it caused no emitted-proposal or feedback failure in this panel.

nodes.hypothesis: Extend the Parent's existing atom-change menu with single-center tetrahedral-carbon configuration assignment or inversion, preserving the molecular composition and connectivity while allowing canonically distinct stereochemical neighbors to enter the unchanged novelty, tabu and accepted-score walk.
nodes.finding:
All 24 configuration-only edits reached evaluation as distinct molecular identities while preserving composition and connectivity. Each assigned one previously unspecified carbon center; both relative orientations were sampled, but no assigned-center inversion was selected. Nine of these neighbors became the next current molecule with exactly the same score as their source. Assignments also survived many subsequent structural edits: 488 of 4,350 emitted neighbors contained an assigned carbon center, compared with none for the parent. Across 32 actually evaluated pairs sharing the same graph but differing in the extent of stereochemical assignment, every pair received equal scalar feedback. The complete three-seed mean nevertheless fell from 0.520918 to 0.511159, a paired change of -0.009759, exceeding the allowed 0.002 loss. Seed changes were +0.013487, +0.001052 and -0.043817; the main losses were in DRD2 and sitagliptin, while median improved slightly and the other two task means were unchanged. The proposal mechanism activated, but this panel does not support its score usefulness.

The missing configuration channel was a real generator limitation: it can now supply fresh evaluated identities without breaking the repaired identity join or changing graph chemistry. Its immediate effect here was neutral movement through differently annotated states. Because the inherited local motifs omit stereochemistry, all nine selected assignment moves advanced memory age without installing new inverse restrictions. Such moves can alter later search even when their own scores tie; later endpoint differences therefore do not demonstrate a preference for either configuration. The equal scores establish a limitation for the sampled unspecified-to-assigned comparisons only. No opposite fully assigned pair was evaluated, so the response to genuine configuration inversion remains open. The molecular assessment also shows that stereochemical labels leave the pre-existing aromatic, reactive-heteroatom and densely bridged sulfur-rich chemistry largely intact. Partial assignments neither resolve all centers nor establish accessible three-dimensional geometry or synthetic plausibility. The experiment narrows the next scientific question to whether configuration coverage can have useful measured consequences under this feedback and walk, rather than whether the generator can emit it.

nodes.hypothesis: Publish a validation-selected exponential moving average of unlabeled recurrent training weights, with decay 0.999 and the Parent raw training trajectory and raw-NLL stopping rule preserved.
nodes.finding:
The averaged weights were distinct from the raw weights throughout validation, and all 6,633 logged coordinate updates matched the registered recurrence. The raw training losses and final raw checkpoint identities remained exactly equal to the Parent. All three preparations completed 29,742 updates and selected the final averaged state by ordinary holdout loss. Mean selected token loss fell from 0.564577 to 0.559834, improving in every seed. Averaging initially lagged the raw model, but its loss stayed lower at every validation from step 5,000 onward in all three seeds.

The final unscored diagnostic also improved in every seed. Across three 4,096-sample panels per model, valid terminated yield increased from 90.41% to 91.85%, giving 177 more valid strings. Each individual panel had no canonical duplicates or missing EOS, so its valid and canonical-unique yields were equal. The gains were 2.34, 1.54 and 0.44 percentage points across seeds. This pure-prior gain did not carry through to higher adapted-policy validity: across the same 12,000 online draws, validity was 70.06% versus Parent 70.34%, with first-batch validity 90.92% versus 91.17% and later-batch validity 67.74% versus 68.03%.

All fifteen tasks completed. Three-seed mean final Top-1 rose from 0.520669 to 0.527370; paired gains were 0.000602, 0.004046 and 0.015453. The improvement was concentrated in sitagliptin, while deco-hop and median scores fell in every seed and zaleplon was mixed. Recorded mean preparation time was 238.0 seconds versus 259.5 seconds, with identical training horizons; these total timings do not isolate the extra averaging and diagnostic cost.

This provides evidence that averaging the same unlabeled weight trajectory can produce a better reusable prior without changing training examples, gradient updates or the online algorithm. Exact raw checkpoint identities and matching raw loss histories rule out altered raw training as the explanation. The final pure-prior comparison was excluded from checkpoint selection, so its consistent yield improvement adds evidence beyond the heldout criterion that selected the average. The early lag also limits the result: the benefit appears after substantial training, and is not evidence that averaged weights are preferable throughout learning.

Better pure-prior likelihood and parseable yield were insufficient to improve validity after task adaptation or provide broad task gains. The chemistry explains why the score increase deserves a narrower interpretation: ordinary aryl/carbonyl and amine families coexist with N-fluorinated motifs, unusual hydrogen-bearing sulfur, azide/acyl-halide assemblies and contracted rings. Favorable scores do not establish those connections as necessary or synthetically credible. Explicit stereochemical configurations remain absent. The remaining question is how much of the improved reusable prior can survive accepted-score adaptation while retaining credible functional-group attachment and useful core coverage; this experiment demonstrates the averaging effect, but does not resolve that downstream limitation.

nodes.hypothesis: At every inherited refit, select the Morgan environment radius of the inherited dot-product count Tanimoto covariance from the menu 1, 2 or 3 over the same chirality-aware 2048-bin folded count vocabulary by the maximum exact log marginal likelihood of the inherited standardized accepted targets under observation noise SD 0.05 and the inherited jitter ladder, preferring the inherited radius 2 on an exact tie or a failed factorization, and use that single selected radius coherently for the training, cross, pool and probe features, the posterior mean and the correlated residual covariance of that batch.
nodes.finding:
The selection ran on every one of the 435 model refits, and an independent recomputation reproduced every choice. It was far from a no-op: the inherited radius 2 won only 67 refits, against 146 for radius 1 and 222 for radius 3. Each task settled into its own pattern, closely matching what the Parent's own data would have preferred. median_2 always chose radius 1 and sitagliptin_mpo always chose radius 3; zaleplon_mpo chose radius 3 in all but one refit. drd2_docking started at radius 3 and moved to radius 2 as the archive grew, and deco_hop depended on the seed. Most choices were decisive (median margin 23 nats). The exception is the very first refit on the ten fixed starting molecules, decided by under 1 nat, which already sent every run off the Parent's path at the first batch. Everything outside the radius behaved identically. Batch sizes, pools, fallbacks, the sulfur gate and random draws were unchanged, and the first-batch candidate pools and random numbers were identical to the Parent's. Compared with the inherited radius-2 model scored on exactly the same molecules and states, the chosen model was slightly better calibrated: squared error on the scored molecules was 0.00845 against 0.00849. It ranked them slightly worse within a batch: rank correlation 0.539 against 0.548. The split follows the radius. Where radius 1 was chosen, ranking improved (median_2 0.80 vs 0.77; deco_hop 0.53 vs 0.51). Where radius 3 was chosen, it worsened (zaleplon_mpo 0.42 vs 0.47; sitagliptin_mpo 0.41 vs 0.43; drd2_docking 0.53 vs 0.56), and the spread of predicted means across the candidate pool shrank to about 0.86 of the radius-2 spread. The complete matched mean fell from 0.5965 to 0.5565, a change of -0.040 against the required +0.002. Seeds moved by -0.089, +0.021 and -0.052, and only 6 of 15 task-seed cells improved. Three cells carry the entire loss: deco_hop seed 0 (-0.221) and sitagliptin_mpo seeds 0 and 2 (-0.217, -0.169). The deco_hop cell is the Parent's rare late breakthrough to 0.856, which the Child, like every recent Child, never reached; it was actually ahead of the Parent at evaluations 200 and 250 before plateauing at 0.635. In the two sitagliptin_mpo cells the Child fell behind early (best 0.28 vs 0.51 and 0.29 vs 0.39 at evaluation 100) and never caught up. median_2, the task the brief singled out, improved modestly: mean 0.2317 vs 0.2227, with one cell at 0.2418, above every round-28 sibling cell. The other twelve cells net to roughly zero.

Selecting a hyperparameter by marginal likelihood has now twice been exactly activated, slightly improved calibration, weakened within-batch ranking and lost endpoint score. Here the selected quantity was the fingerprint radius; in the earlier test it was the observation noise. In this lineage, a better marginal-likelihood fit of the accepted archive is not a guide to better candidate ranking. The decomposition shows why. Radius 3 wins on the data-fit term, not on model complexity. With amplitude fixed at 1 and noise fixed at 0.05, the model cannot otherwise explain near-identical molecules with very different scores. A larger radius makes neighbours look less alike and absorbs the clash. So the radius ends up acting as a stand-in for missing roughness or noise freedom, and the result is a flatter posterior mean that discriminates less among candidates. The molecular review fits this. On the two tasks with the largest losses, the Child's molecules drifted from what the Parent kept: on deco_hop it hung chains on a frozen core where the Parent made a ring-level change, and on sitagliptin_mpo it built dienol and thioketone chemistry where the Parent kept an intact N-aryl ring. Radius 1, by contrast, sharpened ranking where it was chosen, and its median_2 cell at 0.2418 is the first to clear the band that all 24 round-28 sibling cells sat in. That suggests a narrower follow-up: allow only the finer radius, or fit amplitude and noise jointly so the radius stops doing their job, or select by chronological ranking quality rather than likelihood. It also rules out simply turning up locality as a general fix. Still open: whether the radius-1 benefit survives on its own; whether the radius-3 harm is causal or partly path noise, since every run diverges from the first batch; and whether preferences at the edge of the menu point to radius 0 or 4. The deco_hop seed-0 cell should be read as a rare event when comparing against this Parent.

nodes.hypothesis: Coalesce each corpus-observed complete bracket-atom expression into one reversible SMILES token, with inherited Cl/Br-and-character fallback for unseen bracket expressions, so prior learning and its shared sequence interface model an atom together with its explicit hydrogen and charge state.
nodes.finding:
The new representation was used and learned in all three seeds. Every one of the 1,272,851 eligible corpus strings round-trips exactly, and the original training/holdout membership is preserved. Each holdout contains 1,013 complete bracket targets; their average negative log likelihood falls from about 5.08–5.14 before training to 2.07–2.27 after training. On identical holdout molecules, the learned prior also assigns better normalized likelihood to bracket-bearing sequences than the Parent in every seed. Prior freezing, fresh objective state and all online replay/update methods remain intact. Across the search panel, the raw invalid-string fraction falls from 9.568% to 8.573%, and both implementations complete every required batch. That local improvement does not yield the expected score gain: the macro mean is 0.506571 versus 0.507554, a paired change of -0.000983 rather than the registered increase of at least 0.002. Seed changes are -0.022179, +0.002069 and +0.017160. Gains in three task means are offset mainly by a 0.058039 decline in the sitagliptin mean, present in all three seeds. The smaller observed score SD, 0.004690 versus 0.011518, is descriptive evidence from this panel, not a reliability guarantee.

Learning coherent atom-state units is supported, but better likelihood on those units does not ensure that objective-driven generation retains or exploits more of them. Accepted original strings containing bracket atoms actually fall from 1,269 to 835 out of 4,350 proposals; charged forms also become less common. The output still reaches recognizable medicinal scaffold families, while the Molecular assessment finds excessive low-scoring growth, reactive outliers and unspecified configurations. The experiment therefore narrows the unresolved issue to how a learned representation interacts with the existing search dynamics and chemical coverage, rather than a failure to encode or learn the registered units. The reduction in aggregate invalid strings does not identify bracket syntax as the Parent error source because rejected strings were not saved. No stereochemical supervision exists in this corpus, and none is created by the representation. The panel varies both preparation and search by seed, so it cannot isolate which stage caused the mixed task effects.
