nodes.hypothesis: Among exact accepted-score batch maxima, select the neighbor with greatest multiset-Jaccard distance between its inherited radius-one motif occurrence counts and the current source's counts, then use canonical lexical order for any remaining tie.
nodes.finding:
Twenty choices among equally best accepted molecules changed the next walk state, and all 20 increased exact motif distance from the current molecule without giving up the accepted maximum score. Eighteen occurred at the same score as the source, one during an improving move and one during a worsening move. Nineteen choices had actual continuations; one was terminal. The rule encountered 40 exact maximum ties, compared with 26 in the parent, while preserving canonical fallback and the original feedback, archive and memory rules. Plateau episodes contained 60 equal-score moves, each visiting a distinct motif profile within its episode, compared with 49 such moves in the parent. Coverage per move was unchanged, and the longest plateau grew from six moves to nine. The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.519947, a paired loss of 0.001812 against the required gain of 0.002. One seed improved slightly and two declined. Only deco_hop endpoints changed; the other four task endpoints were identical in every seed.

The experiment rules out failure to exercise the selector: it changed real, scored next states and was followed by 600 later accepted proposals after removing overlap between the recorded histories. It also shows why larger local structural steps are insufficient evidence of more useful exploration. The extra plateau profiles came with extra plateau moves, and longer equal-score episodes still appeared. Twenty later archive gains occurred in the affected continuations, compared with 26 in the corresponding recorded parent histories, but the overlapping paths prevent assigning a causal gain to each tie choice. The rule sometimes chose smaller molecules and sometimes larger ones. The molecular assessment finds that some equally scored differences introduce reactive attachments or unusual sulfur connectivity, while conventional ring and carbonyl families remain available. Greater distance between local motif counts therefore supplies neither compactness nor chemical plausibility. The direct selection mechanism is confirmed; its proposed overall score benefit is refuted on this panel. What remains open is whether a distance that distinguishes useful structural alternatives from score-insensitive local decoration can improve later search; this experiment does not settle that broader question.

nodes.hypothesis: A corpus-trained autoregressive SMILES policy is adapted independently in each objective by Augmented Hill-Climb on only the current scored batch elites, fitting policy log likelihood toward frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward, and proposes new molecules by direct token sampling from the updated policy.
nodes.finding:
Macro mean 0.4766 on the single screening seed, with per-task finals of 0.6029 on deco_hop, 0.99999961 on drd2_docking, 0.1844 on median_2, 0.1428 on sitagliptin_mpo and 0.4532 on zaleplon_mpo. That drd2_docking figure is effectively a saturated objective and the highest single-task result among the three roots examined here; the sitagliptin_mpo figure is the lowest. All observables behaved as intended and the falsifier was not triggered. The corpus prior learned well - token-normalized next-token loss fell from 4.5609 to 0.5625 on a fixed 4096-sequence holdout over 29742 steps on 1268755 sequences - and was verifiably frozen thereafter, with the prior checkpoint hash and zero prior-parameter changes recorded across all 5 initializations and all 150 updates. The update mechanism did what it claims: mean elite squared error fell from 201.89 to 110.54, decreasing in 148 of 150 updates, and mean elite sequence log-likelihood rose by +2.321 while non-elite log-likelihood fell by -1.052, confirming the update is genuinely selective rather than raising everything. All 750 training members were verified to be the current batch's top-scoring half, with zero historical replay anywhere. Generation stayed healthy: 10492 of 11632 sampled sequences were RDKit-valid, a rate of 0.902, and all 145 rounds filled a batch of exactly ten valid novel molecules with zero rejections at the evaluator.

The campaign now has a sharp picture of when elite likelihood sharpening pays. Among the thirteen Discovery roots on this seed, spanning 0.2331 to 0.5103, this sits fifth at 0.4766, but the aggregate hides the real signal: this method produced both the strongest single-objective result in this group and the weakest. Where a learnable structural motif exists and is reachable from the corpus prior, sharpening onto it is extremely effective - one objective is essentially solved. Where the reward distribution collapses, it has nothing to work with: on the weakest objective the median score across the entire run was exactly zero, its mean elite squared error was 4.94 against 735 on the objective that saturated, and the only two updates in the whole node that increased loss were both from that run. An elite half selected from ten molecules that all score zero is an arbitrary five, and the policy then drifts back to generic prior chemistry. That is a concrete, actionable characterisation of the method's failure mode and a strong argument that any Development on this lineage should target the low-signal regime - a reward transform, a ranking that survives ties, or the historical replay the root deliberately declined - rather than the update rule itself. A second caution: elite likelihood rose in only 111 of 150 individual updates even though the aggregate is clearly positive, so single updates are noisy and the mechanism works on average rather than reliably. Still open: one seed, no paired comparison, no anchor decision, and no evidence on whether the drd2_docking saturation reflects a genuinely easy objective or a policy exploiting it.

nodes.hypothesis: Reduce the scored CMA generation target to the smallest whole number of evaluator-announced batches containing at least two offspring, so accepted feedback updates the inherited Gaussian after each complete protocol batch whenever that batch already contains at least two members.
nodes.finding:
Every completed batch immediately updated the Gaussian, and the next batch used that updated distribution. For each of the five tasks, accepted offspring waited through zero further batch emissions before their update, versus a mean of 0.5 emissions among updated Parent offspring. The Parent also left 10 accepted offspring per task in an unfinished terminal generation; the Child left none. Feedback changed the distribution used for the next proposals after 28 of 28 nonterminal batches, up from 14 of 28. Each task completed 29 updates, including one terminal update with no later proposals. The frozen representation and update equations were preserved, and all rank, covariance, path, step-size and sampling checks passed. Nevertheless, the seed-0 mean of final best scores fell from 0.302617 to 0.280194, a change of −0.022423 rather than the predicted gain of at least 0.002. zaleplon_mpo fell from 0.443203 to 0.363235, deco_hop from 0.610746 to 0.603856, drd2_docking from 0.063511 to 0.029010, and median_2 from 0.208415 to 0.198819. sitagliptin_mpo improved from 0.187211 to 0.206051. Both runs used all 300 evaluations per task. Raw Gaussian decodes rose from 4,800 to 9,280 across the suite; recorded suite time rose from 43.68 to 97.64 seconds, including oracle and runtime variation.

Removing the measured feedback wait did not solve the score limitation in this replica. More updates also meant smaller selected populations: effective selection mass fell from 5.94 to 3.17, and average covariance movement per update decreased on every task. Thus update count is insufficient evidence of stronger or more useful adaptation. The docking trajectory makes the distinction concrete: 25 of its 29 generations contained tied scores, and one update had weighted score enrichment of only about 2.6 × 10⁻¹³ despite moving the Gaussian. The molecular assessment still finds oversized hydrocarbons, repeated imine or sulfur linkers, and elaborate carbonyl-bearing rings, with limited controlled variation of conventional scaffolds. Faster reaction to the available scores did not resolve those generator limitations. This supports investigating the representation and the informativeness of sampled regions alongside adaptation cadence. It does not establish which caused the score loss, whether the smaller selection mass increased harmful noise, or whether the result generalizes beyond the single paired seed.

nodes.hypothesis: Conditionally normalize the unchanged selected current-and-historical augmented likelihood targets by a single shared offset: for a_i = frozen_prior_log_likelihood_i + 60 * accepted_score_i, fit t_i = a_i - max(0, logsumexp_j(a_j)) over the actual selected training union, preserving equal row weights, pairwise target differences and every target when its joint probability mass is already at most one.
nodes.finding:
The intended target and learning changes occurred. Of 430 recorded updates, 232 needed normalization. All 232 removed excess joint target probability mass, eliminated all 1,252 individually positive log-probability targets, preserved the differences between selected targets within the registered tolerance, and changed the combined learning gradient. The other 198 updates retained their targets exactly and had identical projected-target and raw-target gradients. Among the 219 history-bearing positive-offset updates followed by a successful proposal batch, pooled projected mean squared error fell from 164.659 to 9.544 and decreased in every update. Current-example error fell from 311.898 to 13.978 and historical-example error from 17.421 to 5.110. Individual historical errors still worsened in 288 of 1,095 exposures. The raw-target error, measured at those same before/after policy states, rose from 263.347 to 286.769; the optimizer was fitting the changed objective.

Search reliability deteriorated despite those fitting gains. Thirteen of fifteen task replicas completed their 300 evaluations. Docking seeds 0 and 2 stopped at 260 and 140 evaluations because the policy could not refill a valid novel batch. In their final failed requests, 60,076 of 65,544 draws and 65,553 of 65,568 draws did not terminate. The child therefore has no complete three-seed macro mean. The sole complete seed scored 0.527720 versus its parent’s 0.514385, a paired gain of 0.013335. Among tasks completed in all three seeds, mean final-best score increased from 0.459183 to 0.471568 for zaleplon and from 0.601097 to 0.718554 for scaffold hopping, stayed at 0.218884 for median similarity, and fell from 0.288538 to 0.286001 for sitagliptin. These completed-task results cannot establish the proposed three-seed macro improvement.

Removing impossible selected-target demands is sufficient to change the learner, but insufficient to preserve useful generation. Across the same 415 successful suggestion positions, the child used 73,384 raw draws versus 35,144 for the parent. Its duplicate fraction fell from 38.92% to 10.33%, while its unterminated fraction rose from 0.003% to 44.21%; the two failed requests add a further 131,112 draws. Lower duplication therefore did not mean a more productive sampler. Both updates immediately before those failures reduced projected fitting error and had measurable gradient changes, so successful normalization and fitting do not rule out loss of sequence completion. The evidence identifies a failure in the resulting proposal distribution, but does not isolate which token changes caused it.

The condition itself has strong controls: all three median-similarity sessions and two sitagliptin sessions never needed normalization and reproduced their parent molecule-and-score trajectories exactly. Every trajectory that changed first diverged after a positive-offset update. In the useful history-bearing opportunities, the common shift reversed 722 selected rows from upward likelihood pressure to downward pressure, even though their relative target preferences were preserved. This narrows the unresolved question to what the shifted regression does to shared sequence-model support, including termination and molecules outside the fitted union. The supplied chemistry assessment finds recognizable compact aromatic and basic-amine families among the leaders alongside attachment drift, excessive chain or ring growth, and absent stereochemical specification. A necessary probability bound on selected strings does not resolve those chemical limitations. The completed-task gains justify studying the conditional target effect further only with generation reliability and useful chemical transfer measured alongside fitting.

nodes.hypothesis: During unlabeled prior training, mix each selected molecule's supplied SMILES with one cached, deterministic atom-rooted SMILES view whose canonical/isomeric molecular identity is verified, exposing the unchanged recurrent model to equivalent attachment contexts while keeping online learning and sampling unchanged.
nodes.finding:
Across three preparations, changed equivalent views appeared 10,938,511 times and contributed 553,572,420 target tokens to real training batches. Reconstructing all 3,629,346 cached row/view pairs and every training tensor receipt found no identity, token round-trip, length, or holdout-membership violation. The fixed panels contained 11,774 changed views. Their alternate NLL fell from 4.5739 to 0.7043 nats per alternate token. Under the same independent checkpoint comparison, alternate NLL improved from the parent's 1.6256 to 0.7043, while original-string NLL worsened from 0.5638 to 0.6004. The alternate-minus-original full-sequence NLL gap narrowed from 55.16 to 6.61 nats per changed molecule. Each preparation finished 29,742 training batches; mean preparation time rose from 243.5 to 902.0 seconds, with a 401.8 MiB temporary cache. On the same 14 completed tasks, raw validity fell from 90.24% to 86.55%, duplicates fell from 29.22% to 23.47%, and novel draws rose from 61.01% to 63.08%. Mean accepted scaffold counts stayed similar (218.4 to 217.2), while late scaffold concentration increased. The two completed paired seeds scored 0.51444 versus 0.51394, a mean change of +0.00050; their individual changes were -0.00199 and +0.00300. The third DRD2 run stopped at 170 evaluations because an emitted aromatic string changed canonical form when reparsed, activating the unchanged feedback-provenance guard. Its incomplete task leaves the three-seed macro score unavailable. All logged online updates preserve the frozen prior and original accepted replay strings.

Equivalent traversal exposure reached the training loss and transferred to held-out alternative strings. The smaller serialization preference is supported by improved alternate likelihood, while the loss on the supplied strings makes the tradeoff visible. This narrows the bottleneck: adding sequence contexts can improve traversal coverage without delivering reliable chemical search improvement. Lower duplicate rates did not translate into broader accepted scaffold coverage; invalid draws increased and late chemical families became more concentrated. The chemistry still favors conventional aromatic amine and carbonyl families, with unresolved attachment placement, extreme-size tails and reactive outliers. No missing stereochemical information was recovered. The available score changes are mixed and the completed-seed mean gain is below the registered 0.002 effect; the failed third task prevents the full intended score comparison. The specific canonicalization key mismatch identifies a separate robustness gap in the inherited feedback interface. Preparation stayed within the existing deadline and retained the same number of training batches, so lost training steps do not explain this outcome. Whether improved equivalent-string likelihood can preserve original-string quality and improve useful chemical coverage remains open.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove only immediate access of the newest nonempty accepted observe cohort to both breeding-parent consumers by using the original bounded greedy population from immediately before that cohort; release a cohort after the next real nonempty accepted cohort, while ordinary current survival and full accepted-archive GP learning remain immediate.
nodes.finding:
The delay operated in all fifteen task/seed runs. None of 110,134 parent draws used the newest accepted cohort, although 2,522 newly accepted molecules had positive support under the immediate current-population law. Later recursion remained active: 2,409 accepted offspring eventually bred, producing 4,031 accepted products with generated parents. All 435 full-archive predictor fits and all 435 fresh pools completed. Maturity did not guarantee use: 841 retained offspring never received positive support and another 56 supported offspring were never drawn. The final 150 offspring lacked a future maturation event; the preceding 150 matured only at terminal feedback and had no subsequent breeding opportunity.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.543300, a paired change of -0.052370 against the registered 0.002 scale. Seed macro changes were -0.115073, -0.011259 and -0.030776. Ten task/seed endpoints declined and five improved: the exceptions were two zaleplon runs, two median-similarity runs and one decoration-hopping run. Docking and sitagliptin declined in every seed. Seed macro population SD decreased slightly, from 0.026593 to 0.024744.

Strict offspring-versus-best-parent wins increased from 629 to 877, but mean absolute offspring scores fell from 0.385256 to 0.321667 and mean best-generating-parent scores fell from 0.470456 to 0.384678. Incumbent advances fell from 258 to 219, with total increment magnitude decreasing from 5.807663 to 5.022119 across the fifteen searches.

Prompt reuse contributes beyond simply allowing accepted offspring to breed eventually, under this fixed optimizer, feedback cadence and evaluation budget. Full learning from new scores remained immediate, so withholding those labels from the predictor does not explain this contrast. The previous static-initial experiment established the value of recursive access overall; this result adds a narrower timing answer while preserving that earlier finding.

More local parent wins are compatible with worse search when breeding sources themselves have lower scores. Similar numbers of distinct reused offspring also conceal shallower scored ancestry: maximum depth fell from 23 to 14. These observations narrow the explanations, but do not establish that ancestry depth, source quality or molecular age caused the endpoint loss. Support, ranks, sampling probabilities, random consumption and subsequent adaptive histories all changed together.

The molecular assessment found rich ring systems, useful amine and carbonyl arrangements, and seed-dependent scaffold families in both runs, alongside recurring reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds, difficult ring geometries and unspecified stereochemistry. Chemically mixed alternatives and task-specific improvements remain visible. The timing contrast identifies no chemical mediator or general shortage of rings or functional groups. Whole-foundation value, interaction with the separate learner control, and reliability beyond these three matched seeds remain open.

nodes.hypothesis: Sever recursive accepted-offspring breeding feedback by fixing every breeding-parent draw and breeding-cohort availability check to an immutable copy of the ordinary initial usable score-ranked population, while preserving active posterior learning from all real accepted observations and the live survivor updates used for tracking and reporting.
nodes.finding:
Every one of 122,044 Child parent draws came from the unchanged initial cohort; no accepted offspring became a breeding parent. The Parent used accepted offspring in 105,073 of 110,295 draws. All fifteen task/seed sessions matched through their first complete batch, then diverged at the first parent, pool member and evaluated molecule of batch two. Generated offspring still entered the live survivors and the full score archive. All 435 accepted-label posterior fits and original sampled-maximum allocations remained active. All pools filled, all three seeds completed, and no natural fallback or exhaustion occurred.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.335464, a paired change of -0.260206 against the registered 0.002 loss scale. Seed macro changes were -0.306557, -0.273839 and -0.200221. Every one of fifteen task-seed endpoints and all five task means declined. Population deviation across seed macros rose from 0.026593 to 0.047795. Local parent beats increased from 629 to 2,007 against the easier fixed initial comparators, while incumbent improvements fell from 258 to 84. Generation also encountered more duplicate proposals: 14,385 versus 6,358.

These complete, exposed results establish positive conditional contribution of recursive offspring-to-breeder feedback within the current optimizer, even while accepted-label posterior learning remains active. The initial cohort contains ten molecules, but only five have positive support under the inherited unexcluded quantile law. Fixing that breeder holds membership, ordering and cohort size together; this experiment cannot apportion their effects or isolate the survivor rule. It also leaves the broader whole-foundation question open. Separate component removals and shared-Parent siblings cannot be added into a joint value estimate.

The local success counts illustrate why ancestry and endpoint quality must be kept separate. Beating an initial molecule becomes more common, and prediction errors are smaller on the changed evaluated distribution, yet the search makes fewer incumbent gains and ends lower. Every Child endpoint still exceeds its initial best. The molecular assessment finds useful available amines, ring closures and scaffold rearrangements alongside recurring initial amide, nitrile/carbonyl and dione organizations. Some lower-scoring Child leaders have more familiar local chemistry than the higher-scoring Parent leaders. The deficit therefore does not establish an absence of chemical novelty, require reactive motifs, or identify a chemical mediator. Scored ancestry depth one also allows unscored multistep edits and crossover finishing.

The fixed neighborhoods remained productive enough to fill all full pools under inherited bounds, although they required more attempts. No rescue from live survivors was used. Exhaustion and recovery semantics passed source and synthetic checks but were not naturally exercised. Three matched Search seeds support this descriptive conditional result; they do not establish universal reliability or value for unobserved descendants.

nodes.hypothesis: Reserve each selected rollout along its prefix path and include completed plus pending counts in UCT's exploration term, while retaining accepted-only empirical reward means; release each reservation when the rollout is discarded or its observation resolves.
nodes.finding:
On the single paired screening seed, pending work changed 4,361 of 5,834 branch decisions with a choice between eligible children (74.75%). Of these changes, 3,961 came from altered UCT rankings among completed children; another 400 involved priority for children without completed observations. All 2,900 reservations resolved exactly once, without negative counts, leaks or changes to completed reward statistics. Mean concentration of evaluated rollout-start prefixes fell from 0.809379 to 0.117517 across 145 batches, and distinct prefixes per ten-molecule batch rose from 1.73 to 9.54. Single-prefix batches fell from 76 of 145 to zero, with lower concentration on all five objectives and every paired batch. Both runs delivered all 1,450 valid, unique optimizer proposals within the same oracle budget and retained identical frozen prior weights. The macro final Top-1 score nevertheless fell from 0.479189 to 0.473468, a decrease of 0.005720. Final scores rose for zaleplon_mpo (0.394920 to 0.409811), drd2_docking (0.977922 to 0.999998), and median_2 (0.179942 to 0.180094), while deco_hop fell from 0.606003 to 0.580076 and sitagliptin_mpo from 0.237157 to 0.197364. The proposed allocation mechanism is confirmed; its expected positive score effect was not observed.

Delayed-feedback concentration is controllable with the existing frozen generator and accepted-only reward estimates. The controlled replay establishes that outstanding work changes actual choices, and the emitted-molecule analysis establishes that the added branch coverage survives invalid, duplicate and surplus filtering. However, almost complete dispersion across ten starting prefixes did not produce a better overall best molecule within the screening budget. This leaves the useful balance between branch reuse and wider allocation open; the score losses do not establish that reservations are generally harmful. The molecular assessment found broadly diverse ring chemistry comparable to the Parent, with useful amine and heteroaromatic motifs already reachable but inconsistent control of their arrangement and whole-molecule growth. That narrows the unresolved problem to obtaining and refining useful chemical combinations: a larger count of distinct SMILES prefixes alone does not establish better chemical coverage. These structural observations suggest an explanation to investigate, not a demonstrated cause of the score decrease. One seed supports activation and a mixed score outcome, without establishing reproducibility or which degree of allocation spread would improve final Top-1.

nodes.hypothesis: Evolve a task-local population of scored molecular graphs by sampling breeding parents across high-ranked score quantiles, generating de novo offspring with graph crossover and atom/bond mutation, and greedily retaining the highest-scoring observed survivors after each feedback batch.
nodes.finding:
Macro mean 0.4917 on the single screening seed, with per-task finals of 0.5989 on deco_hop, 0.9051 on drd2_docking, 0.2083 on median_2, 0.3315 on sitagliptin_mpo and 0.4145 on zaleplon_mpo. All four pre-registered observables moved in the intended direction and the falsifier was not triggered. Parent selection was strongly score-directed: across 2225 breeding selections the mean topness percentile was 0.883 against a uniform baseline of 0.5, an enrichment of +0.383, and all three declared quantile bands were used on every task. Both operator families produced offspring on every task, with crossover behind 0.439 and atom/bond mutation behind 0.743 of the 1450 emitted molecules; 74 outer retries were needed for 1524 attempts. Feedback demonstrably changed the search: 1025 offspring were admitted to the population immediately, 432 distinct admitted offspring were later chosen as parents 2084 times, and reuse began in batch 2 on every task. Final population best rose above initialization everywhere, most sharply on drd2_docking (0.0190 to 0.9051) and sitagliptin_mpo (0.0021 to 0.3315). The one weak number is local improvement: only 201 of 1450 offspring, or 13.9 percent, strictly beat their best breeding parent, and the mean child-minus-best-parent difference was -0.084.

The campaign now has a strong, cheap baseline. Against the thirteen Discovery roots on this seed, which span 0.2331 to 0.5103, this root sits third at 0.4917, within 0.019 of the best method in the round, and it did that with no pretraining, no corpus-trained generator, no surrogate and no learned policy. That reframes what the more elaborate lineages have to justify: any learned component now has to earn its place against direct selection on task-local scores, not against a naive baseline. The interesting tension is that activation was clean while efficiency was not. Roughly six in seven oracle calls went to molecules that did not beat the parent that made them, and the mean offspring was worse than its parent, so the strong result comes from occasionally getting lucky at scale rather than from reliably climbing. That is precisely the bottleneck a proposal-filtering mechanism would attack, and it is the most concrete Development target this root produces. What is still open: one seed only, so no reliability claim and no anchor decision; no paired comparison against any other algorithm; and the retry machinery was never stressed, since the longest rejection streak was two, so behaviour on an exhausted or hostile neighbourhood is untested.

nodes.hypothesis: Recover the recorded post-adaptation left-inverse crash by promoting the loaded task-local sequence flow and its continuous recurrent forward/inverse latent calculations from float32 to float64, with dtype-compatible probe assignment and unchanged strict token reconstruction checks.
nodes.finding:
On the screening seed, all five objectives complete 300 evaluations. The two sessions that previously stopped at 150 and 240 evaluations now finish, bringing the total from 1,290 to 1,500. All 300 reconstruction checks preserve the full padded token sequence and canonical molecule: 46,500 of 46,500 observation-check instances match exactly. At the former failure points, maximum continuous inverse error falls from 0.405526 to 0.000005301 on drd2_docking and from 0.404005 to 0.00000001510 on median_2. Preparation produces the identical checkpoint. All 150 online adaptations execute their original 24 steps, every GP fit uses freshly encoded observations, PMI still favors informative token blocks, and posterior uncertainty still affects selection. Every emitted batch contains ten valid novel molecules. The completed macro score is 0.419751565. All 1,290 shared trajectory records match the parent exactly, and the additional 210 evaluations produce no new task best. Because the parent lacks a complete macro score, these results establish numerical recovery without establishing a paired macro-score gain.

The result supports finite-precision recurrent inverse drift as a recoverable implementation bottleneck: strict equality survives without omitting padding, dropping observations, or skipping adaptation. It does not identify the original mismatched token positions, so a padding-only explanation remains unproven. Numerical recovery also leaves the main search-quality questions intact. Nominal 95% GP intervals cover only 466 of 1,450 outcomes (32.1%); coverage on the 1,240 shared predictions is unchanged at 444 outcomes, and only 22 of the 210 added predictions are covered. In addition, 97.6% of examined decodes reproduce their generating center. The molecular assessment finds the same narrow high-scoring families and recurring unusual charged heteroatoms and chain growth, with weak chemical plausibility. These findings make surrogate calibration and useful, chemically credible local variation worth probing independently. Recovery is demonstrated for this seed and checkpoint under the existing budget; continuous inverse error still reaches 0.004864 in one successful check, so exact reconstruction here does not establish stability for arbitrary future histories.

nodes.hypothesis: Condition later within-batch posterior draw residuals on earlier selected pool molecules taking their current posterior means, so pending selections remove shared sampling uncertainty before subsequent masked maximization.
nodes.finding:
All 3,915 within-batch projections executed correctly. On identical Child pools and random draws, they preserved all 435 first choices but changed 600 of 4,350 selection positions and 287 of 435 batch sets. Later selected molecules lost an average 3.30% of their original sampling variance; the median reduction was 0.81%. Mean absolute within-batch posterior correlation fell from 0.04721 to 0.04571, and mean nonempty molecular-core coverage rose slightly from 7.06 to 7.14 cores per ten-molecule batch. Neither consequence was universal. All batches and evaluations completed.

The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.57434 to 0.57250, a change of -0.00184 against the registered +0.002 minimum. One seed improved and two declined. Mean final scores rose for sitagliptin by 0.01151 and zaleplon by 0.00714, while DRD2 fell by 0.01705, median similarity by 0.00706 and decoration hopping by 0.00376. Strict improvements over the best generating parent increased from 624 to 677 out of 4,350 offspring, and incumbent improvements rose from 241 to 278. On their respective scored streams, prediction MSE fell from 0.011269 to 0.009821, but mean within-batch rank correlation fell from 0.550 to 0.534 and nominal 95% latent-interval coverage fell from 76.9% to 76.1%. Correct conditioning and better local improvement counts did not deliver the intended final-score gain.

The experiment establishes a real allocation effect and narrows its value: removing some shared posterior variation is insufficient by itself to improve the final best score on this panel. The intervention reaches a modest typical redundancy opportunity, with a larger tail, and still permits related high-mean molecules to occupy the same batch. Even on identical pools, average count-fingerprint similarity increased slightly while posterior correlation decreased. Lower model correlation therefore cannot substitute for chemical diversity or score evidence. More parent-beating offspring and more incremental incumbent improvements also proved insufficient as proxies for the final endpoint.

The lower MSE describes a changed adaptive search stream; the fitted prediction model and its means remained unchanged on shared inputs. Mean conditioning supplied no new labels and did not repair the already poor uncertainty coverage. Whether real pending outcomes would support these zero-innovation constraints remains open, and unobserved counterfactual choices cannot answer it. The molecular assessment further limits the small core-coverage gain: smaller assemblies now contain many more small or tightly bridged rings, while reactive bonds and unspecified stereochemistry persist. Graph-core novelty is not evidence of feasible chemistry. A stronger test of useful batch coordination would need to connect model redundancy to actual score dependence or chemically meaningful alternatives; this run rules out treating the measured contraction alone as evidence of that connection.

nodes.hypothesis: Retain a separate inverse-motif restriction for every still-live selected-transition provenance when signed motif keys overlap, so later installations do not overwrite older provenance and the unchanged same-transition bidirectional veto can use each origin until its own original expiry or documented oldest-entry release.
nodes.finding:
Across the 15 task-and-seed sessions, 45 older restrictions survived overlapping installations without losing their original provenance or expiry. They preserved four bidirectional transition groups that the latest-origin rule would have broken. On the same accepted histories, this produced one additional veto among 4,545 valid novel candidate tests; two other tests gained an older qualifying origin but were already vetoed. The extra veto changed one complete ten-molecule batch in deco_hop seed 1. Its replacement was evaluated, beat the source by 0.004805, became the next state and immediately raised the best observed score by 0.002352. Nevertheless, this seed finished at 0.594191 versus the parent's 0.605140. All 14 other trajectories were unchanged. The three-seed macro mean was 0.521029 versus 0.521759, a paired change of -0.000730 against the required +0.002. Across all 4,350 accepted proposals, the source-beating frequency fell from 10.759% to 10.621%, and strict archive improvements fell from 238 to 232. Provenance retention and evaluation redirection are confirmed; the specified score-benefit claim is refuted.

Premature overwrite can remove a restriction that later matters to an admission decision, so preserving origins does more than increase table occupancy. Yet the opportunities were sparse: 47 collision pairings across 36 installation events yielded only one changed complete batch. The parent and child each recorded 195 vetoes in total, showing why whole-run veto counts alone would have missed this activation. The newly available replacement was locally better and won its batch, but its subsequent walk ended worse. Immediate source or archive gains therefore do not establish useful long-term redirection, and the later loss cannot be treated as the isolated value of the excluded molecule. This narrows the result to coherent short-term provenance protection; it does not establish that shared local motifs identify reversal of an entire edit or that broader retention improves search. The molecular assessment also finds the inherited aromatic and ring-rich families, unusual sulfur bonding, reactive decorations and unspecified stereochemistry largely intact, with no demonstrated chemistry improvement explaining the redirection. The benefit under histories with more overlap-dependent candidates remains open. No obstruction release occurred, so behavior after a release was not tested.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace only the successful active count-GP predictive location with the pinned synthetic-only native-2048-count TabPFN-3.5 accepted-context regression mean, using eight fixed source feature permutations and every chronological accepted row; preserve the exact original count-GP correlated residual so active_values = external_raw_mean + original_score_scale * (original_normals @ original_count_factor.T), followed by the inherited sequential masks and first-index ties.
nodes.finding:
The native predictor operated in all 15 sessions, producing 435 nonconstant full-coordinate prediction pools. It changed 2,834 of 4,350 accepted choices; 775 of those changed sources later produced 2,510 accepted descendants. The substitution therefore reached both learning and breeding. On the same actual labels, however, pairwise ordering accuracy fell from the original GP’s 0.698242 to 0.657184, and mean batch Spearman fell from 0.505819 to 0.402270. Both ranking measures were worse in every early/middle/late phase, and no task/seed session improved both. Mean accepted score fell from 0.372050 to 0.323251. There were slightly more parent-beating offspring (654 versus 648), but their summed positive gain fell from 17.251535 to 14.377969 and sequential incumbent gain fell from 5.819415 to 4.683073. More productive alternative cores entered breeding, yet their descendants delivered less gain. The complete matched final-score mean was 0.520697 versus 0.596453, a change of −0.075756 against the required +0.002. Thirteen of fifteen endpoints declined; seed 1’s macro and two individual endpoints improved. Population standard deviation increased from 0.033970 to 0.058846. All runs completed within the issued resources without model warnings or fallback.

This result rules out absent model exposure, omitted count coordinates, lost accepted-context rows, altered residual draws and construction infeasibility as explanations for this recipe’s failure. Exact-source execution and richer native count input did not make the external predictor a better guide than the original GP on the selected molecular candidates. The extra local wins came against weaker parents, and greater scaffold breadth did not translate into larger useful gains. The chemistry audit helps explain why breadth is an inadequate proxy: some streams enlarged or repeated familiar fragments, while fewer direct N/O–halogen bonds coexisted with more sulfur–nitrogen connections and difficult ring topologies. Those output associations do not identify a chemical cause of the loss. The current exact-lock comparison supports a negative contribution from the whole fixed native-location recipe under this retained search composition; it cannot separate encoding, prior, preprocessing or hybrid-residual effects, diagnose the earlier projected recipe, or establish ranking-mediated causation. The registered complete adverse-result condition is met, so this fixed recipe stops. A checkpoint, width, permutation, precision, target-transform, blend or archive-window sweep is not a justified continuation.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace only the inherited GP covariance with the fixed normalized-count inner product K(x,y)=(x dot y)/(sqrt(sum(x*x))*sqrt(sum(y*y))) for nonzero raw inherited Morgan count rows, with empty/empty=1 and exactly one empty=0, coherently in every training, cross, pool and probe Gram block; preserve the complete correlated posterior-sampling allocator and all noncovariance interfaces.

The kernel changed real decisions: all 435 batch orders and 434 selected sets differed from the original same-state control, with 3,176 strict disagreements under the actual masks and 2,645 newly selected accepted identities. Independent replay reconstructs the coherent GP moments and correlated draws from the original saved normal arrays. On all 4,350 actual accepted offspring labels, active MSE was 0.027650 versus 0.007503 for passive original means; within-batch pair accuracy was 0.610626 versus 0.763745, and mean batch Spearman was 0.287213 versus 0.650562. All 15 task/seed cells were adverse on these three same-label measures. These estimates describe the delivered stream, not unscored candidates.

The complete endpoint mean fell from 0.596453 to 0.519226, a signed change of -0.077227; all three seed macros and 13 of 15 endpoint cells lost. Mean AUC fell from 0.470976 to 0.413188. Macro population SD decreased from 0.033970 to 0.029462, which does not meet the registered +0.002 mean-gain requirement. Strict best-generating-parent wins decreased from 648 to 637. Every task completed; there was no natural fallback, numerical retry, budget or sulfur-gate violation.

The changed geometry and delivered choices happened, but the predicted ranking and productive-exploration benefits did not. This rules out rescuing the tested fixed law with its lower dispersion or slightly higher scaffold-win counts under this composition and profile. New-core local wins arose from weaker absolute sources and did not turn into stronger actual continuation. Draw opportunity, supported-but-undrawn sources, sources drawn without accepted descendants, nonsurvivor fitting and terminal censoring are accounted for; their overlapping ancestry does not establish independent series or chemical mediation. The exact recipe ends after this complete exposed test.

The molecular assessment shows useful aryl, amide, carbonyl and cyclic/aliphatic-amine arrangements among leaders, alongside reactive attachments, difficult bridged rings, unspecified stereochemistry, destructive fragments and excessive concatenations. The inherited sulfur gate contains its specified sulfur signatures but does not solve these broader generation gaps. These associations help describe the weak delivered chemistry; they do not identify why the covariance lost utility. Proportional count directions mathematically alias and discard magnitude, but no unequal proportional-only rows or empty rows occurred naturally, and the seven equal-count distinct-identity alias records did not form accepted-stream alias groups. Alias-mediated failure therefore remains unproved. Pool-wide calibration, passive choice rewards and genealogy, constituent interactions, causal chemistry, other profiles/compositions and unevaluated foundation models remain open.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace only the conditional crossover-partner sampler with a certified deterministic minimum-count-Tanimoto transportation coupling of the original two-role joint law, preserving both original prospective role marginals and every original zero-pair restriction while retaining the exact first-parent sampler and distinct source identities.

The coupling worked as intended in all 435 encountered population states. At each fixed state it preserved each source’s original probability in both parent roles and every forbidden pair, while expected pair similarity fell from 0.7591 to 0.7029. Actual partner identity changed in 30,333 of 34,407 crossovers. Those changed pairs produced 1,277 accepted complete molecules; 683 later served as breeding sources. There were no solver fallbacks or incomplete evaluations. Nevertheless, final Top-1 macro mean fell from 0.59567 to 0.55854: a paired change of -0.03713, failing the registered +0.002 criterion. Six of fifteen task/seed cells improved and nine declined. Seed changes were -0.07451, +0.00075 and -0.03761. The largest losses were decoration hopping in seed 0 and the sitagliptin objective in seed 2. Seed dispersion fell from 0.02659 to 0.00544, which does not establish reliable improvement.

Preserving each role’s score exposure at a fixed population did not preserve the joint best-parent threshold or the quality of later adaptive populations. Expected best-parent score moved upward in 282 states and downward in 153 despite the fixed marginals. The Child recorded more parent-beating offspring (745 versus 629) and more incumbent advances (277 versus 258), but accepted offspring had lower absolute mean scores (0.37150 versus 0.38526), their actual best-parent references were weaker (0.44047 versus 0.47046), and positive incumbent increments were smaller on average (0.01896 versus 0.02251). Thus the extra local wins and reuse do not establish more productive exploration. Changed pairs did reach real complete products and feedback, so lack of downstream exposure does not explain the failed score prediction. The chemistry still spans many ring frameworks and includes recognizable aryl cyclic amines, alongside reactive attachments, questionable bridges and unresolved stereochemistry; the evidence does not identify any of these as the cause of the score loss. Lower count-feature similarity controls source dependence, but this fixed objective did not reliably produce better complete molecular arrangements under the tested conditions. nodes.hypothesis: Remove cross-candidate dependence from allocation residual draws by sampling independent Gaussian residuals with the Parent's unchanged jittered marginal variances, while retaining the fitted count-based joint posterior.

All 435 allocations remove analytic residual cross-covariance while preserving the original jittered marginal variances. Every sampled value and selected identity reconstructs. Replaying correlated draws on the same Child inputs changes 422 of 435 selected sets; thirteen sets coincide, and residuals still move 3,747 of 4,350 choices away from the available mean maximum. The isolated reverse control supports a positive contribution of correlated allocation residuals in the current exchange-free search, with substantial seed and task dependence. Independent draws do not guarantee diverse selections: on the same Child pools they raise mean absolute fitted-model correlation from 0.05063 to 0.05465 and slightly reduce nonempty typed and generic core counts. Strict local parent beats increase from 629 to 661 and incumbent gains from 258 to 273, yet the endpoint mean falls, so these local measures do not explain the benefit. Molecular evidence preserves compact conventional alternatives and some larger improving families alongside reactive bond environments, repeated large assemblies and destructive fragments; no single chemistry or size rule accounts for the score. Which adaptive choices mediate the benefit remains open. The earlier correlation-removal panel still lacks its timed-out seed-0 endpoint, and its two-seed gain under a different Parent and profile remains separate evidence. nodes.hypothesis: Replace binary Morgan-presence covariance with generalized Tanimoto covariance on integer counts of the same hashed local molecular environments, so the accepted-feedback Gaussian process conditions on environment multiplicity.
nodes.finding:
Environment multiplicity changed the similarity matrices and posterior distribution in all 435 fits. On identical archives and pools, 69,570 of 69,600 predicted means changed; replaying the same random draws changed 434 of 435 selected batches. The three-seed macro mean rose from 0.55177 to 0.57434, a gain of 0.02257 above the registered 0.002 minimum. Two seed means improved and one fell. Mean final scores rose for sitagliptin by 0.06213, median similarity by 0.02333, DRD2 by 0.02056 and decoration hopping by 0.00911, while zaleplon fell by 0.00228. On the Child's identical scored molecules, the count model reduced prediction MSE from a passive binary model's 0.011797 to 0.011269, about 4.5%, and raised mean within-batch rank correlation from 0.469 to 0.550. The archive-mean baseline MSE was 0.042504. However, mean latent interval width shrank from 0.263 to 0.168, and nominal 95% coverage fell from 85.6% to 76.9%; including observation noise only raised count-model coverage to 77.2%. This is evidence for better average prediction and search outcomes on this panel, alongside worse uncertainty coverage.

The useful change comes from reweighting ordinary similarity relationships, not from splitting exact fingerprint ties: the only binary-equivalent pair in the Child pools remained count-equivalent. Counts usually increased archive-to-pool similarity and reduced posterior uncertainty, but neither direction was universal. Their prediction advantage was much larger when passively applied to the Parent's selected stream than on their own selected stream, showing why historical prediction gains need to be checked after selection adapts. Sitagliptin supplies the largest score gain even though its paired MSE worsens and its latent intervals cover only one third of scored emissions. Improved mean prediction therefore does not fully explain the whole-search gain; the contribution of changed uncertainty to allocation remains open. Uncertainty calibration is now a concrete issue to probe separately.

The molecular assessment finds smaller families in several streams, yet oversized assemblies, unusual heteroatom bonds, constrained rings and unspecified stereochemistry remain. Counts preserve the same local environment vocabulary and many hashing collisions; they supply neither a demonstrated size penalty nor evidence of synthetic or geometric feasibility. These results establish count-sensitive posterior execution and utility on the supplied panel, while leaving broader chemical usefulness and transfer to other search distributions unresolved.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace the unrestricted connected-fragment crossover constructor with release-specific BRICS single-cut sampling on the two actual scored generating parents, retain the original 0.80 large-first/small-second orientation law, and construct exactly one SINGLE join only when the sampled retained endpoint labels are compatible in RDKit 2023.09.6 reactionDefs; absent cuts or incompatible draws return None through the unchanged bounded failed-crossover admission/refill path.

The typed construction executed correctly on all 43,402 crossover attempts. It made 26,677 valid immediate products, including 20,302 that differed from both parents; 968 typed-route final molecules were evaluated, 797 from distinct immediate recombinants and 171 from parent copies changed by finishing. All mapped raw contexts and permitted single joins checked correctly, and every pool and batch completed.

Release-defined cuts and intact raw source subgraphs create exposed, useful recombinants, but they did not increase productive gain under this optimizer. Yet their direct descendants supplied only 0.429 of sequential incumbent gain versus 0.975 for the Parent crossover cohort, and their transitive descendant unions supplied 2.924 versus 3.473. Local compatibility also leaves whole-molecule limitations unresolved. Finishing changed 429 of the 968 evaluated typed-route identities; only 693 retained an existential match to the entire immediate graph, and seven immediate joining bonds received different labels when re-perceived after sanitation. That is a coverage contrast, not proof that size, a specific attachment or the constructor caused that cell loss.

The matched result rejects the proposed gain benefit for this fixed recipe and satisfies its registered stopping condition. It supports a negative total contribution of this construction variant under these conditions; it does not decide whether crossover presence is beneficial, identify separate contributions of cleavage, compatibility, RNG history or finishing, or establish chemical mediation. nodes.hypothesis: Remove active stable-canonical pool normalization and rejection after the inherited graph checker, routing its original checked molecular object and raw returned identity through existing novelty, pool, emission and pending interfaces while retaining the original stable-admission helper only as a passive comparator.

The removal had a real admission effect. Among 75,958 checked Child attempts, one candidate had an alternating identity string that the Parent rejected. The Child admitted its original checked graph and raw key into the final docking pool. The candidate itself was never selected, emitted or scored, and its two spellings were not shown to be graph-equivalent. Its admission substituted one pool member and shifted 104 shared positions. With the same recorded random-normal draws and unchanged marginal predictions for shared candidates, the final allocation evaluated seven different molecules. Four of those new alternatives remained in the final population; none improved the incumbent. Fourteen of fifteen complete task/seed trajectories were identical.

An unselected pool member can still change which other molecules receive evaluations. Here the pool substitution and index shift changed the correlated allocation, so equal endpoints do not mean identical search behavior. This supplies current downstream exposure that the older two unselected stable aliases lacked. The zero endpoint effect is nevertheless narrow: the sole opportunity occurred in the last batch, after the existing best score was already reached. The changed labels did not train another model or seed further breeding.

The experiment does not establish that an unstable key is safe to emit. That boundary was never naturally exercised, and the missing-provenance guard still raises in an explicitly synthetic control using real archived feedback. Nor does admission removal establish better chemistry: the altered final choices include both a high-scoring halogen-free amine and retained reactive substituents, while the broader ring-geometry and stereochemical limitations remain. Earlier identity exposure, actual selection of an unstable representation and other parser conventions remain open. The observed component result does not establish universal dispensability or effects of combining sibling changes.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove optional post-crossover finishing mutation by setting its existing probability from 0.35 to 0.0 while retaining exactly one original gate draw after every successful ordinary crossover, so its immediate product reaches the unchanged admission pipeline without a finishing call; retain ordinary single-parent continuation and every other active Parent rule.

The separate roles of missing finishing products, altered admission and random streams, and later adaptive feedback remain unresolved. nodes.hypothesis: Replace the single fixed dot-product count-Tanimoto GP covariance with one per-fit exact-marginal-likelihood-selected convex blend K=(1-w)*T_DP+w*K_comp over the frozen grid w in {0, 0.125, 0.25, 0.5} by squared lengthscale in {17/4, 17}, where K_comp is a Gaussian kernel on a fixed seventeen-feature archive-standardized whole-molecule composition/property vector and w=0 reproduces the inherited kernel exactly, then use that one selected kernel coherently in every training, cross, pool and probe Gram block for both the posterior mean and the correlated residual covariance.
nodes.finding:
The likelihood wanted the new whole-molecule view almost everywhere: 431 of 435 refits gave it positive weight, and 304 picked the largest weight on the grid (0.5). Only four early refits, with 20 to 30 molecules in the archive, kept the Parent's kernel. The preference grew as the archive grew and was strongest on sitagliptin and zaleplon. Every refit and every batch reproduced exactly when recomputed independently. Breeding and random draws were untouched: the first batch's candidate pool and random numbers match the Parent's in all 15 sessions.

On the molecules it actually tested, the blended model predicted better than the Parent's kernel would have from the same state. Error fell by about a quarter (0.0077 to 0.0058). Within-batch rank correlation rose from 0.43 to 0.54, and pairwise order accuracy from 0.67 to 0.71. Most of the gain came where the Parent's model was weakest: sitagliptin rank correlation went from about 0.18 to 0.48, and zaleplon from 0.43 to 0.59. deco_hop and median_2 barely moved, and median_2 error rose slightly in all three seeds. The improvement is about half the size the pre-registered replay suggested.

It also changed which molecules got tested. Against the Parent's kernel on the identical pool and draws, it swapped about half of each batch in 428 of 435 batches. It picked larger molecules in 14 of 15 sessions (+2.3 heavy atoms on average, +5 to +7 on deco_hop), and its batches were more self-similar in 14 of 15. The size pull comes from uncertainty, not from predicted score: the blend adds extra posterior spread to molecules at the edge of the archive's composition range, and that extra spread rises with molecule size in every session (rank correlation 0.31 to 0.65).

Scores: the complete matched mean was 0.5834 against the Parent's 0.5965, a change of -0.0131, well short of the +0.002 goal. Seed changes were -0.045, +0.008 and -0.002, and only 5 of 15 task/seed cells improved. deco_hop fell on all three seeds (task mean -0.096). That includes missing the Parent's late 0.856 breakthrough on seed 0, which by itself costs 0.016 of the mean; the other 14 cells net +0.003. On deco_hop the Child's tested molecules averaged roughly 48 heavy atoms against the Parent's 32, reaching 71 in the last third of one session, while the best deco_hop molecules have about 28; oracle time rose 7 to 36 fold. zaleplon (+0.014), sitagliptin (+0.012) and median_2 (+0.005) rose slightly, but the sign differed between seeds. drd2 finished level but progressed more slowly early (area under the curve -0.042). The Child produced more offspring that beat their own parents (860 against 648) and more new incumbents (325 against 255), yet final scores were not higher.

Fitting the weight, rather than forcing it as the earlier equal-weight atom-pair channel did, shows that the labels clearly prefer a whole-molecule composition and property view. It does make the surrogate better on objectives that depend on global properties. But this is the fourth time in this lineage that better ranking of the tested molecules has failed to produce better endpoints. Marginal likelihood selects a kernel that fits the archive, not one that searches well, and that gap is now a pattern rather than an anecdote.

The failure has a specific, traceable route. A stationary Gaussian kernel on archive-standardized descriptors gives every compositionally novel molecule fresh prior variance. Under Thompson sampling that variance becomes a novelty bonus that scales with size, and the generator can grow molecules cheaply by appending atoms. Where the score band is narrow (deco_hop sits in 0.5 to 0.62), variance dominates the draw. The search then drifts toward big, repetitive molecules that the molecular review shows are not where the score is. This rules out implementation error, grid failure or numerical fallback as explanations.

The weight sat at the 0.5 grid edge on three tasks. Larger weights are untested, but given this mechanism they would more likely amplify the drift than fix it. The more informative next step is to separate the two roles: use the composition channel for the posterior mean and keep the Parent's local kernel for the sampled uncertainty, or otherwise stop composition novelty from earning exploration credit.

Still open: whether the small zaleplon and sitagliptin gains are real, given mixed seed signs and only three seeds. Also open: how much of the deco_hop loss is the Parent's one lucky late breakthrough rather than the size drift. All three deco_hop seeds and their areas under the curve are lower, which suggests the drift matters, but the attribution is associative. Among the four same-round variants on this Parent, all lost, and this was the smallest loss; those are dependent comparisons, not a ranking of ideas.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove only the selected first canonical identity exclusion from actual crossover-partner sampling, allowing ordinary self-pair draws under the original score-quantile band and member law while preserving all first-parent behavior and unchanged crossover, finishing and admission.
nodes.finding:
The removal ran as specified and lowered the complete mean from 0.595670 to 0.563677, a decrease of 0.031992 against the registered 0.002 scale. Ten of the 15 task/seed endpoints fell and five improved. Seed-macro changes were -0.092144, +0.012064 and -0.015897; macro dispersion also fell, from 0.026593 to 0.022045. The largest losses were the seed-0 deco-hop and sitagliptin endpoints, while the zaleplon task mean improved.

There were 2,851 actual self-pairs. They produced 359 immediate copies, 2,489 different graphs and three construction failures. Finishing changed 135 copies into different final identities; 224 remained rejected copies. The self channel reached 2,454 fresh pool entries and 155 real evaluations, including 27 parent wins and 14 incumbent advances. Eighty-seven accepted self products later bred, and 41 had accepted children. Separately, replay from identical sampler states found 6,283 changed choices among nonself partners, which reached 346 accepted evaluations. All 15 full cells had evaluated self products, but 310 individual batches had self draws without a self evaluation; these zeros and terminally censored products remain in the comparison.

Enforcing distinct source identities contributes positively under this complete method and evaluation profile, even though self recombination can produce useful, subsequently reused molecules. The tested contribution includes both permitting self-pairs and redistributing probability among other partners, followed by their different random draws and feedback histories. These data do not separate those channels or establish a diversity mechanism.

The extra local wins are especially informative: total parent wins rose from 629 to 673 and incumbent advances from 258 to 265, yet mean accepted-offspring score fell from 0.385256 to 0.371429 and mean best-parent score from 0.470456 to 0.448955. The advances were more numerous but added less total improvement. Thus easier parent comparisons and lower dispersion can accompany weaker endpoints. The molecular assessment also finds different leading aromatic families across seeds alongside recurring questionable attachments and unspecified stereochemistry; those concerns persist in the Parent and do not identify the exclusion rule as their cause. Individual channel contributions, chemical mediation and reliability beyond the measured panel remain unresolved. This result answers the distinct-partner boundary within the retained foundation, without attributing an entire foundation or combining sibling effects.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove only connected-fragment crossover m-00000000000a from sulfur-gated Parent n-1744a1494180 by setting its effective probability to zero, retaining the original pre-branch random draw and routing every attempted proposal through the inherited ordinary single-parent mutation path with unchanged sampled continuation, higher-floor escalation and downstream admission, posterior allocation and accepted-feedback rules.
nodes.finding:
All 73,814 generation attempts used one scored parent and mutation, despite 33,358 natural opportunities for the original crossover rule. Every session was exposed. All 435 pools reached 160 members and all 4,350 emitted optimizer proposals were accepted; the sulfur, canonical-identity, posterior-choice and accepted-feedback audits reconciled.

The matched mean fell from 0.596453 to 0.552813, a loss of 0.043640 against the registered 0.002 scale. Seed macro differences were -0.103844, -0.001329 and -0.025747. Nine of fifteen task/seed endpoints fell and six improved; four task means fell while median_2 rose by 0.001594. Population macro deviation fell from 0.033970 to 0.009762. Strict parent beats increased from 648 to 750 and sequential incumbent updates from 255 to 302, but mean positive parent-beating gain fell from 0.026623 to 0.021520 and total sequential gain across sessions fell from 5.819415 to 5.164818. The separate endpoint-gain requirement remains unmet.

Ordinary connected-fragment crossover has a positive conditional presence contribution on this sulfur-gated composition at the supplied descriptive scale. More local wins are insufficient evidence that the one-parent route substitutes for it: that route faces one parent rather than the crossover better-of-two hurdle, and its mean generating-parent hurdle was lower (0.419758 versus 0.455304 across the accepted streams). Gains were more frequent but smaller. Excluding the inherited decoration-hopping breakthrough cell only as a sensitivity check still leaves a mean loss of 0.029484, so that single cell is not the sole explanation. Two median_2 Child trajectories are byte-identical to earlier removal runs and add no independent historical realizations. This answers the new composition-specific presence question without changing the earlier controls or establishing transfer beyond these seeds.

Structural coverage also gives a mixed picture. Within-session typed core totals rose slightly from 1,847 to 1,867, while generic topology totals fell from 1,147 to 1,005; more accepted offspring were later drawn for breeding, yet accepted ancestry contained fewer descendant/source pairs. The Molecular assessment finds ring-rich output confined to 22-46 heavy atoms instead of the Parent 1-96 range, with no tiny fragments, but reactive attachments, difficult ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry persist. These are observed output differences, not an identified explanation for the score loss. The result measures the whole adaptive rerouting effect, including changed graph RNG, pools, ancestry and future posterior inputs. Specific fragment value, BRICS compatibility, finishing, sulfur interaction and the mechanism of the endpoint loss remain open; higher-floor and numerical recovery were not naturally exercised.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove only active influence of composite posterior selector m-000000000005 at the successful full-pool allocation consumer: emit the first announced-batch-size valid unique sulfur-gate-admitted members in inherited generation order, retaining the entire inherited fresh pool and original accepted-only count-GP fitting, covariance, factorization and normal draws as passive computations, with inherited numerical-failure routing unchanged.
nodes.finding:
All fifteen matched task/seed runs completed with the full budget. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.596453 to 0.468270, a paired loss of 0.128183. All three seed averages fell, by 0.20602, 0.07253 and 0.10599. Fourteen endpoints fell; the sole gain was zaleplon seed 1, from 0.474117 to 0.479919. The control emitted exactly the first ten admitted molecules from every one of 435 complete 160-member pools. The passive original selector chose a different set in every batch and strictly preferred another identity in 4321 of 4350 same-mask selections. There were no natural fallback, incomplete-pool or factorization failures. The entire original GP computation and sulfur rule remained present.

The control produced 634 parent-beating offspring versus 648, but only 155 sequential incumbent advances versus 255. Its average offspring score was 0.22594 versus 0.37205, and average best-generating-parent score 0.31170 versus 0.45530. It created more new typed/generic cores (2366/1815 versus 1820/1117), including more new parent-beating cores (325/229 versus 262/163). Fewer accepted sources later entered breeding (2038 versus 2469). Final-batch sources were censored for later reuse. Prospective prediction accuracy on the control's own accepted stream was better: unequal-label pair accuracy 0.771 versus 0.710 and mean within-batch Spearman 0.666 versus 0.526. Those are different selected streams; at the same actual identity the passive original mean is unchanged and its MSE contrast is zero.

The joint posterior allocation still contributes substantially after sulfur admission changes the available pool and later ancestry. This is now measured under the current gated conditions, with exposure in every task and seed; the earlier ungated loss alone could not establish that. More novel cores, more new parent-beating cores and easier selected-stream prediction did not preserve absolute source quality or incumbent improvement. This rules out treating those local proxies, or the narrower seed-average dispersion, as sufficient evidence of useful exploration. The result concerns the whole successful allocation consumer and its total adaptive effect. It does not isolate a mean, fingerprint, normalization or residual constituent, show a sulfur interaction, or attribute the whole graph foundation.

Chemistry remains mixed. Fewer N-halogen structures coexist with more O-halogen and peroxide structures, while useful conventional ether/ketone and methoxy alternatives and useful permitted sulfur remain. Some of the highest labels still belong to chemically doubtful output, including the cyclic-peroxide family in the sole improving endpoint. Those examples preserve exceptions without proving a chemical mediator, a universal liability penalty or a benefit from broader filtering. Passive alternatives have no new labels or continued ancestry. Current composition review, separate constituent and joint-interaction evidence, chemical mediation, partial alternative-lineage composition and full-history coverage remain open.

nodes.hypothesis: Prioritize a selected transition's globally changed motifs whose signed occurrence changes are supported among the atoms and bond endpoints directly edited by that transition, using this binary site-support priority ahead of the Parent's existing rank within its unchanged bounded sign-balanced inverse-motif installation.
nodes.finding:
On the same 435 selected transitions, the number of installed memory slots supported by a same-sign change at directly edited roots rose from 884 to 1,257 of 1,708 slots, or 51.76% to 73.59%. Retained keys changed at 236 installations; another 64 changed order only. Separate memory histories on the recorded Child walk produced 184 vetoes with the inherited ranking and 117 with site priority: 74 decisions became admissions and seven became additional vetoes. These changes reached 80 actually evaluated molecules across 67 batches, comprising 74 new admissions and six replacement evaluations. Twelve of those molecules improved their source, 68 worsened it, 11 became selected walk states and five improved the archive. All 435 selected-edit replays verified, with no runtime fallback. The three-seed macro mean was 0.520690, compared with 0.521759 for the Parent; the paired change was -0.001069, missing the required +0.002. Two seeds declined and one improved. Mean endpoints improved on four tasks, but the sitagliptin decrease of 0.022009 outweighed those gains, including the DRD2 increase of 0.011290.

Direct edit provenance can redirect scarce memory slots and real evaluations. The unresolved issue is whether the resulting motif restrictions protect useful search behavior. Of the 373 keys added by site priority, 230 later matched a fresh molecule and 60 participated in a bidirectional veto; 105 of the 314 that expired had never matched. Full-stream source improvements increased from 468 to 475 and archive improvements from 238 to 254, while their mean positive gains fell from 0.024350 to 0.022872 and from 0.019744 to 0.018437, respectively. More locally supported credit and more small improvements therefore did not establish the registered panel benefit. A newly admitted sulfur-free aryl-amine molecule reached the DRD2 maximum of 0.949238, showing that useful conventional chemistry was accessible. The molecular assessment still finds reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur, dense ring systems and undefined stereochemistry elsewhere, especially in the weaker sitagliptin outcome. Root provenance is not a chemical-quality test, and a later shared motif does not demonstrate reversal of the same physical site. The records identify 590 later scored descendants of the 11 changed selected states, but they cannot assign those descendant scores to one credited motif or supply the missing scores and proposals of an alternative walk.

nodes.hypothesis: Modify only successful fresh-pool allocation’s predictive location to active_location=0.5*original_count_GP_raw_mean+0.5*frozen_MoLFormer_angular_feature_GP_raw_mean, where the auxiliary GP fits chronological current-Objective accepted labels on unit-normalized masked-mean final-state embeddings of the complete canonical nonisomeric molecular view from the pinned official MoLFormer-XL-both-10pct compat-v4 checkpoint; retain the EXACT original full-count GP score_scale*(original_normals@original_pool_factor.T) correlated residual and inherited masks and first-index ties, with explicit original-count location fallback only for unsupported encoder rows.
nodes.finding:
The frozen molecular encoder and equal raw-mean blend executed in all 15 task/seed sessions. Every one of the 69,600 fresh-pool rows and 4,350 accepted offspring was supported; there were no unsupported-row or numerical batch fallbacks. The location changed 2,368 of 4,350 accepted choices under the same saved count residuals and actual masks. Of those changed choices, 2,282 reached both learners at the next fit and 86 were in the terminal batch. On the same prospective accepted labels, active pair-order accuracy fell from 0.670954 for the original count mean to 0.669109, and mean within-batch Spearman fell from 0.436926 to 0.428857. The auxiliary mean alone was weaker at 0.618377 and 0.311806. Active MSE rose from 0.006501 to 0.006680. Compared with the code Parent, mean accepted-offspring score fell from 0.372050 to 0.334941. Strict best-parent wins increased from 648 to 700, but their summed positive margins fell from 17.251535 to 12.579418, and summed sequential incumbent gain fell from 5.819415 to 4.797752. The complete matched three-seed macro mean fell from 0.596453 to 0.528342, a delta of -0.068111 against the registered +0.002 goal. All three seed macros fell (-0.094788, -0.027975 and -0.081569), and 10 of the 15 task/seed endpoints fell. Mean endpoint changes were -0.010466 on zaleplon, -0.096673 on deco hop, -0.001594 on docking, +0.003991 on median, and -0.235812 on sitagliptin. Macro dispersion decreased from 0.033970 to 0.019708. This is confirmed allocation activation with failed ordering, productive-progress and performance predictions.

This fixed recipe was fully exposed, so its loss cannot be attributed to a missing checkpoint, a silent count-only substitute, an incomplete panel or an untested allocation change. Both registered ranking aggregates decline, and the decline is larger among changed choices. Better local-win counts and more productive new cores did not produce stronger absolute progress: breeding-source scores were lower, positive improvement magnitudes shrank, and gains arrived later. The early-budget cumulative gain was 1.953179 versus 3.602660 for the Parent; some middle-budget recovery did not restore the endpoints. The chemistry assessment shows moderate diversity and some ordinary aromatic amides and diaryl amines, alongside larger linked heterocycles, reactive attachments and dense cages. The larger deco-hop family did not recover the Parent’s compact late high-label arrangement, and fewer N-halogen structures in the sitagliptin family still accompanied a large endpoint loss. Extra cores or fewer suspect local motifs therefore do not establish useful independent chemical alternatives or chemical repair. Those associations do not identify why the predictor or endpoint changed. The result supports negative contribution of this one fixed encoder-view, pooling, angular-GP and equal-blend combination on the inherited sulfur-gated count search. It does not isolate the encoder, pooling, feature kernel, mixing coefficient or location/residual interaction, and it does not reject molecular pretraining generally. Unselected reference alternatives have no counterfactual labels or continuations, so ranking-to-score mediation remains open. Natural inference included 107 complete pool views above the 202-token pretraining cutoff, including one accepted 220-token view; that establishes full-view exposure, not benefit on long molecules. Unsupported-row and failure routing passed construction checks but had no natural exposure. The small raw pooling tolerance exception is retained, while the normalized GP embeddings passed the registered checks. This completes the fixed recipe’s exposed test and supplies evidence for review without a result-driven rescue sweep.
