nodes.hypothesis: Within the inherited selected score band, sample a crossover partner with probability proportional to its accepted-molecule fingerprint Tanimoto similarity to the already selected first parent.
nodes.finding:
The intended pairing mechanism changed actual breeding. Of 34,123 partner draws, 33,350 had unequal similarities and used the registered weights; 7,967 choices (23.35%) differed from the passive uniform choice on the same eligible partners and random variate. On nondegenerate states, expected Tanimoto similarity rose from 0.48313 under uniform selection to 0.51979 under the applied law. Actual mean pair similarity rose from the Parent's 0.48309 to 0.51650. The first-parent rule, greedy survival, graph operators and posterior selection remained unchanged. Both runs evaluated 1,679 crossover and 2,671 mutation offspring. Crossover best-parent beats rose from 172 to 176 and sequential incumbent improvements from 75 to 84. Its mean parent-relative deficit narrowed from -0.15687 to -0.13737, but the mean best generating-parent score also fell from 0.43361 to 0.40325, and absolute crossover-offspring score fell from 0.27674 to 0.26587. Raw invalid crossover attempts increased from 123 to 326. Mutation incumbent improvements fell from 143 to 130, leaving fewer total improvements (214 versus 218). The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.54437 to 0.52840, a paired change of -0.01597; seed changes were -0.00054, -0.06139 and +0.01401. All five task means declined, with the largest mean loss on sitagliptin (-0.06334). Every formal task still completed its full evaluation budget.

The experiment separates selecting related molecules from obtaining more productive chemistry. Similarity enrichment and changed pairings are established, but the smaller parent-relative deficit partly accompanies a weaker reference parent and does not demonstrate stronger absolute offspring. Crossover contributed more local incumbent gains while the inherited mutation stream contributed fewer; mutation is not an unaffected control because new pairings change the accepted population and subsequent random trajectory. Much of the final-score loss came from the second seed's sitagliptin run, so this panel supports negative mean transfer rather than a universal failure of related-parent crossover. Fingerprint relatedness also did not preserve a common core more often: the share of evaluated crossover offspring reusing a generating parent's core fell from 34.25% to 33.00%, while survivor core coverage broadened. The molecular assessment still found repeated large assemblies, reactive halogen connections and strained rings; larger repeated products often offered little score separation from smaller relatives. Thus shared fingerprint features alone did not ensure that the unchanged fragment crossover preserved useful attachment relationships or chemical scale. The conditional-law comparison establishes allocation, but supplies no score for an unchosen partner and no causal attribution for either member of a pair.

nodes.hypothesis: Install and refresh inverse-motif restrictions only when the selected actually accepted neighbor has a strictly higher score than its recorded source; tied and worsening selected transitions still move and age the walk but receive no new memory credit.
nodes.finding:
All 184 tied or worsening selected moves skipped memory installation, omitting 719 attributes while retaining 984 attributes from improving moves. On the Child's recorded history, unconditional credit would veto 188 novel draws; the actual gate vetoed 115. This admitted 74 candidates across all fifteen task sessions, while preserved older provenance caused one additional veto in the opposite direction. Twenty newly admitted candidates became next states. Fourteen improved their source score, thirteen tied and forty-seven worsened it; only two immediately improved the archive. The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.501486, a paired change of -0.020273, against the registered requirement of +0.002. Two seeds declined and one improved. Task means improved for zaleplon and median_2, but declined for deco_hop, DRD2 and sitagliptin, with the largest loss in DRD2. All runs completed their full budgets and batches.

The experiment establishes that protecting nonimproving moves can block useful fresh variations: newly admitted methyl removal and aryl-fluorine removal both produced immediate archive gains. It also rules out an unexercised gate, missing feedback or changed restriction tenure as explanations for the negative panel result. Those useful cases were sparse, and overall source-improvement frequency and positive-gain magnitude fell. The archive improved slightly more often, but its total improvement was smaller. This narrows the question to the search value of the restrictions: withholding credit based on one move's local gain does not reliably identify protection that is expendable on this panel. Whether protecting nonimproving moves helps diversification remains unresolved because the passive comparison cannot reproduce an alternative walk or score excluded candidates. Preserved overlap provenance matters in practice: an older improving pair survived a skipped refresh and blocked a candidate that unconditional credit would admit. Thus the gate does not create a universal admissibility superset. The supplied molecular assessment still finds reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur connections and dense ring systems alongside recognizable aromatic/carbonyl and amine families; the changed allocation supplies no evidence that chemical feasibility improved.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace the inherited score-quantile preference with uniform draws over every eligible member of the current live score-greedy survivor population, retaining the original band construction and band-choice draw passively, the existing member-choice call and partner-exclusion fallback, recursive accepted-offspring breeding, and active accepted-label count-GP allocation.
nodes.finding:
All 106,858 Child breeding draws followed the uniform law over eligible current survivors, including partner exclusion. 53,199 draws used ranks that the inherited score bands could never choose, and 92,549 lay outside the passively drawn band. Mean selected topness was 0.500066, close to the exclusion-conditioned uniform expectation of 0.499988, versus 0.884073 under the original law on those same states. Accepted offspring continued to enter survivors and breed: 3,254 distinct offspring were later used, versus 2,401 for the Parent. All 435 accepted-label count-GP fits and full candidate pools remained active on each side.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.549672, a paired change of -0.045998, exceeding the registered 0.002 loss scale. Seed macro changes were -0.063415, -0.038977 and -0.035602. Thirteen of fifteen task-seed endpoints and all five task means declined. The two exceptions were zaleplon seed 0 (+0.010604) and seed 2 (+0.020822); its seed 1 lost 0.059613. Seed-macro population deviation fell from 0.026593 to 0.019687. All three replicas completed without fallback or missing endpoints.

This establishes positive conditional contribution of the inherited score-quantile preference while recursive feedback, greedy survival and the predictive selector remain active. It does not separate the value of restricting support from the value of weighting supported ranks. It also does not repeat the earlier fixed-initial-parent experiment or settle the value of the whole graph-evolution foundation.

The contrast separates participation from productive progress. Previously unsupported parents contributed to 1,427 evaluated offspring, of which 928 later bred. Yet strict generating-parent beats increased from 629 to 1,055 against weaker sources, while sequential incumbent gains fell from 258 to 203. Predictions also had lower error and higher within-batch ordering correlation on the changed evaluated distribution, despite worse endpoints. None of these selected associations establishes a causal mediator or a transferable surrogate-quality gain.

The molecular assessment finds recognizable biaryl amines and useful aromatic/carbonyl combinations alongside inherited reactive bonds, crowded rings and unspecified stereochemistry. The halogen-free carboxamide improvement and a strong carbon-bound-fluorine leader prevent treating unusual bonds or blanket chemical exclusions as the explanation. Broader parent participation therefore did not resolve chemical feasibility or ensure better endpoint search. Terminal admissions and unselected alternatives provide no unobserved descendant outcomes.

nodes.hypothesis: Add the exact archived mean-fantasy within-batch residual projection to the exchange-disabled Parent: condition future sampled residual rows on each earlier selected molecule taking its unchanged posterior mean, using the original jittered sampling covariance and zero innovations only for batch allocation.
nodes.finding:
All 3,915 projections executed correctly and preserved every first choice. They changed 657 later positions and 295 of 435 batch sets, replacing 493 selected memberships. Later selected sampling variance fell by 3.28% on average. These choices entered real feedback: all 482 nonterminal newly selected molecules entered later fits, and 296 of the 493 new selections later bred. Yet the final mean fell from 0.595670 to 0.553927, a paired loss of 0.041742 against the required gain of 0.002. All three seed macros fell; six task/seed endpoints improved and nine declined. Strict parent wins rose from 629 to 642, while absolute offspring mean fell from 0.385256 to 0.359834 and total incumbent improvement fell from 5.807663 to 5.181529. The largest endpoint losses were deco_hop in seed 0 and sitagliptin_mpo in seed 2; median_2 improved in two seeds but fell in the third.

The result rules out nonactivation, missing accepted feedback or numerical fallback as explanations for the failed endpoint prediction. Lower average model correlation, selected-stream prediction error and seed dispersion were insufficient to improve search. The slightly larger count of parent wins partly accompanies weaker generating parents, so it does not establish higher absolute quality. Downstream opportunity also had limits: three newly selected nonterminal molecules had positive breeding support but were never drawn; four task/seed cohorts of new selections produced no positive direct-descendant incumbent increment, while terminal selections had no later opportunity. The earlier trial under an exchange-containing Parent was also adverse; this complete loss ends the registered fixed transfer without parameter rescue. The molecular assessment still finds chemically varied aromatic and heterocyclic outputs, alongside reactive halogen bonds, difficult ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry. Those liabilities and inconsistent useful family coverage remain relevant gaps, but these data do not identify chemical mediation, an exchange interaction or the contribution of the retained graph-evolution foundation.

nodes.hypothesis: Extend the existing change_atom neighborhood with a direct two-site exchange of a neutral aromatic nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon in the same six-member ring, producing formula-preserving nitrogen positional isomers without an evaluated single-substitution intermediate.
nodes.finding:
Ten fresh formula-preserving nitrogen positional isomers reached evaluation from thirteen sampled exchanges. All ten changed local signed motifs; three improved their source score and seven worsened it, with no ties. Three became subsequent walk states and one immediately improved the best archive. Every sampled exchange preserved atom count, bonds, molecular formula and qualifying-ring aromaticity. The three-seed macro mean rose from 0.520918 to 0.521759, a paired gain of 0.000841, below the required 0.002. One seed improved, one declined slightly and one was unchanged. The largest task change was deco_hop in the improving seed; DRD2 and sitagliptin endpoints were unchanged in all seeds.

The neighborhood extension is demonstrably usable: the ten evaluated products cannot be reached by any single legacy element substitution from their recorded sources. Unlike the earlier configuration-only experiment, nitrogen relocation changes both the motifs seen by tabu memory and the measured source scores. This rules out identity-only or score-invisible activation as the explanation for the limited panel benefit. Exposure is sparse and local outcomes are mixed: only ten of 4350 evaluated neighbors are exchanges, and most lose to their source. One selected deco_hop exchange leads into later archive improvements, but the whole walk and its random draws also change, so those later gains cannot be assigned to nitrogen placement alone. The evidence supports positional-isomer accessibility and score sensitivity, while the preregistered overall score benefit is refuted for this panel. The molecular assessment still finds the Parent-like aromatic/carbonyl families alongside reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur and dense cages; formula conservation by itself has not established better medicinal or synthetic quality.

nodes.hypothesis: Within each existing direct-policy sampling call, admit at most the first valid canonically novel molecule for each successfully extracted nonempty atom/bond-typed nonisomeric Murcko scaffold, resetting the scaffold allowance at the next refill call and leaving acyclic or extraction-fallback identities under inherited admission.
nodes.finding:
The admission mechanism executed correctly in all 497 sampling calls. It rejected 459 otherwise novel repeat-core draws before capacity and produced no repeated ring core within a call; the parent emitted 460 such repetitions. Against equal-sized choices from the same actual draws, 154 calls gained a total of 264 family slots: 259 ring-core appearances and five acyclic singleton appearances. Every added family reached evaluation, and six of those molecules improved the incumbent. Across complete runs, distinct evaluated ring cores increased from 2,813 to 3,079, while the largest occupancy of one core in a session fell from 160 molecules to 44. Total strict incumbent improvements nevertheless fell from 149 to 120.

The three-seed mean final score decreased from 0.522705 to 0.508379, a paired change of −0.014326 against the required +0.002 benefit. Seed changes were +0.002392, −0.018880 and −0.026492. All five task means declined, although the DRD2 endpoint difference was only about two millionths near the score ceiling. Recorded mean AUC increased from 0.405593 to 0.427858; about 94% of that aggregate increase came from DRD2, mainly its much earlier progress in seed 2. All fifteen sessions completed their budgets. Batches needing refills increased from 16 to 33, and measured generation time increased from 24.75 to 37.02 seconds. The utility falsifier is triggered; the verified admission mechanism remains confirmed.

This resolves the earlier uncertainty about whether protected alternatives ever reach useful downstream opportunities. Here, all 264 locally added families were scored, and 111 of their molecules entered fitting, making 212 training appearances, including 101 historical replay appearances. Direct admission therefore carried diversification through evaluation and learning. That propagation was insufficient for a final-score benefit. The 337 calls without a quota opportunity reproduced their local no-quota choices exactly, and paired behavior agreed through the first intervention in every session, narrowing the change to admission and the subsequent feedback it altered.

The result supports a tradeoff between early progress and later refinement. The parent obtained fifteen actual incumbent gains from repeated-core analogues, while the child gained only six incumbents from its locally added families. These are observations from separate completed trajectories, so they cannot price the child’s unscored rejected molecules or establish that those particular rejections caused the endpoint loss. The chemical assessment helps explain why counting cores is insufficient: productive attachment positions and combinations of peripheral groups remained uneven despite broader ring coverage. The number of evaluated molecules with potential tetrahedral centres rose from 846 to 1,145, with no assigned configurations in either cohort; the quota supplied neither configuration control nor a guarantee of preserving useful functional roles.

The open question is whether broader early coverage can coexist with sufficient sampling of productive peripheral analogues to retain late improvements. The AUC gain makes that distinction worth testing, while the lower final score rules out treating increased family coverage alone as evidence of better search.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove descending-score priority from historical replay membership by uniformly sampling the inherited number of eligible original accepted elites without replacement, using the already-consumed session draw and sorting its selected indices into inherited memory order, while retaining score-ranked memory retention, inverse-exposure historical weighting and individual target ceilings.
nodes.finding:
Uniform selection changed the historical identity subset in all 405 nonterminal updates with surplus eligible records. It replaced 1,705 historical row appearances relative to ranked selection on the same states. Every changed subset had lower mean accepted reward than the strongest available subset, and every one changed the weighted gradient direction after clipping, beyond the measured padding discrepancy. The 15 no-surplus controls had exactly zero selection-gradient difference. All 450 real first backward passes matched the actual training objective exactly and produced parameter movement.

Summing distinct replayed identities separately within each task and seed, coverage rose from 525 to 1,023. Mean previous fitting count fell from 4.529 to 1.930, while mean accepted replay reward fell from 0.360292 to 0.286586. On the child's own states, a passive score-ranked selection would have mean reward 0.376524: its 0.089938 advantage establishes the immediate loss of reward enrichment without pretending that this comparator is a separately trained policy.

All fifteen task sessions completed their budgets. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.522705 to 0.499302, a paired change of -0.023403, exceeding the allowed loss of 0.002. Seed changes were -0.012824, -0.008929 and -0.048456; population standard deviation fell from 0.020072 to 0.006326 around the lower mean. Task means changed by +0.007883 for zaleplon, -0.026559 for deco-hop, -0.002636 for docking, -0.000532 for median similarity and -0.095172 for sitagliptin. The losses in deco-hop and sitagliptin occurred in every seed. Mean recorded AUC nevertheless rose from 0.405593 to 0.417991. The endpoint non-inferiority prediction is therefore rejected even though selection and learning activation are confirmed.

Raw duplicate draws fell from 32.21% to 22.56%, and batches needing extra sampling fell from 16 to one. Raw validity fell from 91.79% to 90.15%, but all 4,350 submitted proposals in each panel were accepted as valid and novel. Distinct nonempty molecular cores increased from 2,813 to 2,889. Among the 4,200 accepted molecules following historical updates, strict incumbent improvements fell from 135 to 87; the number sharing a core with the immediately selected history fell from 44 to 11. These are observed molecular outcomes, with initialization and terminal learning kept outside that comparison.

Score priority still contributes to final performance in the combination with exposure weighting and target ceilings. Broader reuse, fewer duplicate draws, broader core coverage and higher average AUC did not make it dispensable. Matching loaded priors and exact behavior through the first 30 accepted observations in every session narrow the intervention to the changed historical subsets. The experiment removes selection priority while preserving score-biased admission and retention; it does not establish that historical replay itself is necessary or unnecessary. The original comparison with current-only learning still has only one paired seed.

Keeping the historical loss share at one half did not keep historical influence constant. The less frequently practiced history began much further from its fixed targets: mean historical squared residual increased from 3.252 to 25.281, and the mean normalized historical-only gradient norm rose from 42.83 to 432.30 on the resulting trajectories. Historical residuals worsened on fewer rows during fitting, 303 instead of 905, yet endpoint performance deteriorated. This narrows a plausible explanation to spending more learning effort on weaker, less practiced history; neither residual improvement nor a fixed coefficient share proves useful preservation. The passive ranked comparator also has a lower previous fitting count than actual uniform history on the child's states, 1.642 versus 1.930, illustrating why a local comparator cannot stand in for the count state of a separately evolved parent.

The molecular assessment explains why additional cores are an incomplete success criterion. The output remains rich in medicinal rings and polar linkers, but broader coverage did not reliably preserve the stronger combinations of compact shape and polar-group arrangement seen in the parent. Oversized growth, unusual attachment chemistry and absent stereochemical definition remain. Those associations do not identify a universal missing functional group or prove the cause of a score change. The remaining question is how to retain useful exploration while preserving replay's reward enrichment; this panel does not identify a replacement selection rule.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace raw accepted-score regression targets inside the retained count-GP selector with deterministic standard-normal midrank targets, preserving exact score ties and applying the inherited centering and population-SD normalization, while all search-state updates and endpoints continue to use real raw scores.
nodes.finding:
The exact tie-preserving map changes all 435 fitted target vectors and all 435 selected sets. All latent models, raw-reference controls and raw-feedback joins reconstruct; normalized covariance and original random draws remain unchanged on identical inputs. Yet mean within-batch ordering correlation falls from the raw reference’s 0.484299 to 0.443166 on the same scored molecules. Mean raw endpoint falls from 0.595670 to 0.574603, a loss of 0.021067 instead of the required 0.002 gain. Seed macro changes are -0.043227, +0.022366 and -0.042341. Six task-seed endpoints improve and nine decline; all three median_2 endpoints improve. Macro dispersion decreases from 0.026593 to 0.011472. Every evaluation completes.

The missing benefit is not explained by an unexposed transformation or unchanged choices: ordinal targets alter the entire panel, but their registered ordering advantage fails. Preserving observed label order is insufficient to preserve useful cardinal spacing or improve prediction on newly selected molecules. Even so, all three median_2 endpoints improve while their ordering correlations worsen, and raw parent beats and incumbent gains rise from 629/258 to 655/272 despite the lower overall endpoint mean. Those counterexamples prevent treating ordering correlation or local gains as complete explanations of search utility. Six distinct-molecule pool pairs still share both folded and native count vectors. Conventional aryl amines and carbonyl families remain useful alongside reactive bonds, complex rings and unspecified stereochemistry; target remapping does not repair those chemistry or identity limits. Latent uncertainty has no established raw-score calibration, and no raw-unit error or coverage proxy is substituted. This is a negative result for the rank-target increment on this composition, while the earlier positive evidence for the composite selector remains intact; the role of lost cardinal gaps and later adaptive paths is unresolved.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove cross-candidate dependence from allocation residual draws by sampling independent Gaussian residuals with the Parent's unchanged jittered marginal variances, while retaining the fitted count-based joint posterior.
nodes.finding:
Allocation cross-covariance was removed in all 426 recorded child batches while each jittered marginal variance was preserved. All recorded draws and all 4,260 masked winners reconstruct from the original normals. Replaying correlated draws on the same child pools changes 1,962 selection positions and 411 of 426 batch sets. The other fifteen sets coincide despite changed draw values; they are downstream non-effects, not failed covariance removal. Initial pools, predicted means, raw standard deviations and normal arrays match the parent exactly in all fifteen sessions.

Fourteen task runs finished. Deco-hop seed 0 timed out after 210 of 300 evaluations, so that seed has no final macro score and the full three-seed non-inferiority test cannot be decided. The two complete seeds improve by +0.011662 and +0.013814: their mean final Top-1 is 0.580592 versus 0.567854 for the same parent seeds. These two successful replicas cannot replace the missing result; the incomplete seed already loses 0.084067 on its completed sitagliptin task. Across the fourteen completed task pairs, mean recorded AUC falls from 0.474455 to 0.441510.

In matched available evaluation windows containing 4,260 scored offspring per panel, strict beats of the best generating parent rise from 615 to 690, and incumbent improvements rise from 238 to 272. Mean offspring-minus-best-parent score is still negative, changing from -0.085277 to -0.072497. The session-averaged accepted batch maximum falls from 0.487030 to 0.456226. Distinct nonempty cores fall from 1,778 to 1,711, while the largest core occupies an average 61.3% of each session's top ten proposals, versus 57.3% before. Prediction MSE falls from 0.011505 to 0.009159, but nominal 95% latent-interval coverage also falls, from 76.74% to 74.20%. These describe changed evaluated streams, not repaired calibration or scores for unselected alternatives.

Small average model correlations can still have a large effect on who wins a sampled maximum. All recorded pools offered a covariance-removal opportunity, and almost every batch set changed even though every candidate retained the same fitted mean and sampled marginal variance on fixed inputs. Removing stochastic dependence also did not make the selected chemistry independent: on the child's same pools, actual selected-pair absolute model correlation is 0.05568 versus 0.05137 under correlated replay, and mean nonempty core coverage is 6.64 versus 6.77. Independence of allocation noise is therefore neither a scaffold-diversity constraint nor removal of the fitted joint model.

The completed seeds leave the narrower dependence-removal hypothesis plausible, but the timeout and mixed task outcomes prevent calling dependence dispensable. The retained full factorization succeeds at its first jitter in every recorded batch. The timed-out stream ends after a complete allocation and emission, with ten externally scored molecules lacking candidate feedback. Its measured fitting time is only 0.46 seconds across twenty fits; the records do not isolate the source of the long task wall time. The parent already needed about 3,265 seconds on that same task and seed, so the evidence does not establish a new covariance-factorization failure or a speed benefit from this change.

The molecular assessment explains why additional local parent beats do not settle chemical progress. Familiar aromatic, amide and amine families still coexist with reactive heteroatom bonds, repeated large assemblies and constrained closures. In matched windows, molecules containing rings of at most four atoms increase from 268 to 920, and products exceeding sixty heavy atoms increase from 168 to 320. Both panels leave every detected tetrahedral centre unassigned. These are observed coverage and plausibility limits; they neither explain the timeout uniquely nor prove that removing a particular bond or scaffold would improve scores.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove individual zero-ceiling projection only from selected historical replay targets: fit t_i = frozen_prior_log_likelihood_i + 60 * accepted_score_i for historical members, while current elites retain t_i = min(frozen_prior_log_likelihood_i + 60 * accepted_score_i, 0), preserving all selected membership, inverse-exposure coefficients and squared-residual Adam updates.
nodes.finding:
All 180 nonterminal updates with positive historical targets changed the learning direction after clipping. The intervention restored 566 historical target appearances that the parent would have capped, while preserving every current target and replay coefficient. Across all 420 nonterminal history updates, mean historical likelihood-derivative pressure increased from 1.211 to 4.849, and every real first backward matched the intended objective. The six median and sitagliptin sessions had no eligible targets and reproduced the parent's complete trajectories exactly.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.522705 to 0.513006, a paired decline of 0.009699 that exceeds the registered 0.002 effect. Seed changes were +0.003786, -0.001762 and -0.031122. Decoration hopping lost 0.025509 on average and declined in every seed; zaleplon lost 0.019707 despite improving in two seeds; docking lost 0.003279, concentrated in seed two. The other task means were unchanged. Population score dispersion fell from 0.020072 to 0.004937, and all fifteen sessions completed. Recorded mean AUC was nearly unchanged, 0.405593 to 0.405885.

Raw duplicate draws rose from 32.21% to 39.50%, and batches needing extra sampling rose from sixteen to forty-five. These coverage and sampling changes do not substitute for the score result.

The historical ceiling contributes useful control even when current elites remain capped and score priority and inverse-exposure weighting remain active. Recovering distinctions among positive historical targets increased their upward probability pressure but did not improve final search quality. The exact inactive sessions and matched policy prefixes rule out changed preparation or a universally different update path as explanations for this result. The improved seed and heterogeneous task responses still preclude a universal claim or an additive decomposition of current and historical ceiling benefits.

The large fitting residuals are partly unavoidable: positive sequence log-probability targets cannot be attained. Historical weighted error on the child's recorded states fell from 121.816 to 110.472 under the restored targets, while the all-capped comparator evaluated on those same states fell from 3.798 to 1.799. This separates an impossible target demand from failure to fit the feasible boundary; the comparator did not run an alternative policy. Clipping reduced gradient magnitude without erasing the directional intervention, and the higher duplicate burden is consistent with spending more draws revisiting structures. Individual current ceilings still do not ensure jointly feasible targets.

The chemistry assessment narrows the limitation further: familiar medicinal scaffolds remain available, yet broader decoration-hop core coverage moves into a lower-scoring leading family. Productive attachment patterns and size balance matter beyond adding more cores or restoring target distinctions. Missing stereochemical specification and uneven molecular size remain shared limitations, not consequences uniquely diagnosed by this ablation. The evidence supports retaining the historical ceiling in this composition while leaving its task dependence and interaction with repeated fitting open.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove latest-transition refresh of an already-live signed inverse-motif restriction: preserve its original entry and expiry unchanged, treating repeated selected-transition credit for that signed key as a no-op until ordinary expiry or release makes the key absent.

All 48 overlapping requests preserved the original restriction and its deadline, with zero refreshes or backfilled credit slots. On the recorded search history, this changed five candidate decisions across four batches: four vetoes disappeared and one was added. All fifteen task–seed runs completed. Latest-origin refresh affects both how long a restriction survives and which signed changes belong to one transition. Preserving an older origin restored one veto against an aromatic nitrogen positional isomer, yet removed four others by splitting newer groups or letting an older entry expire. None of the four newly admitted molecules was selected or improved the best archive, although two beat their current source. Each affected session initially kept the same batch winner; the two endpoint losses emerged only after later trajectories diverged. nodes.hypothesis: Replace point-estimate structural ascent with ascent of a numerically smoothed lower confidence bound on relaxed structural gain, subtracting one standard deviation computed from the full Gaussian coefficient posterior associated with the Parent's accepted-only ridge readout and differentiating that uncertainty through the frozen graph encoder.
nodes.finding:
The intended mechanism ran throughout this screening replica. All 150 accepted-score posterior fits were valid, all 145 feedback updates changed the full coefficient covariance, and all 152 structural optimizations changed their retained categorical distributions relative to the same starting state's mean-only ascent. Every one of the 1,450 emitted proposals used those changed distributions. All eligible nonzero uncertainty corrections reduced the raw gradient's uncertainty directional derivative, and every optimization retained a positive confidence gain; none needed a fallback.

On the single supplied seed, macro Top-1 fell from 0.361872 to 0.307903, a loss of 0.053969. Four objectives improved: zaleplon_mpo from 0.380139 to 0.394051, deco_hop from 0.589062 to 0.602445, median_2 from 0.180051 to 0.183284, and sitagliptin_mpo from 0.234090 to 0.330875. The loss came from drd2_docking, which fell from 0.426020 to 0.028858. Both runs completed all five 300-evaluation tasks with valid, distinct batches.

Local improvement became more frequent: 447 of 1,450 proposals beat their generating molecule, compared with 380 for the Parent. Predicted improvements were realized 41.1% of the time, up from 32.4%. Their average actual score change nevertheless worsened from -0.025853 to -0.031192, and average overstatement of assembled source-relative gains rose from 0.023479 to 0.034251. Better local hit rates did not produce a better overall search result.

This experiment establishes that coefficient uncertainty can change structural search before sampling and survive every downstream assembly step. It also shows that correcting this particular source of uncertainty is insufficient to remove prediction optimism or preserve the best final score. The strongest illustration is DRD2: 188 of 290 proposals beat their source, yet the search settled around a much lower score. The molecular assessment describes increasingly crowded polyacetals with late scores near 0.028858, while the Parent's stronger products belonged to a different biaryl/amine series. Repeated small improvements inside a weak chemical family can therefore make source-beating rates look favorable while valuable regions remain unreached.

The evidence leaves open whether the uncertainty penalty restricted productive exploration, whether early stochastic differences redirected the search, or whether structural information missing from the frozen features dominated the remaining errors. The posterior covers coefficient uncertainty conditional on an empirical noise estimate; it does not cover attachment choices, stereochemistry or the gap between a relaxed state and its assembled molecule. The generated structures still exhibit the reactive attachments and unspecified configurations identified by the molecular assessment. Preserving access to alternative core families and representing attachment environments remain worth testing. One paired seed cannot establish the repeatability of the four gains or the DRD2 loss.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove Morgan occurrence multiplicity only from the active conditional-residual covariance consumer: sample_values = original_count_raw_mean + original_count_score_scale * (original_normals @ binary_pool_factor.T), where binary_pool_factor factors the full binary-support GP conditional covariance with its own successful inherited jitter; retain the exact original count predictive location, nonzero residual influence and full cross-candidate correlation.
nodes.finding:
The covariance removal reached real search: repeated counts occurred in 68,485 of 69,600 generated pool rows, all 435 ordered selections changed against the passive count law, and 431 batch sets changed. It selected 1,590 accepted molecules absent from the passive count-selected sets; 1,538 entered later fits and 774 were later drawn as scored parents. The saved prediction means remained exactly the original count means on every selected identity. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.59645 to 0.55929, a loss of 0.03716 beyond the registered 0.002 scale. Seed macro changes were -0.07507, +0.00262 and -0.03903; nine task-seed endpoints fell and six rose. Task means fell for zaleplon, deco_hop and sitagliptin, while median_2 rose by 0.00860 and drd2 by 0.00041. The Parent’s late deco_hop seed-0 jump from 0.60956 to 0.85615 remains in the complete comparison; omitting that cell only as a sensitivity check still leaves a mean loss of 0.02207. Strict parent wins increased from 648 to 666, but their total positive gain fell from 17.25 to 14.41. Sequential incumbent wins also rose slightly, from 255 to 258, while their total gain fell from 5.82 to 5.26. All tasks completed with the original budget, batching and dependency lock, with no natural numerical fallback.

Count information has positive conditional endpoint value at this residual-covariance boundary even when the count-based predictive location is retained at each actual state. That narrows the earlier full-binary result: an endpoint loss does not require replacing the count mean. It does not measure how much of the earlier all-output loss was mediated by mean versus covariance, and it cannot be added to the parallel location probe. Binary residual geometry produced wider uncertainty on the selected molecules and more new generic-core parent winners, yet delivered smaller gain magnitudes and worse final endpoints. On the Child’s actual labels, count means were also more accurate and better ordered than passive binary means. Wider coverage, novelty and additional local wins therefore do not establish productive exploration. The Molecular review found recognizable amides and amines alongside more direct N-halogen attachments and more very large molecules; geometry and stereochemical identity remain unresolved. Those observations describe uneven chemical coverage, not a chemical cause of the covariance loss or evidence that a blanket filter would help. Shared Parent histories and seeds remain dependent controls. Natural failure-route robustness, separate variance/correlation mediation, sulfur interaction and transfer beyond this frozen panel remain open; final-batch sources without later fits or breeding are explicitly censored.

nodes.hypothesis: Retain accepted historical elites by successive score-ordered rounds across Murcko cores, taking each core's best record before any core's next record, then restore descending-score/canonical order for the inherited uniform replay while preserving original accepted records and the existing memory capacity.
nodes.finding:
Core protection changed 216 of 435 retention decisions that preceded further proposals. Every changed local contest retained more ring cores than greedy selection. Across all 435 local contests, mean ring-core coverage was 28.71 versus 27.50. Seventy-four protected accepted records subsequently entered learning in 83 exposures across 70 updates. All seventy updates showed a measurable protected gradient contribution, and protected target mean-square error fell from 165.10 to 100.63. Summed within sessions, actual replay covered 862 distinct ring cores versus 750 in the Parent, while its mean accepted reward fell from 0.31637 to 0.27659. Duplicate raw draws fell from 30.11% to 25.51%, and batch-level novel-valid yield rose from 60.31% to 64.76%; both runs still submitted exactly 4,350 valid novel proposals. Mean final score was 0.508476 versus 0.507554, a paired gain of 0.000922. The three seed changes were -0.013399, +0.007440 and +0.008726. Median_2 improved by 0.019383 on average, while sitagliptin_mpo fell by 0.015668; the smaller remaining task changes did not produce a clear overall score gain.

The earlier core-retention experiment in graph evolution failed to expose protected records to its restricted breeding sampler. Uniform neural replay opens that route: retained alternatives now enter the real loss and affect learning before later proposals. Access remains sparse, however. Only 74 of 302 protected records with a later nonterminal opportunity were drawn, and protection lasted a median of one retained snapshot after its first event. The same accepted-stream greedy comparison gives a replay reward of 0.31539, so weaker replay reward is a direct retention tradeoff rather than only a difference between generated trajectories. Broader core access and fewer duplicates did not meet the expected 0.002 mean score improvement; useful transfer from those lower-reward alternatives remains unresolved. The generated chemistry remains conventional, ring-rich aromatic amine/carbonyl chemistry with familiar leading families and no specified stereochemistry, so more core counts do not establish the precise chemical coverage the objectives need. Twenty-two protected training targets were positive and unattainable as log probabilities, another inherited limitation. The gradient evidence also has a numerical boundary: two mathematically equivalent groupings differed in combined norm by up to 0.045% under the inherited floating computation. Protected-removal signals exceeded the registered threshold by at least 86,620 times, but full vectors were not retained to establish exact numerical equivalence.

nodes.hypothesis: Search an expanding SMILES prefix tree with UCT using task-local observed returns, expand prefixes from a frozen corpus-trained autoregressive RNN, complete molecules by stochastic RNN rollouts, and backpropagate accepted oracle scores through their generating paths.
nodes.finding:
Both added replicas confirmed the intended search mechanism. Prior weights stayed fixed throughout each task, all 2,900 accepted generated scores updated their recorded tree paths, and all 19,580 traversal choices matched the declared UCT rule. Later accepted scores entered 11,960 chosen value estimates; in 2,120 selections the empirical-mean term made the chosen branch outrank a branch with a larger exploration bonus. The new replicas added 590 prefix nodes across ten task trees and completed every ten-molecule batch without an invalid or duplicate submission.

The two new macro final Top-1 scores were 0.508151 and 0.481129, alongside the original 0.479189. The three-seed mean is 0.489490 with population standard deviation 0.013219. Task means are 0.433514 for zaleplon, 0.612739 for decoration hopping, 0.964212 for docking, 0.177507 for median_2 and 0.259477 for sitagliptin. Docking remained between 0.938221 and 0.977922 across the three seeds; sitagliptin varied more, from 0.206406 to 0.334869. Prefix concentration persisted: 141 of the 290 new batches emitted all ten molecules from one prefix, versus 76 of 145 originally.

The search behavior and strong docking outcomes now recur across independently prepared priors, so the original result was not confined to one trained checkpoint or rollout seed. This replication does not isolate a score benefit from UCT over unguided sampling: all runs use both the corpus prior and tree adaptation, and preparation randomness changes along with search randomness. The substantial sitagliptin spread also shows that similar mechanism activation can yield materially different best molecules.

The search remains shallow at this budget. New rollout-start prefixes averaged about 3.38 tokens while completed strings averaged 38.53, and almost half the batches used a single prefix. Yet the molecular assessment finds broad ring and functional-group diversity, so concentrated short SMILES prefixes do not by themselves demonstrate chemical collapse. They may group molecules with weakly related returns. These observations make pending-rollout accounting and more chemically meaningful reward sharing plausible questions to test, without establishing that either improves final scores. Unspecified stereochemistry, size extremes and occasional awkward functional groups also persist despite the generally recognizable medicinal chemistry.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove Morgan environment multiplicity from the current sulfur-gated Parent by replacing each inherited cached count vector c with binary presence 1[c > 0] for every training, pool and next-fit feature consumer, while retaining the exact generalized Tanimoto implementation and all graph-generation, sulfur-admission, fitting and correlated-allocation rules.
nodes.finding:
The feature and allocation changes reached real search. Repeated raw counts occurred in 68,333 of 69,600 pool rows, and every active feature row matched its exact presence indicator. Same-state posterior changes altered 434 of 435 selected batch sets; 2,181 accepted molecules were absent from the passive count model's selected sets. Of these, 2,100 entered later fits and 847 were later used as scored parents. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.59645 to 0.55766, a removal loss of 0.03879, beyond the registered descriptive 0.002 scale. The Parent's deco_hop seed-0 jump from 0.60956 to 0.85615 at evaluation 281 remains in the complete primary comparison. That cell contributes 0.01666 to the mean loss; its leave-one-cell diagnostic still loses 0.02372. Every leave-one-cell diagnostic remains negative.

Occurrence multiplicity has positive conditional total contribution in the current sulfur-gated composition with the original GP and correlated allocator. The loss is heterogeneous and partly amplified by one rare breakthrough, but it is not confined to that cell. This supplies the previously missing applicability answer while preserving the older ungated loss of 0.05130. Three complete binary trajectories and several Parent trajectories exactly repeat older realizations, so they add no independent historical replication. On the molecules actually scored by the binary run, the passive count model had lower chronological mean squared error (0.01065 versus 0.01807) and better within-batch ranking (0.614 versus 0.389), even though binary latent intervals covered more realized labels. Wider uncertainty and changed allocations therefore do not by themselves establish useful exploration. The molecular assessment found useful amine and fused dione alternatives alongside enlarged connected rings, reactive attachments and much more cyclic cumulene chemistry. Those observations are consistent with uneven preservation of productive molecular arrangements; they do not identify the representation as the chemical cause or certify either run's feasibility. Mean and covariance changed together, and separate mediation, interaction with the sulfur gate and transfer beyond this frozen Search panel remain open.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace the original serialization of each uniformly selected historical elite with a deterministic accepted-identity-equivalent atom-rooted SMILES training view, preserving its original accepted record and score, while reserving one distinct equivalent view from training and keeping current elites, memory membership, the frozen prior and the inherited online loss unchanged.
nodes.finding:
All 2100 historical replay exposures before subsequent sampling used verified new spellings of the same accepted molecules. Their gradients differed measurably from original-string replay in all 420 eligible updates. Reserved equivalent strings, never used for training, improved their mean squared target error from 202.59 to 169.07; every task and seed showed this improvement. However, original historical strings worsened from 144.14 to 152.33, and their average likelihood fell in every session. Duplicate draws dropped from 30.11% to 14.07%, but raw chemical validity fell from 90.43% to 87.24%. The three-seed macro mean declined from 0.507554 to 0.493167, a paired loss of 0.014387 against the required gain of 0.002. Deco_hop improved in all seeds; sitagliptin declined in all seeds.

The new spellings entered the loss and transferred some fitting benefit to excluded spellings, so absence of exposure or complete failure of sequence transfer cannot explain the score loss. That transfer came with weaker support for the originally accepted strings, rather than better fitting across all representations. Keeping the prior fixed did not prevent this tradeoff. The original reward is preserved, but the inherited target depends on the spelling: the new views lower its value by about 47.86 log-likelihood units on average, and reduce positive, unattainable targets from 461 to 64 on the same accepted examples. Thus improved view fit combines different token contexts with different numeric targets; it does not establish representation-independent reward learning. Fewer duplicate samples and somewhat broader core coverage also fail to establish useful molecular transfer. The generated molecules still include recognizable carbonyl and cyclic-amine families, but changed leading arrangements do not consistently improve objectives, and the chemistry assessment retains stereochemical and reactive-group gaps. The experiment confirms a working view-replay and held-out-transfer mechanism while rejecting its overall utility under this panel.

nodes.hypothesis: Sample de novo molecules through a frozen deterministic SELFIES VAE decoder from an adaptive multivariate Gaussian, attach observed scores to the exact generating latent samples, and update the Gaussian mean, full covariance, and global step size using descending score ranks, weighted recombination, and cumulative evolution paths.
nodes.finding:
The macro mean of 0.303 places this eleventh of thirteen. The result is bimodal: 0.611 on deco_hop, which is the third best in the round, and 0.443 on zaleplon_mpo, against 0.064 on drd2_docking, which is the second worst any root recorded there. median_2 reached 0.208 and sitagliptin_mpo 0.187. Every mechanism check was exact. All 70 generations used full 24 by 24 covariance matrices with reconstructed rank-one and rank-mu terms, the recomputed learning constants matched, the cumulative path and step-size control were independently reproduced through eigendecomposition of each covariance, and every one of the accepted offspring joined its exact generating latent and score.

The optimizer is correct and its budget is the problem. Fourteen generations of twenty scored offspring is a very short run for an algorithm that spends its early generations learning a covariance, so the distribution barely finishes adapting before the budget ends. Its collapse on drd2_docking is informative in a different way: that objective rewards a compact basic amine, and this node's proposals there average eighty characters, nearly double every other objective on the same node. The Gaussian drifted into a region of latent space that decodes to large lipophilic molecules and covariance adaptation then reinforced that direction. A smaller population with more generations is the obvious change. One seed only.

nodes.hypothesis: Within reciprocal-compatible donor support, exclude cuts whose valid immediate product equals either generating parent, renormalize the inherited physical-cut and orientation masses, and use the original unconditioned donor law when revised support is empty or inapplicable.
nodes.finding:
The registered exclusion worked on 747 states with both removable parent-copy mass and remaining support. On those same states, the earlier compatible-donor law would allocate an average 47.20% probability to a valid parent copy; the revised conditional law allocated zero. Independent reconstruction found no weight, predicate, sampling or preview/actual discrepancy. Compatible atom-limit products kept their probability mass: 139 were actually selected and failed through the inherited checks. Empty support remained common: 11,911 attempts had no compatible orientation and 18,031 were emptied by removing copies, so both used the original donor fallback.

The conditioned channel produced 4,459 valid immediate products distinct from both parents, 3,408 pooled descendants, 356 evaluations and 134 final survivors. Of the 356 evaluated descendants, 280 were pure crossovers and 76 had finishing mutation; 80 beat their best generating parent, 32 improved the incumbent and 264 later served as parents. Across all branches, distinct-immediate crossover evaluations increased from 1,368 to 1,610 and pure crossover from 961 to 1,122. Fallback still supplied 70 evaluated products made novel only after copying a parent and then mutating it. Coverage remained uneven: median seed 0 pooled 23 distinct conditioned products but evaluated none; seeds 1 and 2 evaluated 13 and 14.

All 15 task runs completed. Mean final score fell from 0.595670 to 0.493017, a paired change of -0.102653 against the required +0.002. Seed changes were -0.066514, -0.030336 and -0.211109; ten of fifteen task-seed endpoints declined and five improved. Seed population SD rose from 0.026593 to 0.074022. More local parent beats, 695 versus 629, accompanied fewer incumbent gains, 249 versus 258, and weaker endpoints.

Removing immediate parent copies did expose a real, useful recombination channel, but solving that allocation obstacle did not make this donor refinement beneficial. Most crossover attempts still used inherited fallback, and more distinct evaluations did not preserve the complete search quality. This complete panel therefore supports a negative contribution from the revised donor law under the tested composition. It preserves the earlier negative compatibility-only result and the separate evidence that crossover itself contributes positively; it cannot isolate the incremental exclusion effect by treating the earlier sibling as the code Parent.

The chemical assessment makes clear why string distinctness is an incomplete target: evaluated descendants include very large repeated assemblies and difficult heterocycles, alongside useful compact amines and amides. A 110-heavy-atom repeated leader and a poorly scoring halogen-rich size tail coexist with stronger compact alternatives. These are observed limitations of selected chemistry, not proof that size or any one bond caused the loss. Local correspondence omits stereochemistry and remote functional relationships, and later mutations can change the matched environment.

The remaining attribution gap is which changed ancestors, pool competition and accepted feedback led to the lower endpoints; unselected previews supply no counterfactual scores. Invalid-only and whole-fragment/exception branches must also remain distinct: atom-limit failures were naturally observed, while other failure controls were synthetic or source-only. The bounded follow-up has now returned another endpoint loss, so its registered review condition is met without turning the result into a broad anti-crossover, validity or safety conclusion.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove nonuniform rank weighting only from each actual first-parent request by sampling uniformly over its exact original positive support after the inherited passive band draw, while retaining the original active score-quantile law and identity exclusion for every crossover-partner request.
nodes.finding:
Every one of 74,353 first-parent requests preserved the original eligible molecules while changing their probabilities; 71,068 actual identities differed from the inherited choice on the same random state. All 33,811 partner requests retained their original conditional law. Expected first-parent score on the actual populations fell from 0.359600 to 0.334474, and expected topness fell from 0.884224 to 0.755392. Changed first choices reached 3,926 of 4,350 accepted offspring; 2,211 of those offspring later bred. Full accepted-score learning, bounded greedy survival, ordinary graph transformations and all 435 complete candidate-pool selections remained active.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.523174, a paired change of -0.072496 against the registered 0.002 scale. Seed macro changes were -0.156631, -0.029176 and -0.031680. Eleven of fifteen endpoints declined. Four improved: zaleplon seeds 0 and 2 (+0.075655 and +0.010925), median similarity seed 1 (+0.013577), and sitagliptin seed 1 (+0.124636). Four task means declined; zaleplon rose by 0.001980. Macro population SD increased from 0.026593 to 0.041376. All task runs completed with their full oracle budgets and no posterior fallback.

The result localizes useful rank preference to the first-parent role while the crossover partner keeps its original law. Earlier removal from both roles could not establish that distinction. This is positive conditional contribution of first-parent rank weights in the tested composition and three-seed panel; it does not determine the partner’s contribution or permit subtraction of the shared-baseline controls into independent effects. The first parent supplies both ordinary mutation and crossover cores, so their separate values remain open.

More local wins did not mean better search. Strict best-parent beats rose from 629 to 819 and distinct accepted offspring later reused rose from 2,401 to 2,511, but mean best-parent score fell from 0.470456 to 0.372509 and mean offspring score from 0.385256 to 0.303045. Sequential incumbent gains fell from 258 to 237, with mean positive gain falling from 0.022510 to 0.019917. The easier parent reference explains why win counts alone would misread the outcome. Molecular inspection finds abundant rings, aromaticity and recognizable amine/carbonyl arrangements alongside reactive attachments and unresolved geometry and stereochemistry. Larger, decorated families did not consistently reproduce the Parent’s useful compact arrangements, but conventional-bond high-scoring counterexamples remain. Those associations narrow the search-quality problem without establishing a chemical cause of the loss. The fixed first-parent control now has an informative answer; support-only value, chemical mediation, the partner-only control and whole-foundation contribution remain open.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove historical replay from the active optimization loss, fitting only the unchanged current accepted elites to their individually ceiling-projected targets with a plain mean squared residual, while retaining historical memory, selection and exposure bookkeeping solely as passive comparison state.
nodes.finding:
Historical examples received exactly zero loss weight and zero likelihood derivatives in all 5,220 real optimizer steps containing history. All 420 history-bearing updates followed by proposals changed the gradient direction after clipping; every real first backward matched the current-only objective exactly. All fifteen matched initialization controls reproduced the same first twenty accepted records, and every session completed its budget.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.522705 to 0.495640, a paired decrease of 0.027066, exceeding the registered 0.002 effect. Seed changes were +0.008523, -0.023353 and -0.066368; population score dispersion fell from 0.020072 to 0.011865. Every task mean fell, led by sitagliptin (-0.072443) and deco-hop (-0.041088), then median (-0.015291), zaleplon (-0.006499) and docking (-0.0000068). Recorded mean AUC nevertheless rose from 0.405593 to 0.430068, with docking reaching strong scores earlier. The final-score loss therefore coexists with better discovery earlier in the recorded budget.

Current projected fitting error fell from 60.166 to 3.804 within updates. On the same actual updates, weighted error on passively observed history rose from 69.678 to 86.195; under active replay in the parent it fell from 3.366 to 2.436. Those are fitting measurements on each run's own states. Raw duplicate draws fell from 32.21% to 25.99%, and batches needing extra sampling fell from sixteen to three, while raw validity fell from 91.79% to 87.35%.

The developed learner still benefits from repeatedly fitting accepted history at the final endpoint. The parent's small historical gradients were not evidence that history was redundant: the records were already well fitted under continued replay. Once replay stopped, previously accepted examples often became much worse fitted even though current elites remained easy to fit. Matched initialization, exact loss isolation and the complete paired score panel support a contribution from replay in this composition. They do not show universal protection against forgetting, and the improved seed plus higher AUC leave the timing and task dependence of that contribution open.

The result separates useful search from generic novelty. Deco-hop explored more distinct nonempty molecular cores, 438 versus 355, yet finished worse. The supplied chemistry assessment finds familiar aromatic amide, sulfonamide and cyclic-amine families on both sides; generally smaller molecules and broad ring coverage did not reliably recover the stronger parent's fragment arrangements. New molecules shared a core with the selected historical set in 320 of 4,200 subsequent emissions, versus 685 with active replay, but that association cannot identify which remembered molecule caused a score change. Unspecified stereochemistry, oversized outliers and unstable-looking linker alternatives remain unresolved.

This removes historical loss contributions, not learned historical information: policy parameters and persistent Adam moments retain earlier current learning. Passive memory selection, exposure counts and union forwarding also remain, so fewer duplicate draws do not establish a replay runtime saving. Individual target ceilings remain active but do not make the joint current target set attainable: 177 of 420 nonterminal current sets still demand total sequence probability above one. Further contribution tests must keep those residual target constraints and the difference between early AUC and final quality explicit.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove optional ordinary single-parent mutation continuation (m-00000000000b). When the inherited saturation floor min(6, 1 + member_attempts // 80) equals one, each ordinary single-parent breeding attempt makes exactly one GraphOperators.mutate call. The original base-length draw rng.choices([1, 2, 3], [0.82, 0.15, 0.03]) is still made at its original position. When the floor exceeds one, the inherited max(base length, floor) walk is kept. Crossover and its finishing mutation, mutate's internal retries, the sulfur admission gate, pool size and correlated posterior allocation are unchanged.
nodes.finding:
The removal ran exactly as intended. In all 15 task/seed runs every ordinary single-parent mutation made one edit, suppressing 8,726 requested second and third edits; the Parent had made 8,742. About 18% of requests (7,463 of 41,716) asked for a longer walk and were cut to one edit, so the removal was exposed in every run. Before the first cut, each run reproduced the Parent molecule for molecule. No multi-edit offspring reached a pool or the oracle; the Parent evaluated 310 of them. Evaluated mutation offspring moved closer to their parents: mean Tanimoto similarity rose from 0.712 to 0.746, and the share below 0.5 fell from 6.2% to 1.9%. Crossover finishing (0.358), mutate retries, full 160-member pools and every posterior fit and selection were unchanged. One prediction failed. Ordinary sulfur-gate rejections were expected to fall below 100 but rose from 100 to 232. Multi-edit rejections did fall from 38 to zero, and the gate rule held in every case. Most of the rise (197 of 295 rejections) came from drd2, where the Child's populations drifted onto sulfur-bearing scaffolds: 97-99% of parents, against 21-41% in the Parent. The mean score fell from 0.5965 to 0.5658 (-0.0307), well past the 0.002 scale, and all three seeds were lower (-0.070, -0.007, -0.015). Nine of 15 task/seed cells were lower, four higher and two within the band. The largest single loss was deco_hop seed 0: the Parent's late 0.856 breakthrough was not reproduced and the Child ended at 0.607, accounting for -0.017 of the mean. Without that cell the loss is still -0.014. zaleplon was lower in all three seeds (-0.012 to -0.024), and in seed 1 the Parent's winning molecule was itself a two-edit product. sitagliptin was lower in all three seeds (-0.032 to -0.088). median_2 was slightly higher in all three (+0.001 to +0.025), and drd2 was mixed.

Optional multi-edit continuation now has a positive contribution on three different Parents: -0.027 on the ungated count-GP Parent, -0.019 on an exchange-containing Parent, and -0.031 here. The sulfur gate, which rejects multi-edit products disproportionately, did not change the sign, so the gap the catalog flagged for this Anchor is closed: keep continuation. The loss does not appear in local hit rates. Parent-beating offspring (648 to 659) and incumbent improvements (255 to 277) were flat or slightly up, and the single-edit products of formerly long requests were at least as productive per evaluation as the multi-edit ones they replaced (95 parent beats in 525 evaluations, against 43 in 310). So the value of the occasional two- or three-edit jump is not a higher success rate per proposal. It lies in the rarer larger moves that set where a run ends up: plateau escapes, late breakthroughs and the zaleplon winner that only a two-edit walk produced. That matches the Molecular assessment: without continuation, late leaders are one-atom permutations of a single inherited core, the 'refining familiar structures' pattern the research brief worries about, now somewhat stronger. Three cautions narrow the reading. First, about half the similarity gain comes from one-edit offspring themselves sitting closer to their parents in the diverged populations, not only from fewer long walks. Second, the uniform sitagliptin loss occurs where the Parent's multi-edit products never improved the incumbent, so part of the effect is adaptive divergence whose mechanism is unidentified. Third, sulfur-gate rejection counts track population chemistry rather than walk length, so they are a poor activation proxy. Worth trying next: a modestly larger or adaptive multi-edit share, testing the opposite direction. This removal does not locate an optimum, and the model-guided continuation variant lost 0.048 elsewhere, so more steps are not automatically better. Higher-floor saturation recovery and interactions with this round's kernel and pool-size siblings remain untested.

nodes.hypothesis: Project each selected sequence's augmented likelihood target independently onto the nonpositive log-probability half-line, t_i = min(frozen_prior_log_likelihood_i + 60 * accepted_score_i, 0), while preserving the Parent's inverse-exposure historical coefficients, selected membership and squared-residual Adam update.
nodes.finding:
All positive target excess was removed, and the change reached actual learning. Among 420 historical updates followed by proposals, 195 contained positive targets: 465 current and 602 historical row appearances were capped, removing 13,705.38 nats of unattainable target excess. Every affected update changed gradient direction after clipping. The three affected initialization updates did too. All 244 no-positive updates retained exactly the same local raw and projected gradient, and every one of the 450 real first backward passes matched the projected objective exactly. No capped row reversed from upward to downward likelihood pressure.

On the child's own historical training states, projection reduced the mean sum of absolute scalar learning factors from 12.795 to 6.305. Projected weighted squared error fell from 26.936 before learning to 2.984 afterward; error against the original raw targets on those same states fell from 135.072 to 97.457. Those are fitting measurements under different target definitions, not score gains. All fifteen tasks completed their budgets. Raw duplicate draws fell from 36.22% to 32.21%, and batches needing extra sampling fell from 29 to 16.

Mean final Top-1 rose from 0.517655 to 0.522705, a paired gain of 0.005050. Seed changes were -0.008594, +0.007415 and +0.016329. The gain was concentrated in deco-hop, whose task mean increased by 0.025328; docking rose by 0.001300 near its ceiling, zaleplon fell by 0.001379, and the other two tasks were unchanged. Mean recorded AUC fell from 0.406769 to 0.405593, so the endpoint gain did not produce faster useful discovery overall. Terminal updates establish execution only and contribute no later proposals.

Removing individually impossible demands can alter the direction of a clipped, exposure-weighted update without reversing any capped sequence's scalar learning direction. The matched controls make this attribution unusually clear: all six sessions without a positive target reproduced the parent's complete molecular records and scores exactly, and every changed session retained its matched proposal prefix until the first positive-target intervention. This narrows the effect to active target projection under the existing replay and optimizer rules.

The mechanism satisfies only the individual probability ceiling. Two hundred of the 420 historical updates still had combined projected target probability above one. Thirty-six batches set all ten selected targets to zero, erasing their raw target distinctions. Positive raw-target appearances actually increased from 977 to 1,067 as search changed; the mechanism removes their excess when fitting, rather than preventing such opportunities. Lower projected loss also does not protect every remembered row: 905 of 2,100 historical residuals worsened, almost the parent's 906, and 1,006 historical likelihoods decreased. Every repeated training appearance was consecutive, so these records cannot establish forgetting between skipped updates.

The chemical assessment places the main gain in a more concentrated decorated quinazoline family, while overall medicinal scaffolds remain ring-rich and attachment chemistry and stereochemical definition remain unresolved. Distinct observed cores increased for zaleplon despite its slightly lower endpoint and decreased for deco-hop despite its gain. That combination rules out treating broader core counts or lower duplication as a sufficient explanation for useful search. The open question is whether the endpoint benefit persists across seeds while retaining distinctions among saturated targets and preserving useful progress earlier in the budget.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove generated accepted records only from active GP conditioning by fitting immutable copies of the original usable initial accepted cohort, while recomputing the inherited score mean and scale from the full current accepted archive at every original fit call and retaining immediate live genetic feedback.
nodes.finding:
All 435 fits kept the same ten initial records in exact order while normalization used the growing accepted archive. The 4,200 generated records with a later fit never entered conditioning, but all entered normalization; 150 final records had no later opportunity. Every first batch matched the Parent exactly. After feedback, all 420 later sets differed from a full-conditioning reference on the same saved pools and normal draws. Of 3,608 actual accepted choices absent from those reference sets, 3,475 later entered normalization and 1,146 later bred. Across all offspring, 1,626 identities served as later parents, so feedback remained active outside conditioning.

All fifteen task runs completed. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.370013, a paired change of -0.225656 against the registered 0.002 loss scale. Seed changes were -0.245204, -0.221990 and -0.209774. Fourteen endpoints and all five task means declined; zaleplon in seed 2 increased by 0.001361. Docking had the largest mean decrease, from 0.998989 to 0.298274. The Child still made 511 strict generating-parent wins and 118 incumbent advances, versus 629 and 258 for the Parent. These local successes did not preserve its endpoint.

Generated conditioning records have positive conditional value even when adaptive normalization, score-based survival and recursive breeding remain available. This answers the missing membership question without treating the intervention as removal of all online learning. The same-input reference had lower prediction error on the actual scored molecules, but it supplies no rewards for omitted alternatives and no alternative future history; prediction error, reuse and uncertainty changes do not identify the route to the endpoint loss.

The earlier joint freeze and normalization-only findings remain intact. With complete matched outcomes and source boundaries checked, the four-treatment arithmetic interaction is +0.108156. Initial-only conditioning with current normalization scored 0.073800 below the jointly frozen version, while the historical full-conditioning comparison supported current normalization. The sign therefore depends on the conditioning context in these observations. This descriptive comparison shares one control, retains mixed task-level interaction signs, and establishes neither independent replication nor additive or mediated effects.

The molecular assessment finds persistent sulfur-rich, heavily halogenated docking families where the Parent reached more conventional aryl/amine arrangements, and more tiny fragments on every task. Useful aromatic amides and alternative ring arrangements still occur. These chemical associations help describe the weaker search outcomes but do not attribute them to one motif or prove a chemical mediator. Bond plausibility, ring geometry, stereochemical identity and the broader graph-evolution contribution remain open.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove the direct formula-preserving aromatic C/N positional-exchange options from the inherited atom-replacement menu, leaving only its original single-atom element substitutions while retaining all other graph, feedback and posterior mechanisms.
nodes.finding:
Exchange selection fell to zero despite 904 eligible selected-site menus; all withheld partners and unchanged legacy choices were verified. Crossover, ordinary mutations, accepted-only learning and correlated posterior selection remained active. All fifteen runs completed. Mean final Top-1 rose from 0.574344 to 0.595670, a paired gain of 0.021326, reversing the predicted decrease of at least 0.002. All three seed macro scores improved; nine task–seed scores rose, four fell and two tied. Gains were largest for decoration hopping and sitagliptin, while mean zaleplon and median-task scores declined. Population SD rose from 0.012317 to 0.026593. Mean recorded AUC increased slightly, from 0.482560 to 0.483817.

The Parent had real local successes from direct exchanges: thirty-five clean exchange offspring included nine parent beats and four incumbent improvements, and thirty later bred. Those successes did not establish that allocating menu probability to this route helped the full count-posterior search. Removing it improved the final mean while barely changing total parent beats, from 624 to 629. The largest decoration gain accompanied a shift from a 71-heavy-atom leader to a 30-heavy-atom heterocyclic family. This supports a contribution test at the level of the complete search process rather than judging an operator from selected success stories. It does not show that every exchange is harmful or isolate the value of an omitted isomer: smaller menus also change later random draws, pools and feedback. The chemistry remains mixed. Large assemblies became less common, but reactive nitrogen-halogen bonds, unspecified stereochemistry and difficult ring geometry persisted, including a high-scoring cyclic cumulene.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove ongoing scored-adaptive source support and rank allocation jointly at the breeder consumer by using uniform eligible first-parent and distinct-identity partner draws from one immutable serial-ordered snapshot of the original retained usable initial LIVE population, including that snapshot in the inherited crossover-availability guard, while ordinary current greedy survivors and full accepted-label count-GP learning remain immediate.
nodes.finding:
Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.59567 to 0.35099 across the five tasks and three matched seeds, a loss of 0.24468 against the registered 0.002 scale. Fourteen of fifteen endpoints fell; zaleplon’s third seed improved by 0.00046. Every breeding draw used an unchanged initial molecule, and 1,309 generated molecules that naturally had positive original breeding support were blocked. All 4,200 nonterminal generated labels still entered later GP fits; the final 150 labels had no later suggestion. Local best-parent beats rose from 629 to 2,033, while incumbent gains fell from 258 to 79: beating weaker fixed sources did not sustain improvement. Prospective selected-stream pair ordering rose from 71.1% to 76.1%, and prediction MSE fell from 0.01272 to 0.00197, yet endpoint quality deteriorated. Seed macro dispersion widened from 0.02659 to 0.07699.

The experiment supports positive conditional value of adaptive source membership and score-ranked allocation together at the breeder boundary, even when every generated score still trains the predictor. It rules out a broken or starved learning archive as the explanation for this panel’s loss, and shows why parent-beat counts and easier selected-stream prediction can mislead when source quality and reward range fall. Chemistry agrees with this pattern: small fragments and acyclic emissions became more frequent, and compact free-amine/aromatic combinations were recovered inconsistently, despite many new cores and continued access to rich ring systems. Fewer questionable reactive bonds did not rescue the endpoints. These are observed chemical associations, not a demonstrated mediator. The earlier fixed ranked-source and live-uniform controls are compatible with this result but share its Parent; their losses cannot be added or used to infer an interaction. The experiment does not divide the value between membership, weights, survivor selection or subsequent learned allocation, and it does not remove retained graph primitives or initial score-dependent retention. The whole graph-foundation contribution gap therefore remains open.
