nodes.hypothesis: Remove only ongoing recomputation of the GP score-normalization mean and scale by retaining the exact initial accepted-label normalization constants, while continuing full-archive raw-label conditioning and the inherited correlated posterior selector at every original fit.
nodes.finding:
The intended control executed while online learning remained active. All 435 fits retained every currently accepted raw label in order, with 4,200 generated labels entering their next fit and 150 final observations correctly censored. The first fit and selected batch matched the Parent in every task and seed. Fixed initial constants then differed from current-archive normalization in all 420 later fits. On the actual Child pools, the passive adaptive-normalization reference selected different sets in 401 of 435 batches; five additional batches differed only in order. Of 1,710 actually evaluated molecules absent from the reference sets, 1,641 entered a later fit and 1,016 later served as breeding parents. All evaluations completed.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.561314, a paired change of -0.034355 against the predicted loss scale of 0.002. Seed changes were -0.098249, +0.017166 and -0.021983; ten of fifteen task–seed endpoints declined and five improved. The Child had more generating-parent wins, 691 versus 629, but fewer sequential incumbent advances, 242 versus 258. Lower local prediction error also failed to translate into a better endpoint: on the same scored Child molecules, fixed-normalizer MSE was 0.005729 versus 0.005867 for the passive adaptive reference, while nominal 95% latent-interval coverage fell from 77.43% to 55.49%.

Updating the score mean and scale has positive conditional value even when the GP continues to learn from every new accepted label. The earlier control froze training membership and normalization together; this result narrows the answer to normalization without undoing that joint finding. It still does not separate centering from scaling, the associated change in raw observation noise, or their interaction with online training. The fixed scale becomes especially small relative to later score spread in docking and sitagliptin, whereas it exceeds the contemporaneous scale in median_2. These measured differences explain why raw uncertainty changes in different directions; they do not identify which consequence caused the endpoint loss.

More local parent wins, more reused breeders and slightly better same-stream prediction error are therefore insufficient evidence for useful search. The molecular assessment likewise finds fewer perceived scaffold families on every objective, but preserves useful aromatic amides, amines and alternative ring arrangements alongside reactive substituents, questionable ring geometry and unresolved stereochemistry. That combination does not support a universal size, ring or heteroatom explanation, nor does it assign the score loss to one chemical motif. The passive reference has no rewards for omitted choices and no alternative future history, so mediation remains open. This complete exposed panel answers the registered normalization-only control under the current budget and composition; it supplies neither a broader claim that uncertainty should always increase nor a reason to retune this fixed control.

nodes.hypothesis: Use a task-local fingerprint Gaussian process to choose genetic-phase evaluations by posterior-function maximization over fresh graph offspring pools, retaining the Parent's mandatory first fresh-policy offspring at each graph-cycle handoff.
nodes.finding:
Both additional seeds reproduced the intended selection and feedback behavior. Every one of their 1,800 selected offspring maximized its reconstructed correlated posterior draw, and uncertainty changed 1,671 choices (92.8%) relative to choosing the highest posterior mean. All 190 fits used earlier accepted scores only, all 1,710 eligible fixed-molecule predictions changed after feedback, and all 100 protected neural-to-graph handoffs were preserved. There were 90 later reciprocal cycles and 4,480 nonzero graph-bearing policy updates. The two new mean final-best scores were 0.528301 and 0.517608, compared with 0.516098 in the original run of the same algorithm. Across all three seeds, mean final-best score is 0.520669 with a population standard deviation of 0.005432. The three-seed objective means are 0.458300 for zaleplon_mpo, 0.615427 for deco_hop, 0.999997 for drd2_docking, 0.204624 for median_2 and 0.324997 for sitagliptin_mpo. Only 246 of 1,900 graph descendants in the new runs beat their best generating parent (12.95%), and their mean child-minus-parent score was -0.110567. Across all three runs those quantities are 386 of 2,850 (13.54%) and -0.099708. These are below the original direct-submission Parent's single-seed parent-beating rate of 18.21%; that historical comparison is not a paired three-seed efficiency estimate.

Replication rules out missing selector execution or a broken reciprocal handoff as explanations for the weak offspring yield: both mechanisms remain active across all three seeds. It also weakens the original suggestion of improved average child-minus-parent score, which held on the screening seed but not on the two additional seeds. The selector consistently changes which offspring are evaluated, but this does not establish that uncertainty itself improves final scores. The original direct-submission Parent has only one available seed, so the earlier paired score gain of 0.005848 remains a single-seed comparison; the new results establish repeatable execution and describe score variability without establishing a paired multi-seed improvement. Prediction error in the new runs is lower than an archive-mean baseline on four of five objectives, yet nominal 95% latent intervals cover only 80.4% of selected accepted scores overall and 41.9% on sitagliptin_mpo, where prediction MSE is also worse than that baseline. These are informative but uncalibrated predictions on the selected molecules. The molecular assessment shows that ring systems and useful basic-amine chemistry are already available, while leading families still mix conventional scaffolds with reactive substitutions, complicated connectivity and unspecified stereochemistry. That narrows the remaining questions toward reliable discrimination among chemically credible alternatives and broader useful scaffold coverage. Matched Parent replicas and a same-pool mean-only or direct-order comparison are still needed to isolate score benefit, efficiency and uncertainty's contribution.

nodes.hypothesis: At each original accepted-archive refit, train a fresh fixed two-hidden-layer Bayesian rank network on uniformly sampled unordered accepted-label pairs with tie-zero, zero-margin ranking loss and source Gaussian KL regularization; replace active GP function-draw allocation by stable masked maxima of the network ten-draw latent mean plus 0.3 times sample standard deviation over the unchanged fresh count-feature pool, keeping the original GP passive.
nodes.finding:
The learner and allocation mechanism ran in all 15 sessions: 421 informative fits produced nonconstant pool means, 3770 of 4210 accepted offspring differed from the passive GP selected set, 3579 changed choices reached informative next-fit training, and 1145 changed parents produced 3427 distinct accepted direct descendants. On the same accepted labels, pair-order accuracy was 0.470128 versus 0.706399 for the passive GP, and mean batch Spearman was -0.074808 versus 0.512550. Both measures were worse in every task/seed aggregate and in each pooled early, middle and late phase; one small middle-phase cell favored the learner. Parent-beating offspring increased from 648 to 801, but summed positive gain fell from 17.251535 to 9.643219 and sequential incumbent gain from 5.819415 to 2.074884. Comparing equal-length Parent prefixes leaves the same adverse direction. All 13 completed task/seed endpoints were lower. The only complete seed macro was 0.303631 versus its matched Parent 0.643098, a delta of -0.339467. Two deco_hop sessions timed out at 190 and 270 observations, so the complete three-seed +0.002 goal and Child dispersion remain unevaluable. Eighteen terminal evaluator labels had saved predictions/provenance but no Candidate offspring receipt; they enter offline ordering and gain measurements, never later-feedback exposure.

This rules out lack of informative pairs, a wholly collapsed rank output, or failure to deliver changed molecules as explanations for the observed lack of benefit. Local win counts were misleading: the Child offspring faced substantially weaker generating parents, with mean best-parent score 0.243566 versus 0.455304, while mean offspring quality fell to 0.197223 from 0.372050. Broader core discovery also failed to translate into stronger progress: productive typed-core first arrivals increased from 262 to 424, yet their accepted descendants' positive gain fell from 4.289217 to 2.151438. The molecular assessment is consistent with this gap: large repeated aromatic assemblies, crowded cages and uneven local heteroatom chemistry coexist with lower labels than the Parent's more compact alternatives. Those associations do not identify a timeout cause or prove that a size/chemistry filter would help. All seven borrowed elements operated, but the explicit count representation, fresh-pool, cadence, tie, learning-rate and random-stream adaptations limit transfer from the source study. The result applies to the joint fixed learner/UCB recipe; it does not isolate the loss or acquisition, prove ranking-mediated score loss, or refute pairwise learning generally. The missing endpoints prevent a complete performance verdict, but the exposed ordering/productivity failures and 13 completed losses provide no justified continuation or parameter rescue for this recipe.

nodes.hypothesis: Train the unlabeled recurrent prior to predict the unchanged original SMILES targets after zeroing exactly one uniformly selected eligible content-token input embedding per sequence, while keeping the Parent uniform token loss, clean fixed-holdout checkpoint selection and all online computations unchanged.
nodes.finding:
The preparation mechanism executed on all three seeds: one eligible content embedding was erased in each of 7,613,952 training-sequence exposures per prior, with the original target strings preserved. Independent replay exactly reproduced all three training-target and erasure-mask receipts. On the entire fixed 4,096-row holdout for each seed, mean erased-downstream negative log likelihood fell from the Parent's 1.00417 to 0.53006; every seed improved. The corresponding erasure penalty fell from 0.53933 to 0.05658. This was a real improvement in prediction with missing context, although clean full-sequence NLL worsened from 0.56458 to 0.57213. Clean likelihood still selected checkpoints, and online computation used intact inputs with a frozen prior. Downstream generation did not gain validity: raw RDKit-valid draws fell from 90.43% to 89.27%. Duplicate draws fell from 30.11% to 27.51%, so the raw canonical-novel fraction rose from 60.31% to 61.76%; all 4,350 submitted proposals remained valid and unique. The final three-seed macro mean fell from 0.50755 to 0.49844, a paired change of -0.00911. Seed changes were -0.01795, +0.00012 and -0.00950. Mean zaleplon score rose by 0.03533, while sitagliptin fell by 0.08046 and lost score in every seed. The intended +0.002 macro improvement was not achieved.

The missing-vector probe measures a capability the prior successfully learned; the absolute erased-context loss improvement is much larger than the small clean-context loss degradation. Its failure to improve raw molecular validity separates this capability from tolerance of the mistakes that matter during ordinary generation. The probe leaves all later teacher-forced tokens correct and never measures recovery from an incorrectly sampled token or molecular graph. It therefore supplies no evidence that the main online error source has been addressed. Lower duplicate concentration broadened the sampled output slightly, but did not preserve the chemical arrangements needed for the strongest objectives. The molecular assessment found mostly conventional medicinal chemistry, together with extreme polar and lipophilic tails; for sitagliptin, the stronger parental polar-ring/carbonyl families were not recovered. This connects the score loss to a change in chemical coverage without identifying a single causal functional group. The evidence supports missing-context robustness as a retained capability, with a clean-language-modeling tradeoff and no demonstrated optimization gain under the tested panel.

nodes.hypothesis: Require each signed inverse-motif match to place the candidate destination occurrence count at or beyond that selected transition's pre-move count in the inverse direction before it can participate in the existing same-transition bidirectional tabu veto.
nodes.finding:
Count qualification excluded 176 of 4,653 active signed matches. On the same actual candidates and memory tables, this reduced vetoes from 171 under the parent rule to 160. Eleven fresh molecules entered nine complete batches and received evaluation; three became the next walk state. One improved its source by 0.004513 and the archive by 0.002061, while ten lost to their source and none tied. Attribute selection, selected-transition credit and restriction lifetimes remained unchanged when compared on the same accepted history. All fifteen sessions completed their full budgets. The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.495641, a paired change of -0.026119 against the required +0.002. The paired seed changes were +0.023133, -0.011512 and -0.089977. DRD2 accounted for most of the loss: its task mean fell by 0.130008. The deco_hop mean rose by 0.001763, zaleplon fell by 0.002347, and median_2 and sitagliptin retained exactly the same molecular trajectories and scores.

Occurrence counts identify a real admission distinction that signed motif coverage alone misses: two of the eleven newly evaluated molecules still matched every live attribute of a qualifying transition. However, most count-ineligible matches were not allocation bottlenecks: 157 of 176 occurred in candidates already admitted by the parent's one-sign or cross-origin rules. The eleven actual admissions therefore establish changed allocation, not a general score advantage from more quantitatively specific memory. Source-beating proposals became slightly more frequent across the full stream, but their total positive gain and the total archive improvement both fell. Together with ten source-worsening new admissions and strongly different DRD2 outcomes across seeds, this narrows the useful question to which abundance reversals support productive exploration, rather than whether count boundaries are implemented correctly. The three selected admissions have real later descendants and archive gains, but those paths also include changed random-draw consumption and subsequent edits; their gains cannot be assigned to the admission alone. The stricter parent alternatives stopped short in all nine affected batches, so their missing members and scores remain unknown. The molecular assessment likewise finds no established improvement in practical chemistry: recognizable aromatic and amine families still coexist with reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur frameworks and undefined stereochemistry. Restoring motif abundance is neither a physical edit-site measurement nor evidence of chemical stability.

nodes.hypothesis: Ablate the retained aromatic C/N relocation menu augmentation so each change_atom draw chooses only its inherited single-element substitution options, removing direct formula-preserving nitrogen exchanges and their allocation competition while retaining the complete inverse-memory and accepted-walk rules.
nodes.finding:
Direct nitrogen exchanges fell from 13 proposals, 10 accepted molecules and 3 selected states to zero, despite eligible pairs appearing in 92 child batches. Removing their menu entries changed 65 of 435 submitted batches and 54 selected states, while the retained tabu gate, overlap refresh, graph validation and accepted-maximum walk passed reconstruction. All fifteen tasks completed. Mean final score fell from 0.521759 to 0.520918, a paired change of -0.000841 within the specified 0.002 margin. Seed changes were +0.000374, -0.002898 and zero; the largest task loss was deco_hop seed 1 at -0.014491. Twelve of fifteen final task scores were unchanged. Every complete child trajectory exactly reproduced the historical repaired ancestor. Live exchange enumeration disappeared, but unmatched wall timings do not establish a speedup.

The result confirms the expected reversion and repeatability; it adds no independent seed evidence beyond the historical ancestor. This sparse exchange allocation is not needed to stay within the supplied mean margin on this panel, although individual paths benefit and one replica loses more than the margin. The experiment also shows why the exchange chemistry cannot be credited or blamed alone: in one shared-source batch, the Parent exchange was not selected, but the changed random-draw progression altered a later ordinary carbon extension into an oxygen extension and changed the winner. Removal measures the whole menu allocation policy. Nitrogen-containing molecules remain reachable, and the resulting families retain reactive bonds, unusual sulfur, dense rings and unassigned stereochemistry. The evidence supports a narrower proposal path in this particular walk, without demonstrating better chemistry or general dispensability of nitrogen relocation.

nodes.hypothesis: Renew an inverse-motif restriction for exactly one additional inherited tenure when that specific live entry has actually participated in a same-transition bidirectional veto during its initial tenure, retaining its original selected-transition provenance and allowing no further renewal.
nodes.finding:
The intended lifetime and evaluation changes both happened. All 343 used restrictions that survived to their original deadline renewed once, adding 1206 completed restriction-steps; none exceeded the eight-step limit. Renewed entries caused 65 additional vetoes in 53 batches and displaced 62 candidates from complete, reconstructed ten-member comparator batches. All 62 replacements were evaluated, seven became walk states, eight beat their source and two improved the best archive. Renewal changed at least one batch in every task/seed session, while credit selection, overlap replacement and provenance remained intact. All fifteen sessions completed their full budgets. The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.513767, a paired change of -0.007992 against the required +0.002. Seeds 0 and 2 improved by 0.018110 and 0.028962, but seed 1 fell by 0.071049. Mean DRD2 score fell by 0.068863 and deco_hop by 0.008789; gains in zaleplon (+0.022797), sitagliptin (+0.013894) and median_2 (+0.000999) did not offset those losses. The renewal mechanism is confirmed; its preregistered score benefit failed.

This rules out a merely larger memory table or a lack of later recurrence as the explanation for the result: renewed restrictions changed both evaluated membership and selected states. Recurrence remains a weak guide to value. Of 343 renewals, 240 never participated in another qualifying veto during their observed extension, and partial matches alone accounted for 103 of those cases. More concretely, at the first DRD2 divergence in seed 1, the renewed memory excluded a neighbor that the actual Parent had scored from the identical source and selected as its winner, improving that source by 0.059783. The Child instead made a worsening move. This is direct evidence that extending an exercised restriction can remove a useful opportunity; the later endpoint loss cannot be assigned to that one veto because subsequent draws and walks diverge. The molecular assessment also finds reactive heteroatom bonds and complex sulfur cages among strongly scored structures, so this recurrence signal provides no demonstrated improvement in chemical stability or makeability. The open question is whether a task-independent signal can distinguish harmful revisits from productive reuse; actual veto participation alone did not supply that distinction in this panel.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace the Parent's exposure-weighted squared residual with an exposure-weighted Huber residual whose transition is the detached starting weighted root-mean-square residual of each update, floored at the square root of the inherited stopping tolerance and held fixed through that update, thereby capping individual residual influence while preserving selected members, augmented targets and exposure coefficients.
nodes.finding:
The cap executed in all 450 updates. In the 420 historical updates followed by new proposals, it reduced influence on 1,465 of 4,200 selected row exposures at update start, including 1,092 current elites and 373 historical elites. The capped rows' mean share of absolute scalar influence fell from 69.22% to 59.37% on those same inputs. Every one of these updates changed the combined gradient direction even after global norm clipping, and every real first backward matched the Huber diagnostic exactly. Huber loss fell in 419 of the 420 updates, although 928 of 2,100 individual historical row exposures ended with larger residuals. All replicas completed. The three-seed final mean fell from 0.517655 to 0.508373, a paired change of -0.009283, with seed changes -0.026055, +0.032442 and -0.034235. The endpoint gain expected by the intent was not observed. Recorded mean AUC nevertheless rose from 0.406769 to 0.458439 and improved in every seed. The largest endpoint changes were a sitagliptin decrease of 0.080247 and a zaleplon increase of 0.035486. Raw duplicates rose from 36.22% to 48.80%, and batches needing additional sampling doubled from 29 to 58, while all 4,350 submitted proposals remained valid and novel.

Global gradient clipping did not make the row-level cap redundant: relative learning direction changed measurably in every prospective fitting opportunity. That establishes a real learning intervention, but more balanced residual influence did not provide the proposed final-score benefit. Faster discovery and the final endpoint separated: much of the AUC gain came from reaching strong DRD2 molecules earlier, where the parent already finished near the score ceiling, while sitagliptin lost substantial endpoint value. The molecular assessment found its stronger compact lactam–sulfonamide family in only one seed; broad core coverage in the other seeds did not supply equally useful structures. The cap also left target feasibility unresolved: historical exposures with positive, unattainable log-probability targets increased from 489 to 752 on the resulting trajectories. Starting caps affected current elites much more often than history, yet accepted-score averages and AUC increased, so the prediction of uniformly weaker early exploitation is not supported either. What remains open is how to preserve these early gains while reducing later repetition and avoiding the task-dependent loss of useful molecular families. The evidence does not isolate a particular suppressed row, token change or chemical feature as the cause of the endpoint loss.

nodes.hypothesis: Extend the existing change_bond neighborhood with relocation of an intact single-attachment acyclic branch from an aromatic carbon to its adjacent hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon, directly exposing substitution-position isomers while preserving the branch, ring framework and molecular formula.
nodes.finding:
Ten fresh positional isomers reached evaluation from thirteen sampled branch relocations, with all atoms, the complete branch, molecular formula and aromatic ring framework retained. Six moved one-heavy-atom groups and four moved larger groups. One thiol position change improved its source score; the other nine lost. None won its batch, updated the best archive or produced a later walk descendant. The three-seed macro mean nevertheless rose from 0.520918 to 0.525257, a paired gain of 0.004339 that exceeds the 0.002 target. One seed improved and two declined; the largest endpoint gain was in one DRD2 seed, while median_2 and sitagliptin endpoints were unchanged throughout.

Direct positional accessibility is established: none of the ten scored products is reachable by a single original bond-order change, and each changes local motifs and measured score. Intact-group retention therefore avoids the necessary atom loss of branch deletion, but it does not reliably make a stronger neighbor. All four evaluated larger-branch relocations lose to their sources, including the methoxy and carboxyl shifts. The distinction between a successful panel and useful new molecules matters here: since no relocation is selected, the panel gain cannot be credited to descendants carrying a moved group. The expanded menu also changes proposal choices and batch competition among the original operators. The evidence supports a working positional channel and one local thiol-position gain, while leaving a reproducible score benefit from retaining a new position unresolved. The stronger sulfur-free aryl-amine series identified by the molecular assessment is an original-operator outcome and still contains strained nitrogen rings; other populations retain unusual sulfur and reactive heteroatom bonds. Conserving the existing group and ring has not established better stability or synthetic accessibility.

nodes.hypothesis: Among exact accepted-score batch maxima, select the candidate with the fewest heavy atoms before applying the inherited canonical lexical fallback, so an equally scored larger neighbor cannot become current solely because of its canonical spelling.
nodes.finding:
The rule changed six of 435 accepted transitions, all on equal-score plateaus in deco_hop seeds 0 and 2. Each selected an already scored maximum with one or two fewer heavy atoms than the lexical alternative, saving 10 atoms across those same-batch comparisons. All selected identities reached the actual current state and memory update. The other 429 choices, the immediate maximum score, canonical fallback and independent archive rule passed reconstruction checks. The three-seed panel mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.520655: paired change -0.001104 against the preregistered +0.002 minimum. Deco_hop endpoints fell by 0.001632 in seed 0 and 0.014925 in seed 2; every other task/replica scored trajectory was identical. The local tie mechanism is confirmed, while its expected score benefit was not observed.

Canonical ordering did sometimes choose unnecessary growth at an exactly tied score, so this experiment establishes a real selection opportunity. Avoiding that growth did not preserve a permanently compact or more productive walk: every changed choice was followed by a later growth move, and the six-transition plateau containing the first seed-2 change kept its original length. Mean proposal size in the affected task decreased by only 0.30 heavy atoms, with the median unchanged at 38. Smaller also did not mean chemically simpler: one changed choice introduced a carbon-sulfur triple bond, and the molecular assessment still finds reactive heteroatom attachments and questionable complete structures. Half of the changed choices altered bonds or elements without shrinking their own source; the other half deleted one atom. The poorer later results therefore concern changed chemical neighborhoods and memory provenance, not an isolated effect of size. In the seed-2 continuation, accepted source-beating neighbors fell from 19 to nine. The evidence narrows the opportunity to sparse exact ties in one objective family and makes chemically meaningful tie preferences or persistence of compact states worth testing separately; neither has a demonstrated score benefit here.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace any-single-attribute tabu vetoes with same-transition bidirectional inverse-attribute matching: veto a valid novel graph edit only if its signed motif changes match at least one active positive restriction and at least one active negative restriction originating from the same selected accepted transition.
nodes.finding:
Across the two added replicas' observed streams, the original any-match rule would veto 1,578 of 2,831 valid novel attempts (55.74%); the paired rule vetoed 121 (4.27%) on the same candidates and live memory. All 1,457 newly admitted proposals reached evaluation, accounting for 53.76% of optimizer evaluations. Of these, 141 beat their current source (9.68%), and their mean neighbor-minus-source score was -0.09247. They supplied 141 actual next-current states and 60 strict incumbent-improving observations. The remaining restrictions vetoed 112 distinct task/run molecular identities, changed 79 of 271 batches and produced nine selected next states absent from the passive unfiltered batch. Matching and memory-lifecycle checks agreed with the intended rule throughout the observed execution.

The first added replica completed all five tasks at 300 evaluations each, scoring 0.5277988 in macro final Top-1 versus 0.5180779 in the earlier screening replica of this same algorithm. The second added replica completed four tasks but crashed on zaleplon after 110 evaluations. Its completed final scores were 0.6092183 for decoration hopping, 0.9148144 for DRD2, 0.2018564 for median_2 and 0.4484554 for sitagliptin. The evaluator reports 1,310 total calls and no macro score for that replica, so there is no complete three-seed score estimate.

The crash occurred after the evaluator scored a full ten-molecule batch. The first accepted molecule's canonical spelling changed between generation and feedback, so its pending record could not be found. All ten evaluations are visible in the trajectory, but none of that batch's feedback was ingested and no next state was selected.

The narrower reversal test reproducibly changes oracle allocation and the walk while retaining active structural memory. Correct same-transition matching, intact four-step expiry and the surviving fresh-identity vetoes rule out erased memory as the source of easier admission. Most newly admitted neighbors still score below their source, so greater admissibility has not established better average neighborhood quality. The useful effects arise from a minority of admitted moves; the separate value of the remaining vetoes remains unmeasured because rejected alternatives were never scored.

The identity lookup failure previously seen only in the supplied smoke evidence now occurs in a formal replica. Its cause is localized: the generator keys pending proposals by a molecular spelling that changes when the evaluator canonicalizes it. The failing proposal was one of the newly admitted partial matches. This exposes an inherited execution limitation on the newly accessible trajectory and prevents a claim of complete or repeatable score benefit. A stable identity join and a complete replica are needed before assessing that benefit.

The molecular assessment shows that partial-overlap admission still explores recurring ring-rich families with unusual sulfur bonding, dense ring junctions and unspecified geometry. Memory selectivity does not establish chemically plausible alternatives or broad useful scaffold coverage; those limitations remain separate from the verified matching effect.

nodes.hypothesis: Quadruple only the fresh offspring pool target per announced batch member, from sixteen to sixty-four (160 to 640 candidates per announced batch of ten), so the unchanged accepted-only count-Tanimoto GP correlated Thompson selector takes its ten sequentially masked joint-draw maxima over a four-times larger field of fresh de novo offspring produced by the unchanged breeder, operators, continuation, crossover and finishing, sulfur gate and stable identity admission.
nodes.finding:
The enlarged field was built and used. Every one of the 435 batches across the complete fifteen-cell panel ranked exactly 640 fresh offspring, never truncated, at a modest generation cost of 1.147 breeding attempts per admitted member against the Parent's 1.093; the inherited escalation branches never fired and the longest struggle for a single pool member anywhere was nine attempts. The extra candidates genuinely competed: 73.3 percent of the 4,350 oracle calls went to members generated beyond position 160, the selection index distribution is nearly flat over all 640 positions, and the first 160 positions took 26.7 percent of the choices against the 25 percent expected if all members were interchangeable. That last number is the whole result in miniature: the later-generated members behaved exactly like the earlier ones. They beat their own generating parent at 0.152 and improved the incumbent at 0.063, against 0.153 and 0.067 for the members inside the Parent-sized prefix.

The screening-quality prediction failed. The registered test was that selected candidates should sit further above their own pool in posterior mean than the Parent's +1.054 standard deviations. They sat at +1.043, slightly lower, and fell in eight of fifteen cells, while the pool's own best available candidate did improve (+1.841 against +1.735). So the wider field did offer better candidates and the unchanged Thompson rule did not take them: it drew relatively more uncertain members (selected posterior SD 0.897 of the pool average, against 0.849 in the Parent), disagreed with the posterior-mean argmax in 92.8 percent of choices instead of 86.5, and picked members ranked on average 135th of 640 by posterior mean, 76.6 percent of them outside their pool's top ten. This is the registered failure mode for this intervention: four times more candidates means four times more chances for an extreme residual draw on an uncertain molecule, and that is what the enlarged field was spent on.

Downstream effects were real but tiny, and they went both ways. Parent-beating rose from 0.149 to 0.152 and incumbent improvement from 0.0586 to 0.0644, prediction error on emitted members fell slightly (batch MSE 0.0106 against 0.0112) and within-batch rank correlation rose from 0.526 to 0.546. Against that, the molecules actually evaluated were worse on average (mean offspring score 0.360 against 0.372) and larger (30.7 against 28.4 heavy atoms), with 181 emissions of five heavy atoms or fewer against 105.

The endpoint moved the wrong way. The complete matched panel mean fell 0.016060, from 0.596453 to 0.580393, against the registered requirement of at least +0.002; seed macros moved -0.044984, -0.012371 and +0.009174, six of fifteen cells improved, and the mean AUC fell from 0.4710 to 0.4555. Dispersion across seeds narrowed (population SD 0.0211 against 0.0340), which is not a substitute for the endpoint. Most of the panel loss is one cell: deco_hop seed 0 at -0.2459. The two runs were level there until evaluation 280 (Child 0.6088, Parent 0.6096), and then the Parent made its single rare late jump to 0.8561 while the Child finished at 0.6102. Excluding only that cell the panel would be close to flat. The largest gains were sitagliptin_mpo seed 2 at +0.0922 and zaleplon_mpo seed 0 at +0.0515. Compute behaved as predicted: non-oracle work rose about fourfold to a mean of 106 seconds per task, the worst task used 10.8 percent of its timeout and the worst node 2.9 percent, with no fallback, no truncation and every Cholesky succeeding at the smallest jitter.

Candidate-set breadth is now measured on this lineage and it is not the lever. The pool multiplier had been 16 in every node since the screening layer was introduced, and the Parent's near-uniform use of all 160 positions had been read as evidence that the selector was field-limited. Quadrupling the field falsifies that reading: the selector spreads over 640 positions just as evenly, which means the uniformity was never a sign of hunger for more candidates, only of how flat the sampled posterior is across fresh offspring of one population. At a cost of four times the generation work per evaluation, the panel mean fell 0.016 and not one intermediate quantity moved enough to matter. Breadth under this selector is exhausted as a direction; the remaining headroom in this component is in the posterior and the acquisition rule, not in how many molecules they are shown.

The sharpest thing learned is the split between the field and the choice. The best candidate available in the pool improved measurably when the pool grew, yet the chosen candidate did not: the enlarged field's extra quality went into the tail of the sampled draw rather than into what was evaluated. With unit prior amplitude and a fixed noise SD of 0.05, a joint Thompson draw over a larger correlated field gets its maximum increasingly from residual extremes on uncertain members, and the diagnostics show exactly that drift. This makes a concrete, cheap next test available: hold the pool at 640 and shrink the effective residual scale, or take the posterior-mean argmax for a fraction of the ten slots, and see whether the improved pool maximum can be converted into improved selections. It also sharpens the reading of the earlier removal results, which showed the composite selector worth 0.128 on this Parent: that contribution is about having a posterior-ranked fresh field at all, not about its size.

The chemistry explains why extra screening could not help. The molecular review of this node finds the generator producing ring-rich frameworks finished with N-Cl, O-Cl, S-F and N-F bonds, free imines and thiocarbonyls, no trifluoromethyl group in 4,350 molecules, no formal charge and no assigned stereocentre, and on the flattest objective it grows oligomers to a mean of 43 heavy atoms and QED 0.19 rather than finding alternatives. A larger pool samples that same vocabulary more densely; it widens the degenerate tail along with the useful one, which is visible here as 181 near-trivial fragments emitted against the Parent's 105, and as the deco_hop seed-0 cell where mean emitted size reached 55.7 heavy atoms and 600 crossover products were rejected as invalid. Scaffold diversity, distinct scaffolds among the best fifty, and late-phase pairwise distance are all unchanged from the Parent, so the wider field did not produce collapse and did not produce discovery either; it produced more of the same chemistry.

Two things stay open. The deco_hop seed-0 contrast is dominated by the Parent's single late breakthrough at evaluation 281, which no Child in three rounds has reproduced, so the size of the loss is fragile even though its sign holds on two of three seeds; a trustworthy reading of that cell needs more seeds, not more analysis. And this result constrains one multiplier at one announced batch size. It does not establish that 16 is optimal, does not rule out that a much smaller field would do as well for a quarter of the compute, and says nothing about breadth under a different acquisition rule. The compute-efficiency question is now the interesting one in the other direction: if 640 buys nothing over 160, it is worth asking what 4 would cost.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove optional second and third successive GraphOperators.mutate calls from ordinary single-parent proposals when the inherited saturation floor is one, retaining the original sampled base-length draw and the full max(base length, saturation floor) schedule whenever that floor exceeds one.
nodes.finding:
Ordinary second and third mutation calls disappeared under real requests for longer walks. The Child made one call in all 41,665 ordinary attempts; 7,373 requests would have allowed continuation, suppressing 8,589 requested calls. The Parent actually executed 8,737 continuation calls. Of the affected first-call products, 6,980 entered the candidate pools and 518 reached accepted evaluation; 100 beat their generating parent and 35 improved the incumbent. Internal retries, crossover finishing mutations and correlated posterior selection remained active. Neither side exercised saturation recovery.

The complete matched three-seed panel fell from mean final Top-1 0.595670 to 0.568802, a paired change of -0.026868, exceeding the registered 0.002 loss scale. Seed changes were -0.047714, -0.009154 and -0.023735. Population dispersion decreased from 0.026593 to 0.012088, but every seed macro was lower. Ten task-seed endpoints declined and five improved: all three median_2 endpoints, zaleplon_mpo in seed zero, and sitagliptin_mpo in seed one. Three task means declined and two rose. Correct execution and the predicted endpoint loss support a positive contribution from retained ordinary continuation in this composition.

The removal exposed useful first products, yet useful local steps did not preserve final search quality. Across the whole Child, parent beats increased from 629 to 714 and incumbent improvements from 258 to 299 while endpoints fell. Those counts depend on changing ancestors and incumbents; they cannot tell us what the omitted continuations would have scored. This resolves the previously open current-composition contribution question, separately from the earlier exchange-enabled experiment. It does not make the separate crossover and posterior-component losses additive.

The molecular assessment helps narrow the next question to coverage of useful structural arrangements. The Child still finds varied aromatic, carbonyl and amine families, but its leading repeated aza-aryl family does not recover the Parent’s compact carbonyl-thione organization. Some other families improve, and reactive bonds, difficult ring geometries and unspecified stereochemistry persist on both sides. Fewer calls therefore do not establish chemically simpler or more feasible output. These associations do not identify which omitted product or molecular feature caused the score loss. Saturation recovery remains untested, and fewer calls did not yield an observed speedup: total wall time was about 1,778 seconds versus 579, alongside much greater oracle time on the changed molecules.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace the accepted-prefix categorical reference penalty KL(policy || frozen prior) with KL(frozen prior || policy), preserving the existing coefficient, sequence normalization, score-ranked replay and trajectory-balance objective.
nodes.finding:
The reference gradient changed in all 7,185 updates after the policy and prior differed; the 15 identical initial states correctly showed no gradient difference. That activation did not produce better measured retention. Across 230,400 replay occurrences, prior-to-policy KL rose from 0.473648 before updates to 0.475468 afterward, and total variation rose from 0.215919 to 0.216668. Both average changes were unfavorable in every task-seed session. The inherited policy-to-prior diagnostic was also higher than the parent overall, although the two runs followed different histories.

Raw valid novel emission increased slightly, from 7,991 to 8,050 of 12,000 draws, or 66.59% to 67.08%. Mean accepted policy-origin score increased from 0.204941 to 0.222083, and graph feedback continued to affect later generation. Nevertheless, the three-seed mean final score fell from 0.550198 to 0.543814, a decrease of 0.006384. Paired seed changes were +0.000428, -0.027151 and +0.007572. The main final-score losses were in zaleplon_mpo and median_2, whose task means fell by 0.024000 and 0.020793. All fifteen task replicas completed their 300 evaluations.

A restoring component on nearly abandoned prior-supported alternatives was present, yet that component alone did not preserve conditional support under these joint score-driven updates. This rules out an unchanged KL orientation, a drifting prior, missing graph feedback or altered replay labels as explanations for the outcome. The registered retention-benefit falsifier is triggered even though mechanism execution is confirmed. The loss can improve while its reference-divergence component worsens; changing direction at the inherited coefficient therefore does not establish the intended protection.

The small gain in valid novel strings cannot be credited to demonstrated support retention. Its seed dependence, the missing parent prior-to-policy diagnostic and the different search histories leave that causal connection unresolved. Graph-bearing policy movement and later scaffold matches increased, which also argues against explaining the score loss as a simple shutdown of graph-to-policy learning. The molecular assessment still found a mixture of plausible compact molecules and oversized or chemically questionable assemblies. The experiment therefore narrows the next question to how joint training can retain useful conditional support without losing objective progress; changing the reference gradient alone did not settle it.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace dot-product count Tanimoto covariance by exact min/max count Tanimoto K(x,y)=sum_i min(x_i,y_i)/sum_i max(x_i,y_i) on unchanged folded Morgan occurrence rows, with empty/empty=1 and empty/nonempty=0.
nodes.finding:
The changed posterior reached every batch: all 435 selection orders changed against the passive original GP, and 433 selected sets changed. All 4,350 emitted offspring were accepted with their logged identities. On those same scored offspring, pair-order accuracy was 70.68% versus 71.51% for the passive original model, mean batch Spearman was 0.522 versus 0.536, and prediction MSE was 0.009562 versus 0.009146. Productive search also weakened overall: 623 offspring beat their best generating parent versus 629 for the actual Parent; sequential incumbent gains fell from 258 to 232, and beats of the whole-batch pre-feedback incumbent fell from 346 to 311. Mean offspring and source scores fell, while generic-core novelty on parent-beating events rose slightly from 190 to 195. Final macro mean fell from 0.595670 to 0.547424, a matched change of -0.048245 rather than the required +0.002. Seed macro differences were -0.083646, -0.018090 and -0.043000. Three of fifteen task/seed endpoints improved; twelve declined. Seed dispersion narrowed from 0.026593 to 0.007300 around the lower mean.

This was an exposed covariance intervention: repeated counts were present, all three Gram systems moved, the inherited allocator delivered different candidates, and the numerical and identity audits found no execution failure. Its activation is confirmed; its predicted ranking and endpoint benefit is contradicted under this Parent and profile. Lower MSE against the actual Parent stream did not signify better search: the child sampled lower absolute offspring/source scores, and the original GP fit to the exact same child state predicted its chosen scores better overall. Farther-from-archive accepted pairs and some individual task/seed cells provide positive ranking or local-win counterexamples, but they do not rescue the failed complete gain test or reveal rewards of unselected candidates. Rich aromatic, carbonyl and amine organization remained alongside reactive nitrogen attachments, difficult bridges and unspecified stereochemistry; the molecular evidence does not isolate a covariance-mediated chemical cause. The result closes this exact min/max law without transferring the failure to all count kernels or to those generator gaps. Mean-versus-covariance mediation, independent plausible scaffold supply and broader contribution remain open; terminal records and overlapping ancestry limit continuation claims.

nodes.hypothesis: Select the reusable prior checkpoint by fixed-noise ancestral valid-connected-unique molecular emission yield among unlabeled checkpoints that improve the initial holdout loss, breaking ties by lower original-string holdout NLL while preserving the Parent training and stopping rules.
nodes.finding:
The rule selected different prior weights in all three preparations. On the fixed selection samples, the chosen checkpoints produced 243, 245 and 238 valid, distinct molecules out of 256, compared with 232, 236 and 229 for the lowest-loss checkpoints from the same training trajectories. The independent diagnostic changed those counts by -1, +10 and 0; its pooled gain was only 9 of 768 draws, compared with 29 of 768 on the selection samples. Thus checkpoint choice and its selection-sample advantage are established, while an independent yield advantage appeared in only one seed. All training runs completed the same 29,742 updates, and the ordinary lowest-loss weights exactly matched the published parent weights, so no training-length difference explains the choice. The selected checkpoints incurred small token-loss increases of 0.001852, 0.002624 and 0.003124.

During optimization, valid terminated neural draws fell from 8,441 of 12,000 to 8,156 of 12,000, or 70.34% to 67.97%. Nevertheless, the complete three-seed endpoint mean rose from 0.520669 to 0.550198, with paired gains of 0.026285, 0.051553 and 0.010747. The mean gain, 0.029528, exceeds the registered 0.002 target. Deco hop, median and sitagliptin task means improved; zaleplon was nearly unchanged and DRD2 declined slightly. Every task completed the supplied evaluation panel. The new checkpoints therefore changed useful downstream search outcomes, but the score increase cannot be explained as a consistent increase in valid molecular emission.

The minimum token-loss checkpoint is not the only useful prior along the same unchanged learning trajectory. This experiment cleanly separates checkpoint choice from changes to training representations, gradients or the online search algorithm. It also exposes the limitation of the selection criterion: choosing among 60 checkpoints with one fixed 256-draw sample creates a selection-sample advantage that mostly disappears on fresh diagnostic randomness in two seeds. That pattern is compatible with selection noise and supports only limited generalization of the measured yield gain. The lower online raw validity shows that valid prior sampling and useful adaptation should remain separate measurements; even the first online batch follows accepted-score policy updates.

The molecular assessment gives the same distinction a chemical interpretation. Useful aromatic, amine and carbonyl arrangements coexist with unusual sulfur bonding, nitroso groups, peroxide bonds and unresolved stereochemistry. Valid connected uniqueness does not distinguish those liabilities, and higher endpoint scores do not establish better synthetic plausibility. The campaign now has evidence that an earlier checkpoint can improve the reciprocal search without a reliably better valid-emission rate. Whether a more representative unlabeled diagnostic can predict that downstream usefulness remains open.

nodes.hypothesis: Freeze a corpus-trained bidirectional masked discrete denoiser over SAFE fragment sequences, then repeatedly select high-ranked task-local observed molecules, replace one fragment with a variable-length mask chunk, iteratively denoise the missing tokens while preserving the surrounding context, and use accepted scores to update which whole molecules supply future contexts.
nodes.finding:
The macro mean of 0.495 is second of thirteen. It is the only root above 0.20 on every single objective: 0.908 on drd2_docking, 0.591 on deco_hop, 0.424 on zaleplon_mpo, 0.344 on sitagliptin_mpo and 0.207 on median_2. Context selection enrichment was positive on every objective and held under a tie-midrank sensitivity check. Every remasking attempt decoded with an unchanged prefix and suffix, a nonempty retained subgraph, exactly one replacement block and fixed outside attachment labels. One registered measurement came back against expectation: the mean score of a completion minus its generating context is negative in aggregate and on every task, so individual completions usually score worse than the molecule they came from.

Consistency, not peak performance, is what this node contributes. Its sitagliptin_mpo score of 0.344 is the best in the round and its drd2_docking of 0.908 is third, which no other method combines. The negative context-beating delta is the interesting result: the search improves by keeping the rare good completion and discarding the rest, rather than by proposing better molecules on average. That means throughput of attempts matters more here than proposal quality, which is a different tuning direction from every other lineage. One seed, and the fragment vocabulary itself has not been varied.

nodes.hypothesis: Reject a graph-valid canonically novel neighbor before tabu testing when it increases the source-relative count of bonds between F, Cl, Br or I and a non-carbon heavy atom, redirecting the existing edit stream away from new non-carbon halogen attachment while preserving carbon-halogen eligibility and the Parent walk.
nodes.finding:
The gate rejected 130 valid, novel attachment increases; all 130 would otherwise pass the contemporaneous tabu rule, and each was followed by another actual neighbor from the same source. Starting from zero-count molecules, the complete panel emitted no targeted bonds, compared with 974 affected Parent emissions. Carbon-halogen chemistry remained active in 2670 evaluated molecules versus 2596 before, including 265 source improvements and 153 archive gains. Generation attempts per batch rose from 12.15 to 12.63. The macro mean fell from 0.520918 to 0.513044, a paired loss of 0.007874 exceeding the permitted 0.002. Gains in DRD2 and some other endpoints did not offset the larger sitagliptin losses.

The attachment criterion has a distinct effect beyond existing tabu memory: every measured rejection changes which fresh neighbor can reach evaluation. It also separates carbon-bound halogens from direct nitrogen-, oxygen- and sulfur-halogen bonds, rather than simply eliminating all halogen-containing molecules. The chemistry cleanup therefore happened, but its score cost is real in this panel. The Parent had obtained six immediate archive improvements from count-increasing moves, so this was never a uniformly unhelpful channel; those historical scores do not label the different rejected products. The rule is source-relative and would permit equal or lower counts on a molecule with pre-existing counted bonds. Its complete absence here depends on the zero-count starting states. Other liabilities remain outside the mechanism: the molecular assessment still finds unusual sulfur coordination, dense bridges, small unsaturated rings and undefined stereochemistry. Removing one attachment class neither establishes generally plausible chemistry nor preserves objective performance.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove Morgan environment multiplicity from the shared posterior representation by replacing each inherited count vector c with binary presence 1[c > 0] for every training, pool and next-fit feature use, while retaining the generalized Tanimoto implementation and all fitting, graph-generation and correlated-allocation rules.
nodes.finding:
Every active feature is binary under extensive repeated-environment exposure, and all 435 fitted pools change their posterior relative to counts on the same inputs. The retained correlated draws, graph operations and accepted feedback reconstruct correctly. Mean final score falls from 0.595670 to 0.544374, a paired loss of 0.051296 against the registered 0.002 scale. All seed macros decline: 0.077877, 0.002003 and 0.074008. Twelve task-seed endpoints decline; zaleplon_mpo improves on seed 0, while deco_hop and sitagliptin_mpo improve on seed 1. On the actual binary stream, latent 1.96-SD coverage is 79.75% versus 73.52% for a passive count model using the same earlier labels and scored molecules. Their MSEs are 0.016600/0.009873. Binary error is higher in all fifteen task-seed cells, while its coverage is lower for median_2 on every seed despite the aggregate increase. These diagnostics answer a different question from endpoint search utility.

The isolated reverse control supports a positive contribution of environment multiplicity in the current exchange-free composition. It changes both fitted means and covariance, so the experiment does not assign the gain specifically to calibrated uncertainty. More structural variety is also insufficient: binary selection yields 2,267 typed and 1,546 generic cores versus 1,851 and 1,118 under counts, yet strict local parent beats fall from 629 to 565 and incumbent gains from 258 to 218. Molecular evidence preserves the useful conventional ketone and aminoaryl-dione gains alongside reactive environments, repeated large assemblies and destructive fragments; no universal size or chemistry rule explains the score loss. The fifteen trajectories and all shared non-timing decisions exactly reproduce the earlier binary ancestor. That establishes provenance and rules out treating the replay as new independent evidence; the current matched Parent comparison remains the contribution test. Which changes in similarity, means and covariance mediate the useful search behavior remains open.

nodes.hypothesis: Walk from the best supplied molecular observation by directly evaluating fresh graph-edit neighbors that pass expiring inverse local-subgraph restrictions, move to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even when it worsens the current score, and install bounded inverse attributes of that selected transition while retaining a separate best-observed archive.
nodes.finding:
Both new replicas reproduced the intended graph walk and structural memory. All 2,900 accepted proposals were valid novel edits of the actual current graph. Temporary inverse-motif restrictions vetoed 7,503 otherwise valid novel draws (72.12% of such tests), changed 279 of the 280 batches after initialization, and led to 176 selected next states absent from the first ten unfiltered valid novel neighbors. Every one of 89 required worsening moves occurred; 62 later recovered above their own pre-move score, 24 did not recover despite later opportunities, and three occurred at the terminal step. Memory installation, refresh and four-step expiry reconstructed correctly, and neither new replica needed a forced release. Accepted neighbors beat their generating current score 292 times out of 2,900 (10.07%), with 167 strict improvements to the best-observed score. The new macro final-best scores were 0.49531 and 0.50903, alongside 0.51081 in seed 0. The three-seed mean was 0.50505 with population standard deviation 0.00693. Task means were 0.40256 for zaleplon, 0.60530 for scaffold hopping, 0.83839 for DRD2 docking, 0.18975 for median similarity and 0.48924 for sitagliptin. Every task finished all 300 oracle evaluations, and every final best score exceeded its supplied initial best.

The replication rules out memory acting only as whole-molecule duplicate rejection or as a passive record: its restrictions repeatedly removed unseen molecules and changed actual state selection. Worsening moves can be followed by recovery and later incumbent gains, but the episodes overlap and do not establish distinct successful escapes. The separate best archive matters: on sitagliptin the final current scores were only 0.16887 and 0.20350 while the preserved best scores were 0.41959 and 0.46369. Following the current walk alone would therefore conceal much of what the search had found. Broad structural vetoing still coexists with weak average local proposals: accepted neighbors scored 0.06743 below their current source on average, despite positive average winner transitions. The passive reference has no scores for omitted molecules, so changed batches and incumbent-gain provenance cannot establish an advantage over an unrestricted walk. The molecular assessment further shows that graph sanitization and numerical gains coexist with N-halogen bonds, unusual sulfur valence and strained ring arrangements in tightly related high-scoring families. Correct tabu operation does not make those products chemically plausible or demonstrate broader useful scaffold exploration. A scored comparative walk and chemically meaningful evaluation remain necessary to separate useful memory from redirection toward permissively scored chemistry.

nodes.hypothesis: Choose the fingerprint Gaussian process's standardized observation-noise standard deviation at each fit by minimum exact negative log marginal likelihood over five fixed multiples of the inherited noise level, using only the current accepted archive.
nodes.finding:
The learned noise reached the actual posterior in 255 of 435 fits; 180 retained the reference level and 116 selected the largest allowed value. All five likelihood trials, final conditioning, accepted-label provenance and recorded posterior draws reconstructed correctly. After feedback, mean uncertainty on the admitted molecules remained 0.02821 score units, compared with 0.00405 under the fixed-noise rule on those same current archives.

On the 4,350 molecules actually submitted, the matched fixed-noise comparison shows latent 1.96-SD coverage rising from 79.68% to 82.44%. Including fitted observation noise raises observed-score coverage from 79.72% to 89.84%, with average interval width increasing from 0.1901 to 0.2604. Mean predictive negative log density improves from 6.3965 to 1.9102, and prediction MSE falls from 0.012180 to 0.011625 against an archive-mean baseline of 0.024654. Within-batch rank association weakens from 0.4146 to 0.3943. These are comparisons on identical accepted data and actual emissions.

Search utility declines: mean final-best score falls from 0.551771 to 0.534231, a paired loss of 0.017540 that misses the registered +0.002 benefit criterion. One seed improves and two decline; population standard deviation rises from 0.008223 to 0.023491. DRD2 and zaleplon task means fall, sitagliptin rises, and decoration and median retain exactly the same trajectories in every seed. Actual best-parent beats are essentially unchanged at 592 versus 593. All tasks and pools complete, with no numerical fallback; the additional 2,175 noise-trial factorizations consume 3.745 seconds of recorded unsynchronized host search time.

Archive likelihood can identify and propagate substantial surrogate mismatch without improving the search endpoint. The matched measurements show better average coverage and predictive loss, but wider intervals still cover fewer than the nominal 95% of observed scores, and ranking gets weaker. Better uncertainty accounting is therefore insufficient evidence that the unchanged posterior-draw selector allocates evaluations more productively. The unchanged decoration and median trajectories also show that a measurable posterior change need not alter an emitted choice.

The remaining uncertainty problem includes score scaling. In an early sitagliptin batch, even the maximum standardized noise is multiplied by an archive scale of 0.001: a predicted mean of 0.00111 and total SD of 0.00118 precede a score of 0.18595, more than 157 SDs away. This narrows the next modeling question toward anticipating score-unit changes from a nearly flat accepted archive; expanding the menu alone is not established as a remedy. Frequent upper-endpoint selection leaves the appropriate noise range unresolved, while unchanged binary-fingerprint ties leave representational limitations intact.

The chemistry assessment also finds the existing structural liabilities intact, including unusually large repeated scaffolds, reactive heteroatom bonds, undefined stereochemistry and a new sulfur-radical branch. These observations limit what improved statistical coverage or occasional high scores mean chemically; they do not identify the cause of the aggregate score loss. The evidence establishes noise-learning activation and a failed score-benefit expectation on this panel, without isolating the causal value of any individual changed selection.

nodes.hypothesis: Retain the Parent's local Morgan occurrence-count covariance and add sparse topological atom-pair occurrence-count covariance, using the fixed equal-weight average of their separate generalized Tanimoto kernels for every GP block while preserving raw-score learning and the inherited search rules.

Against the same-input local-only reference, 432 selected sets and 433 orders changed; three sets and two orders remained unchanged. Mean final score fell from 0.595670 to 0.562261, a loss of 0.033408 against the required gain of 0.002. Seed deltas were −0.072325, +0.009185 and −0.037084. Thirteen other pairs shared atom-pair counts but remained distinguishable through local counts; the channels still do not establish complete molecular identity. The negative result belongs to this one equal-weight composition and does not undo the earlier evidence for retaining local occurrence counts or isolate atom-pair information from mixture weighting. Molecular evidence still shows reactive heteroatom-halogen and sulfur motifs, large linked assemblies and destructive fragments alongside conventional high-scoring chemistry. nodes.hypothesis: Rank real task-local molecular observations into positive and negative examples, build fresh categorical regions by randomly fixing a positive exemplar's SELFIES-frame coordinates until every observed negative frame is excluded and the remaining free-coordinate count is bounded, then sample uniform token assignments inside those regions with a broader uniform construction-space component.
nodes.finding:
All five objectives completed on the screening seed, with 300 evaluations each and all 1,450 generated submissions accepted. Every initial molecule preserved its identity through token encoding, every returned score stayed attached to its actual sampled frame, and all 150 rank-label snapshots included the required cutoff ties. All 1,355 constructed regions retained their positive exemplar and reduced the number of included observed negatives to zero, while leaving exactly four of 79 token positions free. Real feedback was reused: all 1,400 generated observations with a later opportunity participated in subsequent region construction. However, the final restrictions in every region were identical to those obtained from the four-free-coordinate limit alone.

The five-task final Top-1 mean was 0.315539, compared with 0.208492 for the supplied initial observations. Initial-to-final Top-1 scores were 0.305105 to 0.345581 for zaleplon_mpo, 0.548381 to 0.579123 for deco_hop, 0.019041 to 0.120104 for drd2_docking, 0.167839 to 0.167839 for median_2, and 0.002094 to 0.365051 for sitagliptin_mpo. All 18 incumbent improvements came from regional submissions. Only 67 of 1,304 accepted regional proposals (5.14%) beat their selected exemplar; mean child-minus-exemplar score was -0.096376. There is no Parent comparison or additional seed in this root experiment, so these within-run gains do not establish a comparative score advantage.

Negative examples were consulted and newly admitted negatives prolonged the exclusion phase in 330 regions, so the classifier was active. Yet exclusion always finished after at most 70 fixed coordinates, while the uncertainty limit required 75. The limit therefore determined every final mask, and perfect exclusion supplies no evidence for an additional contribution of negative labels to proposal geometry or score. The observed procedure supports direct molecular score provenance and feedback-guided sampling around positively ranked exemplars; whether making negatives influence the final region improves search remains open.

Distinct token restrictions also did not imply distinct molecular neighborhoods: 48 raw decodes overlapped an earlier different region, and ten draws recovered a currently negative molecular identity through another encoding. Filtering caught these cases, but it cannot repair weak molecular geometry. The molecular assessment finds frequent radicals, unusual charges and reactive linkages among high scorers, with only an uneven subset of conventional scaffold chemistry. Together with the low exemplar-beating rate and the unchanged median_2 incumbent, this identifies useful, chemically credible token neighborhoods as an unresolved bottleneck. Neither reliable performance across seeds nor a benefit from alternative serialization views is established.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace dot-product count Tanimoto covariance with fixed Matérn-3/2 covariance on L2-normalized unchanged folded Morgan count rows: z(x)=x/||x||2 for nonzero x and z(0)=0; r=||z(x)-z(y)||2; K(x,y)=(1+sqrt(3)*r)*exp(-sqrt(3)*r), with lengthscale one and unit amplitude.
nodes.finding:
The replacement changed 434 of 435 accepted candidate sets and 435 selection orders when compared with the original predictor on exactly the same pools, earlier observations and random draws. All 4,350 Child offspring reached real feedback with their original pre-label predictions; no formal numerical fallback or rejection occurred. On those actual Child selections, unequal-label pair-order accuracy was 0.646947, versus 0.731356 for passive original predictions; average defined within-batch Spearman was 0.380506, versus 0.579077. Raw-unit selected-stream MSE was 0.012160, versus 0.007080 for the passive original and 0.032088 for the archive mean. The actual Parent stream had pair accuracy 0.711063, Spearman 0.532208 and MSE 0.012718; those adaptive streams differ after the first batch. Strict best-generating-parent beats increased from 629 to 682, and sequential incumbent advances from 258 to 269. Batch-frozen incumbent beats were 373 versus 346. Despite those local events, mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595669649733 to 0.568161409345, a signed change of -0.027508240389. Seed macro changes were -0.062538302981, +0.001846540890, -0.021832959074; 4 of 15 task/seed endpoints improved. Population seed dispersion was 0.007592488960 versus 0.026592870628. The complete +0.002 gain criterion failed.

The failure is informative because the new predictor had real allocation exposure, complete accepted feedback and intact numerical controls: an inactive implementation or unseen changed choices cannot explain the negative endpoint result. More parent-beating offspring and incumbent events did not translate into better final best molecules. Average best-generating-parent score fell from 0.470456 to 0.416185, and offspring score from 0.385256 to 0.338080: beating weaker sources more often is not independent evidence of stronger exploration. The original predictor also ranks the very same scored Child selections better, narrowing the predictive hypothesis without requiring unscored pool labels. Local event counts and selected-stream errors cannot stand in for the benchmark objective. Normalizing count rows deliberately loses overall count scale and introduces proportional-coordinate aliases by construction, although no proportional-only pairs or zero rows were naturally exposed in this panel; those effects belong to the complete tested covariance recipe and were not separately randomized or attributed. Productive-event reuse, later conditioning and descendant cores remain conditional associations with overlapping ancestry and censored final-batch sources. The chemistry assessment also shows familiar useful carbonyl/aromatic and amine frameworks alongside reactive heteroatom-halogen arrangements, unresolved stereochemistry and occasional large elaborations; compact leaders and useful deletions show that blanket growth, fluorination or fragmentation rules are not justified. No evidence identifies that chemistry as a mediated consequence of covariance geometry. End this exact exposed complete law under the registered rule. A future materially different law needs a sourced distinguishing hypothesis; transferable kernel-family benefit and independent plausible descendant coverage remain open.

nodes.hypothesis: Offer direct transfer of a ketone carbonyl oxygen to an adjacent methylene as an alternative within change_bond, preserving molecular formula, the carbon skeleton and ketone class while exposing a new carbonyl position to the inherited fresh-pool selector.
nodes.finding:
The oxygen-position mechanism happened. All 70 executed shifts retained the molecular formula, carbon skeleton and ketone class and produced a different, stable molecular identity. Forty-eight pool entries retained the exact immediate shifted graph, covering 39 distinct identities. Four reached evaluation as sole changes to accepted scored molecules: a DRD2 transfer improved its source by 0.003265, a median_2 transfer lost 0.003475, and two ring transfers tied. A fifth evaluated history included an additional atom replacement and lost 0.002890 against its generating parent. All five entered the survivor population; none improved the incumbent.

Every generated pool and batch was full, but deco_hop in seed 2 timed out after 240 of 300 evaluations, leaving 14 of 15 task sessions complete. The two complete seed macros average 0.553584 versus their matched parent's 0.553199, a paired gain of only 0.000385, with one seed lower and one higher. This is below the registered 0.002 target on the available complete seeds; the full three-seed effect cannot be evaluated. The parent completed the entire panel. The changed whole-search chemistry still contains reactive bonds, large repeated assemblies and unspecified stereochemistry.

A ketone can move within these observed ring and acyclic carbon frameworks without destroying its class or changing the molecule's composition. That establishes a usable positional neighborhood, while the direct score results show that utility depends on the particular position and molecular family. Exposure is narrow: only 140 of 7,723 bond-change calls had an eligible source, and only four of 4,290 scored proposals isolate the transfer itself. The available evidence therefore supports access to this neighborhood more strongly than a reliable optimization benefit.

The largest whole-search improvement, a 0.083867 gain in one sitagliptin run, occurred with no selected ketone transfer at all. Two eligible calls instead chose the original bond-order mode, changing subsequent random consumption. This rules out interpreting that gain as an observed benefit of the shifted oxygen; selected molecules and later search history changed together. The four direct comparisons are the evidence for local positional utility. Their unchanged composition also explains why they do not establish repair of the chemical liabilities identified by the molecular assessment. Broader useful exposure, consistent improvement and completion of the full score panel remain open.

nodes.hypothesis: Condition the retained connected-fragment crossover donor-cut distribution on reciprocal endpoint-context compatibility with the unchanged first-parent cut whenever compatible support exists, preserving the inherited donor behavior otherwise.
nodes.finding:
The conditional donor law worked exactly on 26,727 informative crossover attempts. On those same states, the inherited chance of a reciprocal context match averaged 9.55%; the applied law made it 100%. Independent reconstruction found no key, weighting, support, sampling or product-identity discrepancy. The resulting channel was usable: 354 compatible products that differed from both parents reached evaluation, including 257 pure crossovers. They produced 70 strict best-parent beats and 32 incumbent gains; 268 later served as parents. However, 22,117 of the 26,727 conditioned immediate products reproduced a parent. Of 850 evaluated conditioned descendants, 496 became novel only through finishing mutation. No informative nonidentical product reached evaluation in any of the three median-task runs.

Total crossover evaluations rose slightly from 1,492 to 1,549, but novel crossover pool entries fell from 29,730 to 22,962. Evaluations following genuinely nonidentical immediate crossover fell from 1,368 to 1,023, and pure crossovers fell from 961 to 725. All fifteen task runs completed, with every announced batch valid and unique. The complete matched endpoint mean fell from 0.595670 to 0.575399, a change of -0.020271 against the required +0.002. Seed changes were -0.061941, +0.019643 and -0.018514; ten of fifteen task-seed endpoints declined. Seed population SD fell from 0.026593 to 0.008463. Overall local parent beats nevertheless increased from 629 to 654, and incumbent gains from 258 to 277.

Constructing compatible donors avoided the earlier hard gate’s near-elimination of evaluated crossover, but retaining the route count did not retain its composition. Exact local correspondence often selected a fragment that rebuilt an existing parent; subsequent mutation then supplied novelty. This separates three claims that a matching percentage conceals: correct donor allocation, exposure to genuinely new recombination, and improvement of the complete search. The first is established, the second survives in a smaller channel with a clear task boundary, and the endpoint improvement prediction is contradicted. The experiment supports a negative mean contribution from this particular refinement under the tested composition; it does not overturn the separate evidence that crossover itself is useful.

Local correspondence also fails to certify chemistry. The output remains rich in aromatic, carbonyl and amine families, with conventional alternatives alongside reactive halogen bonds, doubtful ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry. In the fluorinated family, fewer nitrogen-halogen molecules accompany more oxygen-halogen molecules, so one reduced alert would hide a changed liability. Finishing mutations can also remove the matched attachment environment. The useful next distinction is whether donor choices preserve favorable complete molecular relationships while producing a distinct, chemically credible product. Neither excluding reproduced parents nor filtering unusual bonds has been tested here. Which change in ancestry, pool competition or later feedback caused the endpoint loss remains open; the scored cohorts do not provide labels for unchosen donors.
