nodes.hypothesis: Fit a task-local regularized linear score model on exact molecular count descriptors, then construct new bounded peripheral regions of scored molecules by maximizing that predictor in a mixed-integer graph program whose atom, bond, attachment, valence, connectivity and descriptor constraints jointly define the submitted molecular graph.
nodes.finding:
All five tasks completed on the screening seed. The optimizer supplied 145 full batches and 1,450 novel accepted molecules from feasible integer assignments, with zero discrepancies across their 384 count descriptors. All 150 ridge fits reconstructed from accepted task-local scores, and the 140 feedback refits with later opportunities changed subsequent construction objectives. Accepted constructions were selected again as sources 525 times. Of 1,450 proposals, 1,400 had positive predicted gains over their source; 578 of those predictions became actual gains. Overall, 598 proposals beat their source and 36 improved the running best, although mean child-minus-source score was negative on three of the five tasks. The final five-task Top-1 mean was 0.286518. Initial to final Top-1 changed from 0.305105 to 0.395373 for zaleplon_mpo, 0.548381 to 0.583606 for deco_hop, 0.019041 to 0.189601 for drd2_docking, 0.167839 to 0.175888 for median_2, and 0.002094 to 0.088123 for sitagliptin_mpo. This root has no Parent, and one screening seed does not establish comparative advantage.

The construction and adaptive feedback mechanisms happened. This result establishes that exact count realization and sufficient integer-construction throughput are attainable in this bounded peripheral-edit domain; the remaining predictive errors cannot be attributed to a mismatch between optimized descriptors and submitted graphs. The representational limit is visible in the accepted data: different molecules with identical full descriptor vectors received different scores on every task. In the docking trajectory, the two fluorine-position variants highlighted by the chemistry assessment share all 384 counts but score 0.124071 and 0.189601. No refit of this descriptor-only linear predictor can distinguish that pair. The chemistry assessment also finds familiar inherited rings carrying many reactive or unconventional appendages, alongside simpler high-scoring alternatives. Together, these observations make richer chemical-environment representation and constraints on functional-group compatibility worth testing while keeping exact realization as a control. They do not establish that either change will improve scores. Current evidence covers neutral, unspecified-stereochemistry peripheral trees and retained ring frameworks; new ring construction, broader chemistry and reliable advantage across replicas remain open.

The largest losses include failure to recover the Parent’s compact high-scoring decoration-hopping arrangement, while much larger decorated structures, reactive nitrogen/oxygen–halogen bonds, difficult ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry persist. Those associations suggest a gap in useful feasible alternatives, but neither the cleaner counterexample nor the liabilities identify the chemical cause of the loss. Partner identities, subsequent graph randomness and adaptive feedback remain inseparable parts of this measured total effect.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove only original sampled residual influence on successful pool allocation by choosing the maximum original count-GP posterior mean on each inherited available mask, resolving exact ties by the first pool index, while retaining full original covariance, Cholesky, normal-array consumption and correlated sampled arrays as passive computations with unchanged failure routing.

Every mean-only choice followed the original model mean, with no non-tied mean-loss decisions. The original sampled rule preferred a different identity at 3,958 of 4,350 actual mask positions. A separately masked replay changed all 435 batch orders and 434 selected sets; 2,731 actual accepted molecules were outside its sets. On these same Child pools, mean-only selection raised the average sum of ten predicted means from 3.16569 to 3.42482, lowered selected latent SD from 0.03059 to 0.01583, and raised count-Tanimoto redundancy from 0.58199 to 0.82801. Local parent wins rose from 648 to 668, but mean best-generating-parent score fell from 0.45530 to 0.37127 and mean offspring score from 0.37205 to 0.33081. Lack of later breeding is also insufficient as a general explanation: 657 of 659 nonterminal parent-winning Child sources were actually drawn, versus 636 of 639 in Parent. However, 390 drawn Child winners had no productive direct accepted descendant, versus 343 in Parent. Each panel's 150 final-batch offspring remain censored. This answers the current gated residual-presence criterion as one total adaptive removal contrast. It does not establish constituent additivity, sulfur interaction, the value of covariance dependence, independent validation, a complete optimizer foundation or transfer from older ungated Parents; those questions remain open.

nodes.hypothesis: Rank each selected transition's changed motifs first by absolute occurrence-count change divided by the larger of its before and after counts, then by the Parent's existing rank, so the unchanged bounded sign-balanced inverse installation prioritizes complete motif turnover over partial changes to recurring motifs.

The new ranking changed the retained key set at 104 of 435 installations and replaced 114 attributes. On those same recorded transitions, mean selected occurrence turnover rose from 0.931289 under the old ranking to 0.965876, without reducing it at any installation or changing the number of slots assigned to either sign. Partly changed motifs occupied 110 of 1,707 slots, down from 221 under the old ranking. Separate memory histories on the recorded candidate stream yielded 28 newly admitted evaluated molecules and four new vetoes. Three vetoes caused evaluated replacements; one occurred beyond the alternative batch cutoff. This establishes changes to 26 complete scored batches. The recorded stream resolves all ten alternative legacy members in three of those batches; the other 23 alternatives remain incomplete. Among the 31 affected evaluated molecules, seven improved their source, one tied and 23 worsened it; six became next states and three immediately improved the archive. The complete three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.519304, a paired change of -0.002456 against the required +0.002. One seed improved and two declined. This rules out absent exposure, mere reordering and failure to change evaluated allocation as explanations for the missed score target. More complete turnover demonstrably changes which local attributes receive memory and which fresh molecules are tested. It also changes admissibility in both directions, so it is not a general relaxation of tabu. The full stream produced slightly more source improvements and archive improvements than the Parent, but their average positive gains were smaller; those event counts did not translate into better final search. The largest loss is not explained by rejecting the best immediate neighbor at the first divergence: in the affected sitagliptin seed, both runs chose the same next molecule after replacing a losing proposal, and their later histories separated. Nine of eleven first batch divergences similarly preserved the next state. Later archive gains are therefore evidence of actual descendants, not isolated causal rewards for particular retained motifs or missing alternatives. Turnover measures how much of a motif multiset changed, without identifying a physical edit site. The molecular assessment still finds reactive heteroatom bonds and dense sulfur cages alongside more conventional aromatic families; the improved memory proxy has not established better chemical plausibility. The unresolved question is which local environments deserve exclusion for useful search, rather than whether fractional ranking can redirect it.

nodes.hypothesis: Reject a complete, RDKit-valid, canonically novel policy draw before emission when it contains a neutral divalent C-O-C linkage whose adjacent neutral tetrahedral carbon has a single bond to terminal neutral Cl, Br or I; continue the inherited bounded direct-policy refill with all learning and token sampling unchanged.

Mean recorded AUC remained 0.405593, and every recorded best-so-far trace was unchanged. This meets the registered 0.002 endpoint non-inferiority allowance on the complete panel. Both active batches filled without another sampling call. Overall raw generation stayed at 35,568 draws, including 32,647 valid strings; extra calls remained 23 across sixteen batches. Preserved scores have a limited but clear explanation. Both interventions were late, the removed parent examples had not improved their incumbents, and neither replacement nor any of the 48 identities appearing only in the child's affected sessions produced a new incumbent. The test establishes delivery of the specified chemistry without losing observed progress. It does not establish a reward gain or show that earlier, more frequent exclusions would be equally inexpensive. Iodine and haloalkyl-ester contexts had no observed opportunities.

The molecular assessment still describes ring-rich medicinal scaffolds with unresolved size, linker and reactive-form variation, and 843 generated appearances with unassigned perceived tetrahedral centres. Eliminating this attachment leaves those gaps open. The useful next question is whether precise form control can preserve incumbent progress when opportunities occur more often. Reduced raw motif prevalence, greater stability and practical synthesis remain separate claims requiring their own evidence.

Nevertheless, the common mismatch became much larger in the resulting histories: its mean squared contribution was 44.130, compared with 4.418 in the parent, accounting for 62.59% rather than 14.95% of trajectory-balance loss.

Raw valid novel yield fell from 7,991/12,000 draws (66.59%) to 6,861/12,280 (55.87%). The first adapted policy batches improved in validity, but later yield fell from 64.00% to 51.82%. Mean accepted policy-origin score fell from 0.204941 to 0.172874, and later emitted molecules matching previously trained graph scaffolds fell from 53 to 15. The three-seed mean final score fell from 0.550198 to 0.542654, a decrease of 0.007543; paired changes were -0.009239, -0.029845 and +0.016454. All fifteen task replicas completed their 300 evaluations.

The common policy-credit component was not merely an expendable normalization error in this setting. Removing it left the scalar objective unchanged at a given state, yet shifted much more unresolved error onto the normalizer and weakened later transfer of graph feedback into neural proposals. This happened while graph-origin replay share increased from 73.54% to 75.43%, so dilution of graph records is not the explanation. Greater emitted scaffold variety and the disappearance of duplicate raw draws also failed to compensate for lower valid yield and policy-origin scores.

The early-versus-late reversal narrows the problem to continuing accepted-score adaptation rather than a different prepared prior: the checkpoint identities and preparation were unchanged. Preserving the direct normalizer derivative was insufficient to preserve its trajectory, because the policy state and shared clipping changed. The improved sitagliptin endpoint must also be read alongside the molecular assessment, which found prominent peroxide-linked, stereochemically undefined structures; broader graph coverage does not establish better chemical quality. Mechanism execution is confirmed, while the registered search-advantage condition is unsupported. The remaining question is how to control common and relative learning jointly without discarding the useful molecular transfer observed in the parent.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace independent first-parent requests within each suggestion by uniformly permuted systematic blocks of length equal to the inherited fresh-pool target, preserving the exact inherited prospective categorical rank probabilities and positive support while leaving every second-parent request on the original quantile law.
nodes.finding:
The scheduler preserved the original prospective rank preference and balanced all 870 preallocated blocks. It consumed 75,411 of 139,200 records; the other 63,789 were unused. Each suggestion actually used every supported first parent, raising mean distinct first-parent coverage from 24.32 to 29.00. More accepted offspring beat their generating parents (720 versus 629), and more accepted records were later used for breeding (2,636 versus 2,401). Yet average offspring score fell from 0.385256 to 0.352623, and the average positive incumbent increment fell from 0.022510 to 0.018417. All fifteen task/seed runs completed on each side. Macro mean fell from 0.595670 to 0.553508, a paired change of -0.042161 against the required +0.002 gain. Every seed macro declined; eleven task/seed endpoints declined and four improved. The improved cells were zaleplon seeds 0 and 2 and median-2 seeds 1 and 2. Macro dispersion also decreased, from 0.026593 to 0.018224, without meeting the performance prediction.

Balanced prospective allocations transmitted into real accepted descendants and more complete breeder coverage. That exposure makes this a useful negative result: coverage and local parent-win counts are insufficient evidence of endpoint benefit for this fixed scheduler. The Child’s generating parents had lower absolute scores, so its extra local wins were measured against weaker references; more incumbent advances also came in smaller steps. The largest losses involved decoration hopping and sitagliptin, while median-2 and zaleplon task means improved. The chemistry assessment found substantial formal scaffold variety and useful aromatic, amine and carbonyl arrangements, alongside reactive bonds, strained closures and unspecified stereochemistry. Plausible alternative leading families remain limited even where graph counts are broad. Those descriptions do not establish which chemical feature caused the score loss. The fixed scheduling approach has a complete adverse result under this profile. The respective roles of changed parent sequences and their associated graph-RNG paths in producing those losses remain unresolved, as does contribution of the broader graph-evolution foundation.

nodes.hypothesis: Reject an otherwise valid canonically novel close_ring neighbor before tabu testing unless its source shortest path overlaps the existing ring graph in zero atoms, one atom, or exactly one existing ring edge, thereby redirecting new-cycle proposals away from extended or separated ring overlap while retaining the Parent's edit sampling and accepted-score walk.
nodes.finding:
The gate rejected 275 valid, fresh ring-closure attempts. Independent reconstruction of the current tabu table shows that 257 of these would otherwise have been admitted; each was replaced by a different neighbor from the same scored source before feedback. Emitted closures with extended or separated overlap fell from 241 to zero. Ring growth remained active through 40 permitted closures: six paths outside existing rings, three with a single old ring atom and 31 sharing one old ring edge. Nine permitted closures beat their source score and seven improved the best archive.

The overall molecules also lost much of the targeted complexity. Among 4,350 emitted neighbors, the number with a pair of RDKit-perceived rings sharing at least three atoms fell from 1,867 to 10, while mean ring-atom participation changed only from 62.89% to 61.70%. This preserved substantial ring content while removing most extensive ring overlap. All batches completed, requiring 12.83 attempts per ten submitted molecules versus 12.15 for the parent. The complete three-seed mean fell from 0.520918 to 0.517522, a paired change of -0.003396 that exceeds the allowed 0.002 loss. Seed changes were +0.004044, -0.024305 and +0.010073. DRD2 improved on average; the other four task means declined.

The experiment establishes that a narrow source-path rule can strongly control ring-junction growth without disabling all closures or disturbing identity, memory and feedback. Most evaluated rings remain, and the admitted closure repertoire still produces improvements. The score cost is nevertheless real on this panel: the parent had 37 source-improving and 19 selected closures in the now-excluded class. Those historical observations explain why score retention required a test, but they do not provide scores for the newly rejected structures or identify which missing transition caused a later loss.

The chemical assessment shows what the topology restriction leaves unresolved. Less elaborate ring cages still contain unusual sulfur coordination, reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds and unspecified configurations. The permitted classes do not establish accessible three-dimensional geometry or synthetic plausibility, and the rule neither removes complexity already present in a source nor constrains other edit types. The campaign now has evidence that extensive ring overlap can be suppressed selectively, alongside evidence that this degree of suppression did not retain the registered mean-score margin. Ring topology and local chemical bonding remain separate limitations.

nodes.hypothesis: Select oracle-bound offspring by maximizing independent joint posterior function draws from a task-local fingerprint Gaussian process over a fresh pool generated by the Parent's unchanged graph evolution operators.
nodes.finding:
The two additional runs reproduce posterior selection and feedback. All 2,900 selected offspring maximize their reconstructed correlated function draws, uncertainty changes 2,693 choices (92.86%) compared with choosing the highest posterior mean, and all 2,800 eligible predictions on the same molecules change after accepted feedback. All 290 fits use only earlier accepted observations. Mean final-best score across the five objectives is 0.558863 in the first additional run and 0.526723 in the second, compared with 0.547535 in the original run of this selector. Across all three seeds, mean score is 0.544374 with population standard deviation 0.013310. The intended offspring-efficiency improvement does not appear: only 371 of 2,900 new offspring beat their best generating parent (12.79%), and their mean child-minus-parent score is -0.100465. The original direct-submission Parent's single-seed references are 13.86% and -0.084154. Across all three selector runs, 565 of 4,350 offspring beat their best parent (12.99%). The original paired screening-score gain of 0.055880 remains a one-seed comparison because matched additional runs of the direct-submission Parent are unavailable.

The experiment now separates reliable selector execution from the hoped-for improvement in offspring yield. The new runs' posterior means contain useful predictive information on the selected molecules: pooled prediction MSE is 0.017182 versus 0.036613 for the same-fit archive mean, with average within-batch rank correlation 0.412. Yet this information and widespread uncertainty-driven choice do not produce a higher parent-beating fraction. The remaining question is how to turn predictive information into more productive evaluations relative to already strong parents. Prediction quality is also uneven: on sitagliptin_mpo it is worse than the archive-mean predictor in two of three seeds, and that objective has the largest final-score variation. The chemistry assessment shows ample aromatic amides, cyclic amines and carbonyl-containing rings, alongside reactive substitutions and destructive edits; access to recognizable molecular families is established, while reliable discrimination among useful, chemically credible alternatives remains open. The unused pool members have no scores, so these runs cannot identify which rejected alternatives would have been better. Matched Parent replicas and same-pool comparisons with mean-only and generation-order selection are needed to isolate score benefit, efficiency, and uncertainty's contribution.

nodes.hypothesis: At objective initialization, refine each identity-mismatched initial encoding by bounded gradient descent on frozen-decoder target-token margin loss, and replace its particle starting position and admit its real initial score only when unchanged deterministic decoding exactly recovers that initial canonical molecule.
nodes.finding:
Exact starting coverage increased from one to two of the ten supplied molecules. The same additional molecule was recovered in all five objective sessions after 168 latent updates: its mean target-margin loss fell from 0.168312 to 0.019830, and its checked position was installed in two particles per session. This doubled scored initial particle memories from two to four out of twenty. All ten recovered particle copies supplied actual motion sources; their memories produced 44 nonzero personal-attraction terms and 252 nonzero attractions from other particles. Eight other mismatched molecules reached the 256-step limit and retained their original positions, while the original exact match stayed unchanged. These five sessions reuse one fixed ten-molecule set and are not five independent reconstruction tests. The frozen model and exact score-position provenance remained intact. On the supplied seed, the mean final Top-1 score fell from 0.450789 to 0.347733. Zaleplon improved from 0.374833 to 0.390441 and median_2 from 0.167839 to 0.202143; deco_hop fell from 0.592706 to 0.553113, drd2_docking from 0.859171 to 0.412549, and sitagliptin from 0.259395 to 0.180421. Every task completed all 300 evaluations with no invalid or duplicate evaluator submissions.

At least one missing starting identity was already representable by the frozen decoder: correcting its coordinates recovered that identity without changing neural weights or transferring a score to a different molecule. The causal path from recovery to installation, motion and scored attraction is therefore established. That repairs a real coverage defect, but this run does not support the expectation that doubling the initially scored particles improves overall search quality. On drd2_docking and sitagliptin, both recovered personal memories were replaced after their first proposals, before they could supply a nonzero personal pull; their shared memory still influenced other particles. On deco_hop, the recovered shared attractor was referenced in 210 motions and both recovered personal memories survived to the end, yet the task score was lower. The amount of attractor reuse alone is therefore insufficient evidence of useful search guidance. All nine optimization attempts lowered their best visited mean loss, but only one recovered its molecule, so the token-margin proxy cannot replace the production identity check. The eight failures do not establish that those molecules lack an inverse: the bounded local optimizer may simply have failed to find one. Mean decoded fingerprint distance from the source remained large, increasing from 0.854 to 0.864. The molecular assessment likewise finds abundant rings alongside long unsaturated chains, labile polar linkers and irregular ring arrangements. Exact initialization does not control those downstream structural changes. Broader inversion coverage and the usefulness of moves around a recovered position remain separate open questions; this single seed establishes activation and an observed score loss, without establishing a reproducible score effect.

nodes.hypothesis: Reduce only CONFIG['posterior_selector']['pool_multiplier'] from 16 to 4, so the unchanged accepted-only count-Tanimoto GP correlated Thompson selector chooses the announced batch through its original sequentially masked joint-draw maxima over a complete fresh field of four admitted candidates per announced batch member (40 instead of 160 at batch ten), with every generator, admission, prediction, residual, survival and fallback law inherited.
nodes.finding:
All 435 smaller fields filled and the original correlated sampler operated correctly. Breeding attempts fell from 76,081 to 18,643, and mean task non-oracle time fell from 26.20 to 16.72 seconds. Selected standardized residual leverage fell from 1.998 to 1.506 in every matched task/seed cell, supporting the predicted reduction in extreme positive residual competition. Selected mean enrichment nevertheless fell from 1.054 to 0.885 pool standard deviations. There were 650 strict generating-parent wins versus 648, but actual offspring scores averaged 0.3469 versus 0.3720, and total sequential incumbent gain fell from 5.819 to 4.883, with 220 advances versus 255. The complete endpoint mean fell from 0.596453 to 0.534036, a paired change of -0.062417: thirteen of fifteen cells and all three seed means were lower. The +0.002 target fails despite lower seed dispersion. The Parent's rare late decoration-hopping breakthrough remains in the primary panel and contributes -0.015340 to the mean difference; the descriptive remaining fourteen-cell mean is still -0.050440. Total wall time rose because one decoration-hopping oracle run took much longer, so the demonstrated saving concerns non-oracle work.

Lower residual competition is real here, but it does not establish productive selection. The retained predictor gives exactly the same predictions as its passive original-model reference on the same real inputs; the lower selected-stream MSE on the Child is accompanied by worse pair ordering and batch rank correlation on a different accepted history. Generic core novelty rises, yet total incumbent progress and typed-core productivity fall. Future rank-band support is similar in aggregate, while fewer generation opportunities leave 355 eligible accepted records undrawn versus 50; this is measured exposure, not proof that reduced reuse caused the loss. The molecular assessment also finds useful compact aromatic amides and cyclic amines alongside reactive attachments, dense ring growth and unresolved stereochemistry. More ring-rich or novel structures do not guarantee preservation of favorable functional-group context, and the sulfur rule supplies no whole-molecule plausibility certificate. The complete loss and the still-negative sensitivity rule out a performance rescue by this fixed smaller-field recipe. They do not identify statistical or chemical mediation, an optimal width, a monotone width response, or a transferable benefit. The exposed recipe ends; whole-selector and whole-foundation contribution questions remain separate.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove only the active influence of frozen pretrained accepted-context predictive-location component m-000000000016 at successful fresh-pool allocation: use the original raw count-GP mean plus the EXACT inherited score_scale*(original_standard_normals@original_Cholesky_factor.T) residual, with inherited sequential masks and first-index ties; retain every original TabPFN-v2 projection, accepted-context fit, prediction, numerical check and failure route as passive computations in the exact Parent environment.
nodes.finding:
The control completed all 15 task/seed sessions. Mean final Top-1 rose from 0.544774 to 0.596453, a paired gain of 0.051679: all three seed means improved, 14 of 15 endpoints rose, and median_2 seed 1 fell by 0.014163. Seed dispersion increased from 0.016490 to 0.033970. The location change reached real feedback: all 435 fresh-pool sets changed, with 2777 strict same-mask winner disagreements and 2457 accepted identities absent from the passive external batch. Both predictors still refitted 435 times on complete accepted contexts; 14 external preprocessing overflow warnings remained visible, with finite outputs and no numerical fallbacks.

On the control's same 4350 accepted labels, GP pair-order accuracy was 0.709552 versus 0.663999 for the passive external mean, and mean batch Spearman was 0.525513 versus 0.422185. Both ordering measures improved in 14 sessions; zaleplon_mpo seed 2 was a counterexample. GP MSE was slightly worse, 0.011213 versus 0.011061, contradicting the lower-error prediction in 11 sessions. Accepted offspring scores increased from 0.298274 to 0.372050 and cumulative incumbent gain from 5.044230 to 5.819415, while local parent wins fell from 703 to 648 and sequential incumbent advances from 268 to 255. Stronger absolute progress therefore did not require more relative wins or uniformly better squared error.

This complete comparison closes the active-location contribution gap for the frozen pretrained recipe inside the retained count-GP residual selector: its active location harms this matched panel at the registered 0.002 descriptive scale. Full model work remains in the control, so the gain cannot be assigned to skipping neural computation or changing the environment. Ordering, calibration and search progress are distinct: improved same-label ordering accompanies stronger absolute accepted progress even though squared error is slightly worse and one session loses both ordering measures. Actual changed identities enter later fits and breeding, but those joins do not identify mediation, and unused passive alternatives have no labels or continued histories. The projection, weights, preprocessing and raw conversion still constitute one recipe; their individual effects and transfer remain open.

All current trajectories reproduce earlier original-GP trajectories exactly, so they add a compatible treatment-versus-control answer rather than independent replication. The earlier cross-lock endpoint comparison remains unpaired, and its original Anchor performance target is not achieved or retroactively repaired. The molecular assessment associates higher labels with useful compact aromatic/carbonyl and cyclic-amine contexts in several series, while reactive local bonds, strained ring arrangements and unspecified stereochemistry persist. Better scalar search scores therefore leave chemical plausibility and broader generator capability unresolved. This bounded control supplies its component answer without settling those wider gaps.
